_meta.header_sentence: 111 systems onboarded. Financial window FY2019 to FY2025. Latest filed year: FY2025 for 73 systems, FY2024 for 35, FY2023 for 3. Latest sub-annual: FY2026 Q1.

methodology_changes.title: A filed period shorter than twelve months is kept as filed, labeled as such, and no flow metric is computed on it
methodology_changes.body: A company that changes its fiscal year end files one short period to bridge the gap. Until now this cohort had never held one, and there was no rule for it: the two returns ending in the same calendar year would have collided on one spine key and the second would have silently overwritten the first, so one filed return would have vanished with nothing going red. That is why the company carrying it was deferred rather than guessed at. The rule now is that the short period is carried EXACTLY AS FILED, as its own row, labeled with its month count and its filed period end. NOTHING IS ANNUALIZED. No figure on that row is scaled to a twelve-month equivalent, which was already this project's rule for every other period and is restated here because this is the one place the temptation exists. The four flow metrics, which measure activity over a period, read "not a full year" followed by the month count rather than a ratio, because a ratio taken over seven months is a different measurement from one taken over twelve and printing them side by side would invite exactly the comparison it cannot support. The wording deliberately avoids "not comparable", which already means three other things on this platform. Equity as a share of assets DOES compute and is shown, because it is net assets over total assets, both end-of-year as-of figures, so the length of the period cannot distort it. The row is excluded from the company's own multi-year figures and from every cohort quartile, median and baseline, the same treatment a form-change year already gets, and that exclusion is structural rather than a filter: every one of those figures is computed from the annual rows, and this row is not one of them. No existing company's figures move, because no other company in the cohort has filed such a period.

methodology_changes.title: Cohort positions are stated in position words rather than quartile ordinals, because the ordinal claimed a direction
methodology_changes.body: A cohort position used to read "3rd quartile" and now reads "upper middle". No figure moved: the cuts, the counts and every company's placement are identical, and only the words changed. The ordinal was the problem. In this project's code "1st" is the LOWEST quarter, which is the statistical convention, while a reader meeting "1st" in a financial report reads it as best. Both readings are ordinary English, so the ambiguity was invisible, and it handed the reader a direction on a block that exists precisely to avoid claiming one. The four words are lowest quarter, lower middle, upper middle and highest quarter, each still followed by the cut it was taken against and the n. A position word says where a value sits and nothing about whether sitting there is good. The same correction was applied to the cohort sentence on each metric chart, which computes its position separately in the browser, so the page now speaks one vocabulary rather than two. A code comment asserting that every anchor is higher-is-better was removed at the same time: it contradicted the research report, which says plainly that this project does not say which end of any metric is the good end.

methodology_changes.title: Each anchor metric now shows where this system sits among the cohort, as a quartile and never as a score
methodology_changes.body: Every mutual tearsheet now carries a cohort position: for each of the five anchor metrics, which quartile of this project's filers the system falls in, with the n and the quartile boundaries stated on the line. It is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. The quartiles are never added up, weighted or reduced to a single figure, because a composite reads as a verdict and this project reports figures as filed. Three of the five place against a different figure than the chart band uses, and the figure is named on each line: the operating ratio uses the median of the company's own window rather than its latest year, reinvestment uses the cumulative window figure rather than the per-year ratio, and rate discipline uses the growth differential rather than the revenue index. A metric a system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place at tier A or B, is named as left out with what it would need, and is never counted as a zero: 27 systems are placed on all five, 15 on four, 23 on three and one on two. The growth differential is now derived once in the data layer and read from there by everything else, rather than computed separately in the cohort baselines.

methodology_changes.title: The representative bill is computed in the unit and the billing period the company filed, which corrects a published figure for seven companies
methodology_changes.body: This corrects figures that were published on this dashboard and were wrong. The three usage levels are defined in hundred cubic feet (HCF), while each company's filed tier thresholds are in the unit that company files in. Twenty of the twenty-seven companies with a filed rate schedule file in HCF, where the two are the same thing and the bill was right. Seven file in Gallons or Thousand Gallons, and for those the usage was never converted: a customer using 10 HCF, which is 7,480 gallons, was billed for 10 gallons. The label had been converted while the number had not, so the page read "At 10 Thousand Gallons per month" beside a figure computed on ten of them. Two companies published a monthly water bill of 15 cents and one published $132,172.85. The usage is now converted into the filed unit before the filed tiers are applied, at 1 HCF = 748 gallons and 1 thousand gallons = 1,000 gallons, and the bill states both numbers. The bill is also stated as a monthly equivalent in every filed billing period, not only the bimonthly one: a bimonthly structure is computed at twice the monthly usage and divided by two, a quarterly structure at three times and divided by three, each with its factor stated on screen. The twenty companies filing in HCF are unchanged to the cent, because their conversion factor is one. No figure as filed moved: the filings were read correctly and only this derived illustration was wrong. A unit or a billing period that is not recognized is no longer read as HCF or as monthly; no bill is computed from it and the block says so.

methodology_changes.title: A mutual that sells water to other systems is classed wholesale and leaves the per-connection statistics
methodology_changes.body: A connection count only means a household where the system sells to households. One company in this cohort sells water to other water providers and to cities, on its own website's words, and files 21 service connections against revenue in the tens of millions. It is now classed a wholesale mutual in the registry, cited to that page, and a wholesale mutual sits outside every size band and every per-connection statistic: it is neither banded itself nor pooled into any other company's band. It keeps its place in the whole cohort, because the operating ratio, days cash and equity share are ratios rather than per-connection figures. The class follows the company's own stated words and never the shape of its numbers: four other candidates were checked against the same rule and not reclassified, because their own filings say only that they supply water to their members.

methodology_changes.title: Each anchor chart carries the cohort's own quartiles beside the external reference
methodology_changes.body: The operating ratio, days cash and equity charts now shade the 25th to 75th percentile of the company's peer cut, with the median through it, and name the cut and how many peers it holds. The peer cut is the company's size band by service connections where a count is held, and the whole mutual cohort otherwise. Only tier A and B values are pooled, the same rule that decides what may be ranked, and a cut holding fewer than five values carries no band. The cohort band is labelled as this project's own filers and the external reference keeps its own label, because they are different kinds of claim. The reinvestment and rate discipline charts carry no band and say why: the reinvestment chart plots each year while the cohort figure is cumulative, and the rate discipline chart plots an index with no cohort measure on its axis.

methodology_changes.title: Days cash on hand now counts marketable securities
methodology_changes.body: The headline now counts cash (Form 990 Part X lines 1 and 2), publicly traded securities (line 11), and other securities (line 12) where the company's own Schedule D Part VII describes them as marketable. Restricted holdings, stock or equity interests, ambiguous and undescribed holdings are left out and listed beside the figure with their dollar amounts. The cash-only figure is shown next to the headline. Form 990-EZ filers remain not reported, because the short form has no depreciation line.

methodology_changes.title: Operating ratio uses one direction everywhere
methodology_changes.body: Every operating ratio is revenue over expenses, where 1.0x or above means revenue covers expenses. The investor-owned utility card, which showed expenses over revenue as a percent, now uses the same direction, and the duplicate card on Community Mutual Water Company is removed.

methodology_changes.title: The header states the financial window and each company's latest filed year
methodology_changes.body: The header no longer says data runs through the newest year in the cohort. It states the window and how many companies have filed through each year, and every company page states its own latest filed year.

methodology_changes.title: Negative equity is explained in plain words
methodology_changes.body: Where net assets are below zero, the equity share carries a note saying that liabilities exceed assets, and names the years.

methodology_changes.title: Unverified claims are labeled, and two litigation claims are now sourced
methodology_changes.body: Two Eaton Fire litigation claims are now events with sources. Claims no source confirms stay listed so the gap is visible, each labeled as unverified and not presented as fact.

methodology_changes.title: Reinvestment ratio is now a cumulative figure over the window
methodology_changes.body: The headline is the total change in gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10a) over the total depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the comparable years in the window, with the latest year shown beneath it. It replaces an average of yearly ratios, which let one reversal or one lumpy year dominate. A net decrease stays in with its sign; a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant reads no material change; no ratio is drawn across a move from Form 990-EZ to Form 990. Flags mark depreciation unchanged for three years, an implied depreciation rate outside 1 to 6 percent, a reversal, and gross plant unchanged for three years. Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.

methodology_changes.title: Revenue per connection divides each year by that year's own count
methodology_changes.body: Each fiscal year is divided by the State Water Board eAR active service connection count from the reporting year closest to its fiscal year end, within 366 days. A company keeps one source for every year; an SDWIS or member count is used only when no year pairs with an eAR count. Every figure names its count, reporting year and any gap from the fiscal year end. It replaces one undated SDWIS snapshot applied to every year. The indexed trend is built on total revenue and total expense and did not change.

methodology_changes.title: Every reported value carries a comparability tier
methodology_changes.body: Tier A, B or C states whether a value is comparable enough to rank, with the rule that set it and what would change it. Ranks and the similarity report use tiers A and B only; a tier C value is shown and listed as not ranked. This is separate from the high, medium and low confidence tag, which is unchanged.

methodology_changes.title: Days cash reads a blank line as zero only when the filer's total foots without it
methodology_changes.body: Where Form 990 Part X line 1, 2, 11 or 12 is blank and total assets (line 16) equal the other asset lines to the dollar, the blank line is read as zero; where Part IX line 22 (depreciation) is blank and total expenses (line 25) equal lines 1 through 24 to the dollar, depreciation is read as zero. Each year this applies is labeled on the card. Where the total does not foot, or the filing is a Form 990-EZ, nothing is read and the figure stays not reported.

explainer.title: How a California water system fails
explainer.standfirst: The registry shows each system's standing with the State Water Board: Not At-Risk, Potentially At-Risk, At-Risk or Failing. Those are not just labels. Each one sits on a ladder the state built, and the rungs above it carry powers the state can actually use, up to and including taking a company's water system away from it. This page explains what those powers are, in the order they arrive, and what the two documented endings have looked like in practice.

sections.title: The ladder, and what each rung means
body: The State Water Board assesses every community water system in California and publishes where each one stands. The four rungs run in one direction and each one means something specific.

**Not At-Risk** means the assessment found no significant risk. **Potentially At-Risk** means some indicators are flagged but not enough to place the system on the At-Risk list. **At-Risk** means the state has identified the system as likely to fail without intervention. **Failing** means the system is not currently delivering water that meets drinking-water standards, or cannot reliably do so.

A system can also be placed At-Risk **automatically**, regardless of its scores, for a specific condition such as relying on bottled or hauled water. That is worth knowing before reading the label: an automatic designation says something about how the system is currently getting water to people, not necessarily about its finances.
The rung matters because it decides which of the powers below the state may reach for. Failing systems are the primary target of mandatory consolidation; since 2023 at-risk systems are reachable too.

sections.title: Mandatory consolidation: the state can order a merger
body: **Consolidation** means joining one water system to another, so that the larger or healthier system takes over supplying the customers. It can be physical, connecting the pipes, or managerial, where one system runs another.

Since 2015 the State Water Board has been able to **order** it rather than ask. SB 88 (2015) added Health and Safety Code sections 116680 to 116684, which let the board require a failing system to consolidate with a nearby one, and require the receiving system to accept it. The board must first give the systems a chance to consolidate voluntarily.

SB 403 (2023) extended that authority beyond failing systems to systems the board has designated **at-risk**. That is the change that makes the registry's standing column consequential rather than merely descriptive: an at-risk designation now sits inside the reach of an order.

An order is not instant. The statutory process involves notice, consultation, technical and financial analysis of the receiving system, and funding arrangements, and it has in practice taken years rather than months.

sections.title: An administrator: someone else runs the company
body: Short of a merger, the State Water Board can petition to have an **administrator** appointed over a system. An administrator is a person or firm given authority to operate the system and make decisions the existing board or owner would otherwise make.
The company continues to exist. Its customers keep receiving water. What changes is who is in charge of running it and spending its money.

sections.title: Receivership: a court takes control
body: A **receiver** is someone a court appoints to take possession of property or a business and run it under the court's supervision. California Code of Civil Procedure section 564 is the general statute that lets a court do this, and it is the route used for water systems where the operator can no longer run the system safely.

The petition is typically brought by the Attorney General on the State Water Board's behalf. Once a receiver is appointed, the owner no longer controls the system: the receiver does, and reports to the judge.
Receivership is not by itself a resolution. It stabilises the system and buys time. What it does not do is produce a buyer, and a system can remain in receivership for years while one is sought.

sections.title: What it looked like: Sativa
body: The Sativa Los Angeles County Water District served roughly 1,600 connections in Compton and Willowbrook. After sustained complaints about discolored water and findings of mismanagement, the Los Angeles County Local Agency Formation Commission, the body that decides the boundaries and existence of local agencies, voted to **dissolve** the district in 2019 and named the County as its successor agency.

The County ran the system, then brought in an operator: Suburban Water Systems, a private utility regulated by the California Public Utilities Commission, operated it under County oversight. In January 2023 the County announced it had transferred the system to Suburban permanently.

The shape of this ending: the original entity no longer exists, the customers kept their water, and a larger regulated utility absorbed the system. It took roughly four years from dissolution to handover.

sections.title: What it looked like: Big Basin
body: Big Basin Water Company served about 500 connections in Boulder Creek, Santa Cruz County. After years of drinking-water violations and enforcement, the Attorney General petitioned the Santa Cruz County Superior Court on the State Water Board's behalf for the appointment of a receiver. The case is **23CV01615**.
The court granted the petition in 2023 and appointed a receiver to take over the water system, and the company's wastewater operations with it.

The shape of this ending, so far, is that there is no ending. The system remains in receivership. No buyer has taken it on. That is the honest contrast with Sativa: the same machinery, applied to a smaller and more remote system, has not yet produced anyone willing to absorb it.

sections.title: Watch items: what the Legislature is doing now
body: Two bills in the 2025 to 2026 session would change parts of this machinery. Neither is law. Both are shown with the last action their official record carries, and nothing here predicts what will happen to either.

bills.title: Mutual water companies: assessments and water charges: notice.
bills.status_as_filed: Assembly amendments concurred in. (Ayes 29. Noes 7.) Ordered to engrossing and enrolling.
bills.plain: This one is about how a mutual water company must notify its shareholders before levying assessments and water charges, which is exactly the mechanism the fire-hit Altadena companies have been using. It cleared both houses on 25 August 2026 and was ordered to engrossing and enrolling. Its record does NOT yet show it presented to the Governor, so it is not accurate to describe it as awaiting signature; it is at the step before that.

bills.title: An act to amend Section 116680 of the Health and Safety Code, relating to drinking water.
bills.status_as_filed: May 14 hearing: Held in committee and under submission.
bills.plain: This one would amend Health and Safety Code section 116680 itself, the definitions section of the mandatory consolidation statute described above. It was held in the Senate Appropriations Committee under submission on 14 May 2026, which means it did not advance and is not moving unless the committee takes it up again.

sections.title: How to read a check that found nothing
body: This dashboard reports what it checked as carefully as it reports what it found. Every source it consults keeps a check log with one row per company, and that row carries one of four states. The difference between them is the difference between a finished answer and outstanding work, and collapsing them would let a gap read as a clean bill.

**checked_and_clean.** The check ran and came back with a finished answer, whether that answer found records or found none. This is a statement about the CHECK, not a clean bill of health for the water system. A system with 11 open violations is checked_and_clean here and shows its violations in the anomalies table below.
**not_matched.** The check ran and nothing could be attributed to this company: no key to join on, or a key that returned no record. A finished state, not a task.
**source_gap.** The source itself could not be read or reached. The company is answerable; the source did not answer. This is outstanding work.

**not_yet_checked.** The check has not run for this company, INCLUDING the case where the dialect holds no row for it at all. This is outstanding work, and a missing row counts here rather than vanishing from the tally.

The distinction that costs the most to keep is between **not_matched** and **not_yet_checked**. Not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed. Not-yet-checked means nothing was searched. They look identical on a page that only reports what it found, and they are not the same fact.

The California Secretary of State is where that distinction currently bites. The corporate register is reachable only through a real browser session with an operator present, and that route now answers a persistent hCaptcha interstitial, which this project will not attempt to solve. So the companies whose registration has not been read are recorded as not-yet-checked and deliberately not as not-matched: nothing was searched for them. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence there could never be a finished answer in any case. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

Each company's governance block shows that state and the date it was recorded, and links here rather than repeating this explanation. The reason recorded for that individual company is kept in full in the data layer behind the page.

explainer.footer: This page describes the law and two documented case histories. It is not legal advice, it is not a prediction about any company, and no company in this registry is named on it. Sativa and Big Basin are context and are deliberately not part of the registry. Every source linked here was requested and answered on 27 August 2026.

company_index.title: Company Index
company_index.scope_note: This indexes the California mutual water companies Hydronomics has screened so far. It is not every California mutual. The screened set is drawn from the IRS Business Master File, which is authoritative but not a complete census: some mutual water companies file under other subsections of section 501(c) and some are absent from the file altogether, both confirmed against companies already onboarded here. The roster covers organizations the IRS lists under section 501(c)(12); a small number of California mutual water companies file under other subsections and are not yet included, among them Community Mutual Water Company, already onboarded here as cawc_0013, which files under subsection 05. Treat this as a coverage map and not a count of the universe.
company_index.availability_note: Yes means Hydronomics holds the data today, not that it could be obtained. No means the data is not held, and every no carries its reason. For a candidate, which is a company identified but not yet onboarded, unknown means nothing has been pulled or checked; a candidate reads no only where the filing type settles it, as a Form 990-N postcard filer has no financial detail in existence to hold. Nothing on this page is estimated: where a fact is not recorded it reads not recorded. SDWIS violation history carries a fourth state, checked and none found, because a system nobody checked and a system checked and found clean are different facts and this column used to show them the same way. On that column yes means a violation record was actually retrieved from the US EPA Envirofacts federal mirror and is held here; checked and none found means the mirror was queried on the stated date and returned nothing, a finished state; no means there is no PWSID, so there was no key to query with and nothing was checked; and unknown means the check could not be trusted or has not been run. Every one of those but yes carries its reason on the cell.
company_index.candidates_note: 624 screened candidates are carried from data/company_index_candidates.json, marked candidate, not yet onboarded. No data has been pulled for any of them, so their availability cells read unknown, except where the filing type settles it: the 202 Form 990-N postcard filers have no financial detail in existence and read no. A candidate is a company we have identified and screened, not a company whose figures we hold.
company_index.age_note: Age is the year recorded in the company's own context page, carried with the qualifier as written. An IRS recognition year is a tax-recognition date and implies formation in or before that year; it is not a founding date and is never presented as one.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)
Form 990 Part IX line 25 (total functional expenses)
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation), subtracted for the excluding variant
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Both variants are shown and the displayed variant is labeled (5A).
metrics.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

metrics.name: Days cash on hand
metrics.subtitle: days of operating cost covered by cash and marketable securities

blank_lines_read_as_zero.label: blank on filing; read as zero because total assets foot without it
blank on filing; read as zero because total assets foot without it

metrics.limitation_note: Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

metrics.reference_source: Rating-agency convention: 200 plus days is strong, under roughly 90 days reads as stress, on unrestricted cash and investments (the State Water Board's SAFER risk indicator uses the same basis: Draft Final White Paper, Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, p. 28). Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.
metrics.formula: (cash, line 1; savings and temporary cash investments, line 2; publicly traded securities, line 11; other securities described as marketable on Schedule D Part VII, line 12) x 365 / (total expenses, line 25, less depreciation, line 22)
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 1 (cash, non-interest-bearing)
Form 990 Part X line 2 (savings and temporary cash investments)
Form 990 Part X line 11 (investments, publicly traded securities)
Form 990 Part X line 12 (investments, other securities), counted only where Schedule D Part VII describes the holding as marketable
Form 990 Part IX line 25 less line 22 (operating expense excluding depreciation)
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Lines 1, 2 and 11 are counted as filed; line 12 only where the filer's own Schedule D Part VII description reads as marketable. Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

metrics.name: Reinvestment ratio
metrics.subtitle: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: cumulative over 4 comparable years (FY2021-24), excludes 1 not-reported year

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment at cost), year over year
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation)
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 6 documented, 1 partial, 1 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: The service-area boundary is State-verified in SABL (independent, not self-declared) and every one of the 1,469 connections is metered and counted, so the record documents both a defined resource and a defined membership. The shareholder roll and the share-to-land mapping are not in the record, so the documentation is strong but not complete.
principles.finding: Members are shareholders of the mutual, and the service area is a State-verified SABL boundary with 1,469 metered connections.
principles.signal: State-verified SABL service-area boundary; eAR total connections 1,469.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: A published five-tier increasing-block rate priced per hundred cubic feet, plus meter charges that scale with meter size, documents that each member's cost is tied to use. No cost-of-service study or rate-setting record is in the file, so the calibration of the tiers to actual cost is not documented.
principles.finding: Five-tier increasing-block water rates and meter charges that scale with meter size tie cost to how much a member uses.
principles.signal: eAR rate structure: Variable Base residential, five tiers, priced per Hundred Cubic Feet.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: Shareholders elect the board, so the formal mechanism is documented, but the record carries no turnout, no contested seats, and no member votes on capital. The mechanism is on record; evidence that it is actively exercised is not, so the documentation is partial. The specific board is now on the record: the Statement of Information filed 3/24/2026 names 5 directors and 2 officers, transcribed as filed. That closes one of the gaps named above. It does NOT close the others: a filed roster shows who governs, not how members choose them, and carries no election, turnout or member vote. The evidence status therefore stays PARTIAL, because what this principle asks about is member participation and that remains undocumented.
principles.finding: Shareholders elect the board by the mutual's structure, but participation records (turnout, contested seats, votes on capital) are not reported.
principles.signal: Mutual shareholder governance; participation records not reported.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Every connection is metered and the State risk assessment independently rates the system Not At-Risk with zero violations across all six categories, so operational monitoring is documented and externally checked. The financial-side monitor is thinner: the 990 confirms audited financials but does not name the auditor and no audit report is published.
principles.finding: Every connection is metered and the State risk assessment shows the system Not At-Risk with zero violations.
principles.signal: eAR metered connections; SAFER Not At-Risk, 0 of 6 violation categories.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: A published rate schedule documents a 10 percent late penalty, reconnection charges, and a written service-resumption process, so consequences are defined and public. The record documents a single flat penalty step rather than escalation that rises with repeated or severe violations.
principles.finding: The rate schedule sets a 10 percent late penalty, reconnection charges, and a written service-resumption process.
principles.signal: Published rate schedule: delinquency penalty, reconnection and service-resumption charges.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No conflict-resolution policy or forum beyond ordinary board meetings appears in the record. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found; it is an evidence gap to close, not a finding that the company lacks a dispute process or governs badly.
principles.finding: No conflict-resolution policy or forum beyond ordinary board meetings is separately documented in the record.
principles.signal: Not reported.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: The right is documented by two independent authorities: the State Water Board lists the system as a privately owned mutual water company and the IRS recognizes it as a 501(c)(12). The record documents the legal standing every lawful mutual holds; it does not document that right being actively exercised to change rules or governance. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0114477, first registered 06/06/1925, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 3/24/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: Recognized by the State Water Board as a privately owned mutual water company and by the IRS as a 501(c)(12).
principles.signal: eAR ownership 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company'; IRS 501(c)(12).

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents genuine nesting in a regional supply network: wholesale State Water purchased through CCWA, a Goleta emergency intertie, and active CalWARN membership. The system's governance role in those bodies (a CCWA board seat or vote) is not documented, so nesting is documented on the supply side but not the decision side.
principles.finding: Buys wholesale State Water through CCWA and holds a Goleta emergency intertie, nesting the mutual inside a regional supply network, and is a CalWARN member.
principles.signal: eAR sources: CCWA treated surface water, Goleta WD emergency intertie; CalWARN active.

kv.v: Bimonthly biller: the bill is computed on 20 HCF per bimonthly bill (2 times the monthly usage) against the filed per-bill tiers, then divided by 2 to state it per month.

The usage is converted into the company's own filed unit before the filed tiers are applied, and the bill is stated as a monthly equivalent: a bimonthly structure is computed at twice the monthly usage and divided by two, and any other billing period the same way with its factor stated. member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 24 survey years, 2000 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 22 of the 24 years, across 5 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 22 of the 24 years, across 8 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 79 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 55 were left blank. 8 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2000 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

basins.name: GOLETA
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.

basins.name: FOOTHILL
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) CASGEM/WDL/GWIDS: Long term hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 3-053_7a_Hydrographs_Foothill.pdf

2) Water levels have consistently declined since mid-2000 and the 2014 measurement is within a foot or two of the lowest of record.
Source: 3-053_7a_StatusReportonGroundwaterBasins_Final2-2016.pdf  pg 13
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.
sgma_basin.source: CA DWR Bulletin 118 groundwater basins and SGMA Basin Prioritization, https://gis.water.ca.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Geoscientific/i08_B118_CA_GroundwaterBasins/MapServer/0/query Retrieved 2026-08-18.

sdwis_compliance.plain_lead: Two federal EPA tables disagree about this system. One lists no violations; the other points to 2 violation records it does not actually contain. Because the sources contradict each other, this system cannot be confirmed clean and cannot be confirmed as having violated. The conflict is preserved below rather than resolved.
sdwis_compliance.reason: Checked on 2026-08-31: the federal VIOLATION table returned no rows for PWSID CA4210024, but VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC references 2 violation id(s) for the same system. EPA's own tables disagree, so this system cannot be reported as clean. The disagreement is recorded and not reconciled; no violation record was invented for the referenced ids, because none was returned.

tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA4210024. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.
Returned 4 link row(s) for PWSID CA4210024, naming 2 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 806002, 9306001.

gap_evidence.status_line: 2 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 806002, 9306001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.
gap_evidence.source: US EPA Envirofacts SDWIS, https://data.epa.gov/efservice, tables VIOLATION and VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC, queried with the BEGINNING operator on the full PWSID. Retrieved 2026-09-23.

plant_per_acre.logic: Infrastructure built per acre of service area. how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $6,612,490 (990 program-service revenue) minus $6,481,020 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $131,470. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: For La Cumbre this residual is NOT cleanly assessment revenue: the eAR captured only RESIDENTIAL water rates (no B1.2 non-residential figure was filed), so the residual also sweeps in the system's non-residential water sales and other fees, not just any member assessment.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)

entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company serving Hope Ranch and the Hope Ranch Annex, an unincorporated luxury residential enclave west of Santa Barbara. Ownership attaches to the land, proportional to acreage; every landowner is a shareholder. [1] One of the wealthiest service areas of any California mutual.

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Water sales and assessments to shareholder-customers. Largest single customer is the La Cumbre Country Club, whose irrigation moved to recycled water in 2022 under a 25-year agreement with the City of Santa Barbara. [3] Near buildout at roughly 1,500-connection capacity, so the model is stewardship of a fixed, affluent base rather than growth. [1] Rate schedule published by the company; comparative affordability not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Diversified four ways: local groundwater wells (original source), Lake Cachuma water wholesale through Goleta Water District since the 1960s, State Water Project water since 1997 via the Central Coast Water Authority, and recycled water for the largest irrigation customer since 2022. [1][3][4] Supply read: diversified and buffered, one of the strongest supply positions a small mutual can hold.

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Distribution system dating to the 1920s buildout of Hope Ranch, extended as connections grew from under 100 to over 1,400. [1] Specific asset inventory and construction dates: not reported in public sources. Accounting read: reinvestment has run at 3 to 4 times depreciation over the window, the signature of a system actively renewing itself rather than aging in place. [D]

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Formed 1925 by Harold Chase and associates, the developers of Hope Ranch, alongside the Hope Ranch Park Homes Association, to water the lots they were selling. [1] Service area essentially unchanged for a century. Predates Goleta Water District (1944).

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Five-member shareholder-elected board; general manager Mike Alvarado in recent public statements. [2][3] Style read: professionally managed with a long-tenured GM, communicates through local press and its website, demonstrated proactive supply strategy (the recycled water deal was negotiated ahead of need, mid-drought). Rate posture: not reported in detail; the revenue-per-connection trend on the dashboard shows regular upward adjustment. [D]

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: Wright v. Goleta Water District (Cal. Ct. App. 1985): cross-defendant in the Goleta Central groundwater basin adjudication; the 1970s Goleta connection moratorium did not apply to La Cumbre, which kept connecting new customers through the freeze. [5] 2021: board adopted a voluntary 20 percent use reduction during the statewide drought. [2] 2022: 25-year recycled water agreement. [3]

compliance.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: Four-source supply including a rainfall-independent recycled stream, rare at this size [1][3]. Financial profile at the top of every dossier benchmark: 1.40x operating ratio, 559 days cash, 96 percent equity [D]. Reinvestment at 3 to 4 times depreciation, the anti-aging signature [D]. Affluent, stable, near-buildout customer base with demonstrated drought cooperation [1][2].

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Santa Barbara front-country wildfire exposure; the dossier WUI standard says judge reserves against tail risk, not just routine risk. Growth is finished: revenue upside is rates only, so cost inflation lands directly on members. Heavy outdoor irrigation demand makes revenue drought-sensitive despite supply diversity [2]. Wholesale dependencies (Goleta, CCWA) put two of four sources outside company control [1][4].

exposure.text: Most revenue is volumetric water sales to a small, affluent residential service area, so usage swings with dry weather and conservation. As a member owned mutual it can adjust assessments and water rates to recover costs, which softens the swing. No formal decoupling mechanism is recorded in the Form 990.
exposure._source: Form 990 program service revenue (Part VIII); mutual rate-setting authority

narrative.supply_profile: La Cumbre buys wholesale State Water Project water treated through the Central Coast Water Authority and holds a Goleta emergency intertie, so its supply and its water cost track the imported-water system, not just local rain.
narrative.cost_link: Dry years hit La Cumbre from both sides: lower SWP allocation raises its supply cost while conservation lowers its volumetric revenue. As a member-owned mutual it can raise rates and assessments to recover, which softens but does not remove the swing.

dimensions.label: Water-year type
dimensions.read: A dry Sacramento Valley water-year type means the State Water Project it depends on delivers less, so La Cumbre leans harder on stored and purchased water; a wet type eases that.

dimensions.label: Drought stage
dimensions.read: Local Santa Barbara County drought stage drives customer conservation, which cuts the volumetric water sales that are most of its revenue, so a deep local drought squeezes the top line even when supply holds.

dimensions.label: Precipitation
dimensions.read: Statewide 8-Station precipitation matters to La Cumbre mainly through the State Water Project it imports, not through local runoff; low precipitation years are the ones where its purchased-water cost rises.

dimensions.label: Snowpack
dimensions.read: Sierra April-1 snowpack sets how much State Water Project supply exists to allocate, so a thin snowpack year is a higher-cost supply year for an SWP importer like La Cumbre.

dimensions.label: State Water Project allocation
dimensions.read: The State Water Project allocation percent is the single most direct weather link for La Cumbre: a low allocation (as in the 2021 to 2022 drought) forces it to replace imported water with costlier alternatives or draw reserves.

weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA4210004. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.

gap_evidence.status_line: 13 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 1106003, 8500113, 8500302, 8500303, 8600097, 8600098, 8600596, 8600597, 8600844, 8600845, 8600846, 9306001, 9806002. gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

exposure.text: Revenue is a mix of fixed meter service charges and volumetric water sales, so part of the base is steady while the volumetric part moves with demand in dry years. The District has used drought rate surcharges and holds reserves, which buffers but does not eliminate the exposure.
exposure._source: Goleta ACFR operating revenue composition; District rate structure

narrative.supply_profile: Goleta Water District blends Lake Cachuma surface water, State Water Project imports, and groundwater, so its supply and cost track both local Santa Barbara County reservoirs and the statewide project.
narrative.cost_link: Dry years raise Goleta's supply cost (less Cachuma and SWP, more groundwater) and lower volumetric sales; fixed meter charges and reserves buffer part of the revenue swing.

dimensions.label: Water-year type
dimensions.read: A dry water-year type reduces both local Cachuma inflow and State Water Project deliveries, tightening two of Goleta's three sources at once.

dimensions.label: Drought stage
dimensions.read: Local drought stage drives conservation and drought surcharges; Goleta has used drought rate surcharges to recover cost when volumetric sales fall.

dimensions.label: Precipitation
dimensions.read: Local precipitation fills Lake Cachuma, a core Goleta supply, so a dry precipitation year lowers its cheapest local water and raises reliance on imports and groundwater.

dimensions.label: Snowpack
dimensions.read: Sierra snowpack matters to Goleta through its State Water Project share, one of three sources, so a thin snowpack year raises its imported-water cost.

dimensions.label: State Water Project allocation
dimensions.read: A low State Water Project allocation reduces Goleta's imported supply, pushing it toward Cachuma and groundwater and raising cost in dry years.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4210004&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

exposure.text: As a CPUC-regulated utility, California Water Service has used revenue decoupling (a water revenue adjustment mechanism) that trues up authorized revenue regardless of how much water customers actually use. That largely separates revenue from weather driven volume. The mechanism's exact form has shifted with CPUC decisions over time.
exposure._source: California Water Service 10-K, MD&A discussion of decoupling / revenue adjustment mechanisms

narrative.supply_profile: California Water Service is a statewide regulated utility spanning many districts and sources, and it recovers authorized revenue through a CPUC decoupling mechanism, so weather-driven volume is largely separated from revenue.
narrative.cost_link: Weather flows to Cal Water mainly as cost, not revenue: dry years raise supply and pumping expense while decoupling keeps authorized revenue on track.

dimensions.label: Water-year type
dimensions.read: Dry water-year types raise its supply and pumping costs across districts, but decoupling trues up authorized revenue regardless of the water-year type.

dimensions.label: Drought stage

dimensions.label: Precipitation
dimensions.read: Precipitation affects local supply and cost district by district, not the consolidated revenue line, which decoupling stabilizes.

dimensions.label: Snowpack
dimensions.read: Sierra snowpack affects the surface and project supplies of its northern districts and hence cost, with revenue insulated by decoupling.

dimensions.label: State Water Project allocation
dimensions.read: State Water Project allocation moves the cost of supply in its project-dependent districts; the revenue adjustment mechanism keeps authorized revenue steady.

detail.logic: Whether the cash the system throws off in a year is enough to cover what it owes that year on its loans (principal plus interest, known as debt service). Above 1.0 means it covers it with room to spare; below 1.0 means it does not.

water_rights.note: Water rights as filed with the State Water Resources Control Board. The right type, status, face value and point of diversion are carried exactly as the state publishes them (high confidence). Annual diverted volumes are DERIVED by summing the filed monthly figures for that right, year and diversion type (medium confidence); the monthly figures are the source of truth. exposure.text: A very large, mostly residential customer base and substantial own-source supply from the Los Angeles Aqueduct give the system a broad, relatively steady revenue base. Volumetric water charges still move with dry-year demand, and rate pass-throughs adjust over time, leaving partial exposure.
exposure._source: LADWP Water System ACFR revenue notes; Board rate ordinance pass-throughs

narrative.supply_profile: LADWP draws on the Los Angeles Aqueduct (Eastern Sierra), Metropolitan Water District imports (State Water Project and Colorado River), and local groundwater, so Eastern Sierra snowpack is unusually central to its cheapest supply.
narrative.cost_link: Dry years raise LADWP's supply cost sharply (less Aqueduct, more MWD and groundwater) while its large mostly-residential base and pass-through rates keep revenue steadier.

dimensions.label: Water-year type
dimensions.read: A dry water-year type cuts Aqueduct and imported deliveries together, raising LADWP's reliance on costlier MWD purchases and groundwater.

dimensions.label: Drought stage
dimensions.read: Local drought stage drives mandatory conservation across a very large customer base; volumetric charges fall while a broad fixed base and rate pass-throughs cushion revenue.

dimensions.label: Precipitation
dimensions.read: Local precipitation matters less to LADWP's supply than Eastern Sierra runoff; dry local years mainly raise outdoor demand.

dimensions.label: Snowpack
dimensions.read: Eastern Sierra April-1 snowpack sets Los Angeles Aqueduct flow, LADWP's lowest-cost supply, so a thin snowpack year forces costlier MWD purchases and directly raises supply cost.

dimensions.label: State Water Project allocation
dimensions.read: State Water Project allocation reaches LADWP indirectly through Metropolitan Water District; a low allocation year raises the cost and tightens the availability of those backstop imports.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.absence: No composite is composed for this system. 1 of 3 components could be computed (Drought regime), which is not enough to compose a read over. The components that could not be computed are listed with the reason each one failed; a single reading presented as a composite would claim a completeness this system does not have.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: CARPINTERIA
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. One agency is named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Carpinteria GSA
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 3-018_7a_Hydrographs_Carpenteria.pdf

2) It is noted that during this 10-year period since 1998 (i.e.,1999 through 2008), the annual average rainfall was 16.8 inches, which is approximately 15 percent less than the longterm annual average of 19.8 inches. During this period, however, annual groundwater pumping averaged only approximately 3,600 afy, which is approximately 20 to 30 percent less than the previous estimates of basin yield that range between 4,500 to 5,000 afy. The observation that water levels gradually declined under these conditions of recharge and pumping suggests that previous estimates of basin yield may have been overestimated. The results of the change in groundwater storage calculations are summarized below:
Fall 1984 through Fall 1991: 15,988 acre-feet of storage depletion;
Fall 1991 through Spring 1998: 17,661 acre-feet storage increase;
Spring 1998 through Fall 2008: 5,879 acre-feet of storage depletion.
Source:  3-018_7a_06-0125_TechMemo_Task1_20120221.pdf  pg 9-10

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). exposure.text: The District is a single purpose water enterprise supported solely by water revenue, and it serves a large share of agricultural demand (avocado and citrus) that is highly weather sensitive. With little revenue diversification, dry-year volume changes flow more directly to the bottom line.
exposure._source: Carpinteria Valley Water District FY2023 ACFR, Letter of Transmittal (supported solely by water revenue)

narrative.supply_profile: Carpinteria Valley Water District blends Lake Cachuma, State Water Project, and groundwater and serves heavy weather-sensitive agricultural demand (avocado and citrus), and it is supported solely by water revenue.
narrative.cost_link: With revenue coming solely from water and a large agricultural share, Carpinteria is the most weather-exposed of the cohort: dry years raise supply cost and, through conservation, cut the water revenue it depends on.

dimensions.label: Water-year type
dimensions.read: A dry water-year type reduces Cachuma and State Water Project deliveries at the same time as it raises irrigation demand, a double squeeze for an ag-heavy district.

dimensions.label: Drought stage
dimensions.read: Local drought stage drives conservation among growers; with no non-water revenue, the volumetric drop flows more directly to the bottom line than at a diversified system.

dimensions.label: Precipitation
dimensions.read: Local precipitation fills Lake Cachuma and reduces irrigation demand, so a dry precipitation year both lowers cheap local supply and raises agricultural water use and cost.

dimensions.label: Snowpack
dimensions.read: Sierra snowpack matters to Carpinteria through its State Water Project share; a thin snowpack year raises its imported-water cost.

dimensions.label: State Water Project allocation
dimensions.read: A low State Water Project allocation cuts one of Carpinteria's three sources, pushing it toward Cachuma and groundwater and raising cost in dry years.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

The system's own 2024 report states that 34.5% of its supply came from sources it produces itself, which the single code cannot show. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 5 documented, 2 partial, 1 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
