governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 6 documented, 0 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 630 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents a collective-choice mechanism: customers are shareholders who elect a named board that governs the company. Turnout and specific member votes on major decisions are not documented, but the elected-board structure and its membership are on record.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and run by a named board they elect, documented in its Form 990 governance section.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; named elected board of directors (Form 990).

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0243093, first registered 03/03/1950, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 12/8/2025. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: Nesting is documented on the supply side: SDWIS records the system as buying treated surface water wholesale, so it sits inside a larger regional supplier's system. Its role in basin or regional governance is not documented, so the nesting on record is physical rather than a governed layer.
principles.finding: The system buys treated water wholesale from a larger supplier, so it is nested inside a regional water enterprise.

The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. Point-in-time counts (connections, population) are matched to the closest eAR year and never summed. Every derived figure states its formula and accounting rationale.
denominators.monthly_source: California open-data portal (data.ca.gov): the separate Produced Water (by month and source) and Delivered Water (by month and connection type) resources, which cover every public water system (not only urban suppliers), one resource per reporting year, matched by exact PWSID. member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

pwss_volume.title: Water volume history (DWR PWSS survey)

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending November 30
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends November 30. A fiscal year therefore shares eleven of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other one with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 11 of the 12 years, across 3 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 90 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 13 were left blank. 8 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

basins.name: PLEASANT VALLEY
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has designated it in critical overdraft: the state has found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. That is a supply-risk signal about the basin itself, not a finding about this system. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. 3 agencies are named for this basin, listed below.

basins.gw_level_comment:
CRITICAL OVERDRAFT 2016
Source: 4-006_7a_Hydrographs_PleasantValley.pdf

Source:  4-006_7a_2016GWConditionsReportFINAL.pdf  pg. 12

basins.subsidence_comment:
1) According to the report (wri024136), Water-level declines in the basin have induced land subsidence that was first measured in 1939 and have resulted in as much as 2.7 feet land subsidence in the southern part of the Oxnard Plain. The model simulated a total of 3 feet of land subsidence in the southern part of the Oxnard Plain and as much as 5 feet in the Las Posas Valley subbasins. Model simulations indicate that most of the land subsidence occurred after the drought of the late 1920s and during the agricultural expansion of the 1950s and 1960s. The results also indicate that subsidence occurred primarily in the upper-aquifer system prior to 1959, but in the lower-aquifer system between 1959-93 owing to an increase in pumpage from the lower-aquifer system.
Source: 4-008_7b_SimulationofgroundwaterSurfaceWaterFlowinSantaClara-CalleguarsBasinVenturaCountyCa.pdf

2) Two continuous GPS site in the basin (VNCO in Ventura and P729 near El Rio) showing recent subsidence
Source: 4-008_7b_GPSStationP729 and 4-008_7b_GPSStationVNCO

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.
sgma_basin.source: CA DWR Bulletin 118 groundwater basins and SGMA Basin Prioritization, https://gis.water.ca.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Geoscientific/i08_B118_CA_GroundwaterBasins/MapServer/0/query Retrieved 2026-08-18.

sdwis_compliance.plain_lead: Two federal EPA tables disagree about this system. One lists no violations; the other points to 3 violation records it does not actually contain. Because the sources contradict each other, this system cannot be confirmed clean and cannot be confirmed as having violated. The conflict is preserved below rather than resolved.
sdwis_compliance.reason: Checked on 2026-08-31: the federal VIOLATION table returned no rows for PWSID CA5610058, but VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC references 3 violation id(s) for the same system. EPA's own tables disagree, so this system cannot be reported as clean. The disagreement is recorded and not reconciled; no violation record was invented for the referenced ids, because none was returned.
sdwis_compliance.title: Drinking-water compliance (US EPA SDWIS)

tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA5610058. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.
Returned 6 link row(s) for PWSID CA5610058, naming 3 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 1106005, 806004, 9706003.

gap_evidence.status_line: 3 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 1106005, 806004, 9706003. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.
gap_evidence.source: US EPA Envirofacts SDWIS, https://data.epa.gov/efservice, tables VIOLATION and VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC, queried with the BEGINNING operator on the full PWSID. Retrieved 2026-09-23.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $1,240,240 (990 program-service revenue) minus $997,871 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $242,369. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A shareholder-owned mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving about 630 service connections (roughly 618 households, ~2,079 residents) in Camarillo, Ventura County, on flat valley terrain. [C][E][1] Owned by its shareholders and run not for profit. [1][990]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $1,952,968 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $1,269,651 and total expenses of $1,594,385, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is its own local wells (Wells 4, 5, and 6, used roughly April to November) supplemented December to March with imported water delivered through Calleguas Municipal Water District, about 300 million gallons a year. [1][2] SDWIS classifies the primary source as purchased surface water. [C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Founded March 3, 1950 as a private nonprofit mutual water company owned by its shareholders, serving the Camarillo community. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Shareholder-owned with a board whose meetings are described as open to public participation; the company is a CalWARN mutual-aid member. [1] Named directors and published minutes were not found online. [1]

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: State drinking-water compliance standing is shown below from the SAFER risk assessment. [S] No litigation, fire, or flood affecting the system was found in the public record. [1]

compliance.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Not At-Risk. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-08-27.
compliance.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A clearly documented founding (1950) and supply model: owned wells for most of the year, imported water only in the dry months, which limits purchased-water cost. [1] CalWARN membership gives it mutual-aid backup. [1] Metered connections with a filed rate structure. [E]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Seasonal reliance on imported water still exposes it to wholesale rate and drought-allocation risk in the dry months. [1] At about 630 connections fixed costs run high per connection, and governance detail is thin in the public record. [1]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 13.7% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 13.7% of the service area (128.1 acres), LRA, SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 4.35 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2019-12-01 to 2025-11-30), Ventura County was in severe drought or worse 42.8% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Ventura County (FIPS 06111); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells for 83.6% of its supply and buys 16.4% from other agencies; it holds no surface water right of its own, and the ground beneath it is in critical overdraft, which is the state's finding that the basin is pumped faster than it refills.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.value: Surface Water Purchased (purchased treated surface water)
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Stated in the 2024 report: Fox Canyon and Grimes Canyon aquifers, company deep wells
detail.value: 83.6%. Not printed by the report: it is the remainder after the shares the report does state. The report names exactly two supplies, calls the aquifers primary and states the imported share at 16.4 percent, so the remainder of the supply is the aquifers. The 83.6 figure is that subtraction and is carried at medium confidence; the report does not print it.
detail.source: https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5610058&Year=2024 (as filed: "Our primary water source is the Fox Canyon & Grimes Canyon Aquifers. This water is pumped by our deep")

detail.label: Stated in the 2024 report: Metropolitan Water District of Southern California via Calleguas Municipal Water District
detail.source: https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5610058&Year=2024 (as filed: "Crestview also received 16.4% of our water supply during 2024 from the Metropolitan Municipal Water")

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by PLEASANT VALLEY (4-006) in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

detail.label: Basin placement confidence
detail.value: The basin placement is an areal join and is carried at low; it is never better than the service-area boundary it rests on.
detail.source: BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from this system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report, which states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: These two records disagree and both are kept as filed. The State Water Board inventory publishes this system's primary source as Surface Water Purchased. Its own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report states a mix in which pumps 83.6% from its own wells, which is the majority of its supply. The band above is built from the report, because the report states figures and the inventory states one code; the code is not corrected, overwritten or removed, and a reader can see both.
components.cross_source_heading: The two records disagree, and both are kept as filed
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5610058&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)
Form 990 Part IX line 25 (total functional expenses)
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation), subtracted for the excluding variant

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 5 documented, 1 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Verified, so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 85 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents a collective-choice mechanism: customers are shareholders who elect a named board that governs the company. Turnout and specific member votes on major decisions are not documented, but the elected-board structure and its membership are on record.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and run by a named board they elect, documented in its Form 990 governance section.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; named elected board of directors (Form 990).

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0063646, first registered 12/22/1910, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 12/31/2025. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.
principles.signal: SDWIS Primary Water Source Type: groundwater (shared basin).

structure.display: Uniform: fixed base plus a single volumetric rate, billed quarterly, priced per HCF

usage_levels.sentence: Defined single-family usage levels, identical for every company so the bill is comparable: Low = 5 HCF/month (~125 gallons/day); Median = 10 HCF/month (~249 gallons/day); High = 25 HCF/month (~623 gallons/day). 1 HCF = 748 gallons, and 1 thousand gallons = 1,000 gallons. components.name: Equity as a share of assets

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. The quartiles are never added up, weighted, ranked or turned into a single figure: this is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. A metric this system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place, is named above rather than counted against it.
cohort_position.cohort_note: The cohort is the mutual water companies in this project that file a Form 990 carrying financial data, which is not a sample of California's mutuals. Each metric places only the systems that report it at comparability tier A or B, so the n differs by metric and is stated on every line.

The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 10 survey years, 2013 to 2022. Production carries a positive figure in all 10 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in only 4 of the 10 years, across 3 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 78 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence.
coverage.assurance: This data was pulled and verified in full. The thinness above is what Del Norte Mutual Water Company filed with the survey, not a gap in what we retrieved. Its production filing is complete over the same period, which is the clearest evidence that the pull worked.
coverage.unit_note: 31 of its 77 delivery figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain. Those figures are shown as filed in the table and were not converted to acre-feet, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume. That is why the delivery table shows figures the delivery chart cannot draw.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2022. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

basins.name: SANTA CLARA RIVER VALLEY - OXNARD
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has designated it in critical overdraft: the state has found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. That is a supply-risk signal about the basin itself, not a finding about this system. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. 3 agencies are named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Camrosa Water District GSA - Oxnard; County of Ventura GSA - Oxnard Basin Outlying Areas; Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency GSA - Oxnard
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 4-004.02_7a_Hydrographs_Oxnard.pdf

2) There is evidence for the occurrence of long-term overdraft in at least two of the groundwater basins of the District. Groundwater levels have generally been declining for periods of several decades in the Oxnard Plain and Pleasant Valley basins. While the factors causing declining groundwater trends may have varied among these two basins, long-term replenishment rates have not kept up with long-term withdrawal rates in either of them. Thus, these basins are considered by the District to be in a condition of long-term overdraft.
Source: 4-004.02_7a_2016GWConditionsReportFINAL.pdf  pg. 12
basins.subsidence_comment:
1)  Water-level declines in the basin have induced land subsidence that was first measured in 1939 and have resulted in as much as 2.7 feet land subsidence in the southern part of the Oxnard Plain. The model simulated a total of 3 feet of land subsidence in the southern part of the Oxnard Plain and as much as 5 feet in the Las Posas Valley subbasins. Model simulations indicate that most of the land subsidence occurred after the drought of the late 1920s and during the agricultural expansion of the 1950s and 1960s. The results also indicate that subsidence occurred primarily in the upper-aquifer system prior to 1959, but in the lower-aquifer system between 1959-93 owing to an increase in pumpage from the lower-aquifer system. 

"groundwater and oil and gas production are probably major causes in the Oxnard Plain subbasin, and tectonic activity is probably a minor cause (Hanson et al., 2003)" Subsidence has been documented in the Oxnard Plain:                                                     Source: 4-004.02_7b_SimulationofgroundwaterSurfaceWaterFlowinSantaClara-CalleguarsBasinVenturaCountyWIR02-4136CaPDF
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $1,288,692 (990 program-service revenue) minus $70,000 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $1,218,692. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A California mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving about 85 service connections and roughly 215 residents in Somis, in the Las Posas Valley of Ventura County; strongly agricultural in character, allocating water by acreage and stock ownership. [C][E][1] Its legal corporate name is Del Norte Water Company; the Mutual appears in the water-system label. [2]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $1,390,755 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $70,000 and total expenses of $70,000, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is local groundwater from wells in the Las Posas Valley / Somis area; it is self-supplied and not a Calleguas imported-water member. [C][1] SDWIS classifies the primary source as groundwater. [C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Founded in 1910 (California incorporation December 22, 1910) to provide both domestic and irrigation water in the Somis area, structured as a mutual with 2,500 shares of stock; historically only farming landowners in the service area held stock, and water was allocated by a formula tied to acreage and share ownership. [1][2]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Governed by a shareholder board (CEO John C. Orr and directors per the State corporate record); the allocation rules are set in the bylaws and share structure. [1][2] Published minutes were not found online.

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: State drinking-water compliance standing is shown below from the SAFER risk assessment. [S] In De Boni Corporation v. Del Norte Water Company (2011), the Court of Appeal upheld the company's share-and-acreage water-allocation system, including a domestic-threshold rule, as lawful and non-discriminatory. [1]

compliance.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as At-Risk. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-08-27.
compliance.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A very long-established mutual (1910) with a clearly documented, court-tested allocation system tying water rights to land and shares. [1][2] Self-supplied groundwater with no wholesale purchase cost. [C] Its governance rules are concrete enough to have been litigated and upheld. [1]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Single-basin groundwater dependence in the Las Posas Valley, an adjudicated and stressed basin, is a direct drought and pumping-limit risk. [C] At about 85 connections it is very small, and its agricultural allocation model concentrates decisions among landowning shareholders. [1]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Ventura County was in severe drought or worse 42.8% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Ventura County (FIPS 06111); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; no surface water right of its own is on record, and the ground beneath it is in critical overdraft, which is the state's finding that the basin is pumped faster than it refills.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: No surface water right of its own is recorded
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by SANTA CLARA RIVER VALLEY - OXNARD (4-004.02) in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

detail.label: Basin placement confidence
detail.value: The basin placement is an areal join and is carried at medium; it is never better than the service-area boundary it rests on.
detail.source: BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5602104&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 5 documented, 1 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 47 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents a collective-choice mechanism: customers are shareholders who elect a named board that governs the company. Turnout and specific member votes on major decisions are not documented, but the elected-board structure and its membership are on record.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and run by a named board they elect, documented in its Form 990 governance section.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; named elected board of directors (Form 990).

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0071659, first registered 01/02/1913, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 2/2/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.
principles.signal: SDWIS Primary Water Source Type: groundwater (shared basin).

anomalies.title: FY2022 net assets do not sum to the lines we extract
anomalies.flag_reason: Flagged because the lines we extracted do not sum to the total reported on the filing: the ending net assets on the form do not equal the beginning net assets plus the year's surplus or deficit plus the other changes we read. This may indicate a line on the form that we did not map, rather than an error by the company. The figure is shown exactly as filed, and the difference is noted, not corrected.

what.text: FY2022 net assets are carried exactly as filed at $2,214,030. The lines we extracted do not sum to that total: the ending net assets it reports (Form 990 Part XI line 10) should equal the beginning net assets (line 4) plus revenue less expenses (line 3) plus other changes (lines 5-9), which computes to $2,091,800 (a difference of $122,230 against the $2,214,030 on the form). This may mean a line on the form that we do not yet read, rather than an error by the company. The filed figure is kept and the difference is flagged, not reconciled.

what.confidence_reason: The net-assets figure is a direct filed line item, carried exactly as filed; confidence is held to medium (not high) because the lines we extract do not sum to the total on the form, so the figure is flagged rather than presented as clean. That can mean a line we do not read as easily as an inconsistency in the filing, and this project has found the former three times. Nothing is reconciled.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 10 survey years, 2013 to 2022. Production carries a positive figure in all 10 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 10 of those years, across 2 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 101 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2022. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: SANTA CLARA RIVER VALLEY - SANTA PAULA
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. One agency is named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: County of Ventura GSA - Santa Paula Basin Outlying Areas
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 4-004.04_7a_Hydrographs_SantaPaula.pdf

2) The the majority of wells in the Santa Paula basin have experienced a gradual GWL decline during the 1998-2005 observation period and the 2005 to present observation period. The water level fluctuations observed from 1998 to 2009 in the Santa Paula Basin cannot be attributed soley to spatial or temporal variations in pumping.
Source: Source:  4-004.04_7a_2016GWConditionsReportFINAL.pdf  pg. 12
basins.subsidence_comment:
1) Section 2.8 (2013);  Figure 2.8 shows subsidence zones based on best available data (1973).  Subsidence zones not updated due to lack of geodetic survey data.
Source: Source: 4-004.03_7b_2013_VenturaCountyGeneral_Plan_Hazards_Appendix.pdf
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

basins.name: SANTA CLARA RIVER VALLEY - FILLMORE
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. One agency is named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Fillmore and Piru Basins GSA - Fillmore
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 4-004.05_7a_Hydrographs_Fillmore.pdf

2) Groundwater level decline shown in figures and acknowledged in text of report.
Source: 4-004.05_7a_2014-2015PiruFillmoreBasinsBiennialGWCondRptFINAL.pdf   pg. ii, figures 18-22
basins.subsidence_comment:
1) Section 2.8 (2013);  Figure 2.8 shows subsidence zones based on best available data (1973).  Subsidence zones not updated due to lack of geodetic survey data.
Source: Source: 4-004.03_7b_2013_VenturaCountyGeneral_Plan_Hazards_Appendix.pdf

In addition to the Ventura County General Plan, Hazards Appendix, that identified Fillmore and Piru basins as being in an area of probable subsidence, the 1996 USGS Open-File Report 96-517 discussed non-tectonic deformation and subsidence in the Piru and Fillmore area.  The USGS (1996) report indicated that 60 mm of non-tectonic subsidence occurred between 1975 and 1978.  Between 1975 and 1989, about 1.5 cm was identified in the same area, suggesting that aquifer recharge occurred and that the ground surface elevation somewhat rebounded.  Because subsidence was identified and the rebound was not complete, a small amount of non-tectonic subsidence was interpreted by the USGS to have occurred between 1975 and 1989.  Although most of the 60 mm of observed subsidence appeared to be elastic, the potential for subsidence exists.
USGS Open File Report 96-517.docx
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

gap_evidence.status_line: 3 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 406004, 606005, 9606001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.
gap_evidence.source: US EPA Envirofacts SDWIS, https://data.epa.gov/efservice, tables VIOLATION and VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC, queried with the BEGINNING operator on the full PWSID. Retrieved 2026-09-23.

safer_standing.title: State drinking-water standing (SAFER)
safer_standing.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Not At-Risk. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-08-27.

comparable.state_basis: State Water Board definition: unrestricted cash and investments divided by per-day operating expenses excluding depreciation (Draft Final White Paper, July 16, 2020, p. 28). The Hydronomics headline uses the same basis as far as Form 990 allows. The state publishes a risk level and a threshold result, not a figure, and the file does not state which assessment year it reflects.
comparable.state_definition_source: State Water Resources Control Board, Draft Final White Paper Discussion On: Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, pp. 27 and 28
comparable.ours_basis: Computed by this project from the filed financial statements, on the basis set out in the anchor-metrics framework.
comparable.comparison_note: Two readings of the same indicator from two different bases. They are shown side by side and are deliberately NOT combined: the state's is a threshold test whose definition this project does not hold, and this project's is a computed figure. Neither is used to check or correct the other.

comparable.state_basis: State Water Board definition: operating revenue divided by operating expenses including depreciation (Draft Final White Paper, July 16, 2020, p. 27). The state publishes a risk level and a threshold result, not a figure, and the file does not state which assessment year it reflects.

safer_standing.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad
safer_standing.note: Failing, At-Risk, Potentially At-Risk, Not At-Risk and Not Assessed are the State Water Board's own categories and its own determination about this system. They are carried here in the state's words and are not this project's assessment of the company. An automatic designation is made regardless of the category scores beneath it, so a system can be listed At-Risk while scoring NONE or LOW on most categories.
