how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $504,433 (990 program-service revenue) minus $13,753 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $490,680. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A California mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving about 47 service connections in Fillmore, in the Santa Clara River valley of Ventura County, and describing itself as providing both agricultural and domestic water to its members. [C][E][1] The State-regulated domestic side is a handful of connections; the company also serves irrigation. [2]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $740,896 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $13,753 and total expenses of $675,762, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is local groundwater from four active wells (Wells 5, 7, 8, and 9) in the Santa Clara River valley near Fillmore. [2][C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Incorporated January 2, 1913, one of the older mutuals in the Santa Clara River valley, formed to supply agricultural and domestic water to Fillmore-area members. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Governed by a shareholder board and officers (Vice President Paul Romero, CFO/Secretary Salvador Dominguez, and others per directory records). [1] Published bylaws and minutes were not found online.

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A long-established (1913) mixed agricultural-and-domestic mutual with its own four-well groundwater supply and no wholesale purchase cost. [1][2][C] Serves its members at cost. [990]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Single-basin groundwater dependence in the Santa Clara River valley is a direct drought risk. [C] With only about 47 connections on the domestic side, fixed costs land on a tiny base, and governance detail is thin in the public record. [1]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 20.3% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 20.3% of the service area (644.8 acres), LRA, SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 16.99 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Ventura County was in severe drought or worse 42.8% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Ventura County (FIPS 06111); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 5 documented, 1 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 36 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents a collective-choice mechanism: customers are shareholders who elect a named board that governs the company. Turnout and specific member votes on major decisions are not documented, but the elected-board structure and its membership are on record.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and run by a named board they elect, documented in its Form 990 governance section.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; named elected board of directors (Form 990).

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0090169, first registered 01/05/1920, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 6/2/2022. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period
calendar_basis.label: Same reporting period. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 9 survey years, 2016 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 9 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 8 of the 9 years, across 2 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 65 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 13 were left blank. 8 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2016 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. basins.name: SANTA CLARA RIVER VALLEY - FILLMORE
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. One agency is named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Fillmore and Piru Basins GSA - Fillmore
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 4-004.05_7a_Hydrographs_Fillmore.pdf

2) Groundwater level decline shown in figures and acknowledged in text of report.
Source: 4-004.05_7a_2014-2015PiruFillmoreBasinsBiennialGWCondRptFINAL.pdf   pg. ii, figures 18-22
basins.subsidence_comment:
1) Section 2.8 (2013);  Figure 2.8 shows subsidence zones based on best available data (1973).  Subsidence zones not updated due to lack of geodetic survey data.
Source: Source: 4-004.03_7b_2013_VenturaCountyGeneral_Plan_Hazards_Appendix.pdf

In addition to the Ventura County General Plan, Hazards Appendix, that identified Fillmore and Piru basins as being in an area of probable subsidence, the 1996 USGS Open-File Report 96-517 discussed non-tectonic deformation and subsidence in the Piru and Fillmore area.  The USGS (1996) report indicated that 60 mm of non-tectonic subsidence occurred between 1975 and 1978.  Between 1975 and 1989, about 1.5 cm was identified in the same area, suggesting that aquifer recharge occurred and that the ground surface elevation somewhat rebounded.  Because subsidence was identified and the rebound was not complete, a small amount of non-tectonic subsidence was interpreted by the USGS to have occurred between 1975 and 1989.  Although most of the 60 mm of observed subsidence appeared to be elastic, the potential for subsidence exists.
USGS Open File Report 96-517.docx

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $262,072 (990 program-service revenue) minus $412,478 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $-150,406. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company serving about 36 service connections and roughly 65 residents in Santa Paula, Ventura County, on the Santa Clara River valley floor. [C][E] Unusually, it is recognized federally as a 501(c)(5) agricultural organization rather than a 501(c)(12) mutual, an as-filed classification we preserve. [1]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $346,455 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $412,478 and total expenses of $367,855, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is local groundwater, including a Well 4 rated about 1,300 gallons per minute near Orcutt Road and East Telegraph Road in Santa Paula, used alternately with an existing well. [2][C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: IRS recognition dates to 1934, implying formation in or before then; the company operates in the Santa Paula groundwater area (a basin adjudicated by a 1996 stipulated judgment, though the company's status as a named party was not confirmed). [1][2]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Governed by a shareholder board and officers (President Guy Cole and four directors in 2025). [1] Published bylaws and minutes were not found online.

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: State drinking-water compliance standing is shown below from the SAFER risk assessment. [S] A 2019 CEQA categorical exemption documents the Well 4 project. [2] No litigation, fire, or flood affecting the system was found in the public record.

compliance.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Not At-Risk. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-08-27.
compliance.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A long-established member system (recognized since 1934) with its own groundwater and a recently added well (Well 4), so its supply has been reinvested in. [1][2] Serves its members at cost. [1]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: At about 36 connections it is one of the smallest systems in the cohort; every fixed cost lands on a tiny base. [C] Single-basin groundwater dependence in the Santa Paula basin is a direct drought and adjudication risk. [2] Its 501(c)(5) classification is unusual and its governance detail is thin in the public record. [1]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 8.9% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 8.9% of the service area (76.5 acres), SRA

detail.label: Moderate zone
detail.value: about 0.4% of the service area (3.5 acres), LRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 3.6 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Ventura County was in severe drought or worse 42.8% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Ventura County (FIPS 06111); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds 3 surface water rights of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds 3 licensed surface water rights of its own
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2023 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA5601125 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5601125&Year=2023 (956975 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5601125&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 5 documented, 1 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 110 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents a collective-choice mechanism: customers are shareholders who elect a named board that governs the company. Turnout and specific member votes on major decisions are not documented, but the elected-board structure and its membership are on record.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and run by a named board they elect, documented in its Form 990 governance section.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; named elected board of directors (Form 990).

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0235505, first registered 04/14/1949, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 2/24/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.

metrics.name: Member Income Ratio
metrics.logic: The share of the mutual's income that comes from its own members. The tax rules for this kind of member-owned nonprofit (a 501(c)(12) mutual) expect at least 85 percent to come from members; slipping below can signal that member charges are not covering costs, and can even put the tax status at risk.
metrics.formula: member gross income / total gross income (members + other sources)
source_lines: Form 990 Part V line 11a (gross income from members)
Form 990 Part V line 11b (gross income from other sources)
metrics.confidence_reason: This depends on a figure the filing does not give, so we leave it not reported rather than guess.

unit_economics.title: Unit economics
unit_economics.basis_note: Every metric here is PER CUSTOMER (a metered service connection). It is not a per-member figure; the member (shareholder) count is a different denominator, shown in the denominator block. The visible cell shows the value and its classification; the numerator, denominator, formula, and rationale are in each metric's LOGIC popup.

logic.what_it_is: Revenue customers paid for water service, read straight off the filed eAR Section 8b water-rate line. A DIRECT filed figure, not computed by us.

logic.formula_per_customer: water rate revenue $157,665 / 106 connections = $1,487.41 per connection
logic.formula_share: water rate revenue $157,665 / total annual revenue (eAR Section 8b B1.8) $158,165 = 99.68%
logic.period_treatment: Numerator (eAR Section 8b, the calendar year 2023) and denominator (eAR Section 4 connections reported in the same eAR filing) are both the eAR reporting year 2023, so the two sides are bound to the same reporting year.
logic.rationale: Dividing water-rate revenue by the number of metered service connections gives the average revenue per customer; dividing by total annual revenue shows how much of the system's income comes from water rates.

metrics.name: Assessment revenue (990 program-service revenue not matched to eAR water-rate revenue)

logic.what_it_is: A DERIVED residual (medium confidence): the part of the Form 990 program-service revenue that is not matched by the eAR water-rate revenue for the same period. Computed by us, not a filed line.

input_a.name: Form 990 program-service revenue
input_a.source: Form 990 Part VIII line 2 (total program-service revenue), fiscal year 2023 ending December 31, 2023

input_b.name: eAR water-rate revenue
input_b.source: State Water Board eAR Section 8b, question B1.1 + B1.2 (revenue from water rates), reporting year 2023

residual.period_alignment: Both inputs cover the same period: the eAR Section 8b is the calendar year 2023 and the Form 990 fiscal year 2023 ends December 31, 2023, so the residual is period-aligned.
residual.represents: What it IS: revenue the system booked as program service on its 990 that is not accounted for by the eAR water-rate line, plausibly member assessments and other service revenue.
residual.does_not_represent: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

logic.formula_per_customer: residual $1,181 / 106 connections = $11.14 per connection
logic.formula_share: residual $1,181 / 990 program-service revenue $158,846 = 0.74%

denominators.title: System Size and Water Use
denominators.note: System size and water use per fiscal year (the operating denominators that per-customer and per-acre metrics divide by), each cited to file and field. The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. Point-in-time counts (connections, population) are matched to the closest eAR year and never summed. Every derived figure states its formula and accounting rationale.
denominators.monthly_source: California open-data portal (data.ca.gov): the separate Produced Water (by month and source) and Delivered Water (by month and connection type) resources, which cover every public water system (not only urban suppliers), one resource per reporting year, matched by exact PWSID. This is the aggregate publication of eAR Section 6.

customer.label: Customer (service connection)

member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

rows.alignment_method: eAR annual total, calendar filer, equals fiscal year (not a monthly recast)

connections.note: Point-in-time figure from eAR reporting year 2021, the eAR year closest to the fiscal year ending December 31, 2021. Not recast: a count of connections (or residents) is a snapshot and cannot be summed across months the way a volume can.

This differs from the section-file CurTotalConnections (SDWIS-records) line used for RY2023/2024 by up to one year of growth; both bases are preserved and flagged, never reconciled.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 3 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 85 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 10 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: UPPER OJAI VALLEY
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment: No documented Groundwater Level Declines
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

sdwis_compliance.reason: Checked on 2026-08-31: the federal VIOLATION table returned no rows for PWSID CA5601120, but VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC references 2 violation id(s) for the same system. tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA5601120. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.
Returned 4 link row(s) for PWSID CA5601120, naming 2 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 306002, 9706001.

gap_evidence.status_line: 2 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 306002, 9706001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $158,846 (990 program-service revenue) minus $157,665 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $1,181. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A California mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving about 110 service connections and roughly 340 residents in the Sisar Canyon and Upper Ojai area between Ojai and Santa Paula, Ventura County, on canyon and upper-valley terrain. [C][E][2] It supplies domestic groundwater to its members. [2]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $131,040 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $158,165 and total expenses of $176,668, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is domestic groundwater; the company reported supplying about 907 acre-feet to members in 2022. Sisar Creek forms part of the eastern boundary of the Upper Ojai Valley groundwater basin. [2][E]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: IRS recognition dates to 1952, implying formation in or before then; the company serves the Sisar Canyon corridor in the Upper Ojai Valley. It filed Form 990-EZ through 2019 and full Form 990 thereafter. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Governed by a shareholder board (President John Lemmer, 2024 to 2025; Rod Thompson previously). [1] Published bylaws and minutes were not found online.

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: State drinking-water compliance standing is shown below from the SAFER risk assessment. [S] The 2017 Thomas Fire burned heavily through Upper Ojai, but no source documents specific impact on this system. [2]

compliance.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Not At-Risk. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-08-27.

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A long-established (1952) domestic mutual with its own groundwater in the Upper Ojai Valley and a reported supply of about 907 acre-feet. [1][2] Serves its members at cost. [1]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Canyon and Upper Ojai terrain place it in wildfire and post-fire debris-flow country; the 2017 Thomas Fire burned the corridor. [2] Single-basin groundwater dependence is a drought risk, and at about 110 connections fixed costs run high per connection. [C]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (448.2 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 3.78 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Ventura County was in severe drought or worse 42.8% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Ventura County (FIPS 06111); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5601120&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)
Form 990 Part IX line 25 (total functional expenses)
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation), subtracted for the excluding variant

metrics.name: Member Income Ratio
metrics.logic: The share of the mutual's income that comes from its own members. The tax rules for this kind of member-owned nonprofit (a 501(c)(12) mutual) expect at least 85 percent to come from members; slipping below can signal that member charges are not covering costs, and can even put the tax status at risk.
metrics.formula: member gross income / total gross income (members + other sources)
source_lines: Form 990 Part V line 11a (gross income from members)
Form 990 Part V line 11b (gross income from other sources)

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: An agricultural irrigation mutual water company (501(c)(12)) in the Las Posas Valley near Camarillo and Somis, Ventura County, on flat valley terrain. [1][2] It delivers irrigation water to member landowners and is not a State-regulated public drinking-water system, so it has no PWSID. [C][1]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $118,989 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Water source is not stated in a public drinking-water filing (no SDWIS record). The company sits in the Las Posas Valley basin managed by the Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency and its name references the Arroyo Las Posas, consistent with groundwater irrigation, but no cited source states its wells or volume. [2][C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Incorporated March 1, 1985 (IRS recognition 1987) as an irrigation mutual in the Las Posas Valley. A detailed founding narrative is not documented. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Governed by volunteer, uncompensated officers and directors (President Keith M. Huss, CFO/Secretary Laura L. Huss, and directors per State and IRS records). [1] Published bylaws and minutes were not found online.

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: This company has no PWSID and is not in the State Water Board SAFER risk assessment, so a State compliance standing is not reported. [C] No litigation, fire, or flood affecting the system was found in the public record. [1]

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A member-owned irrigation mutual serving landowners at cost in the Las Posas Valley. [1] Small and low-overhead, with volunteer governance. [1]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Almost nothing about its supply is in the public drinking-water record (no PWSID, no SDWIS entry), so an outside reader cannot verify its source or condition. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.absence: No composite is composed for this system. 1 of 3 components could be computed (Drought regime), which is not enough to compose a read over. The components that could not be computed are listed with the reason each one failed; a single reading presented as a composite would claim a completeness this system does not have.

components.name: Fire hazard

components.reason: No PWSID is recorded for this system, so there is no SABL service-area polygon to intersect with the hazard zone layer. The join is areal and there is no geometry to join with; this is a missing key, not a finding that the system faces no fire hazard.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: An agricultural irrigation mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving farmland in the Piru area of the Santa Clara River valley, Ventura County, on flat valley and river-terrace terrain. [1][2] It is irrigation-only and not a State-regulated public drinking-water system (no PWSID), distinct from the town of Piru's domestic supply, which is run by California American Water. [1][C]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $56,587 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is untreated groundwater from wells plus surface water diverted from Piru Creek, a Santa Clara River tributary conserved by United Water Conservation District, delivered to about 525 acres of farmland. [1][2]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: Form 990 Part X lines 10a and 10b are not both reported for this system, so the ratio is not computable.

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: The company was formed around 1989 to 1991 to take over the irrigation (non-domestic) portion of the former investor-owned Piru water utility; a 1991 CPUC decision describes it acquiring the pumped-well and Piru Creek irrigation systems. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Governed by a shareholder board and officers (President and Treasurer Jim Finch, Secretary Laurie Denger per the 2024 filing). [2] Published bylaws and minutes were not found online.

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: This company has no PWSID and is not in the State Water Board SAFER risk assessment, so a State compliance standing is not reported. [C] No litigation, fire, or flood affecting the system was found in the public record beyond its 1991 formation from the former utility. [1]

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A member-owned irrigation mutual with a documented origin (1991 CPUC decision) and a dual supply of wells plus Piru Creek surface water. [1] Serves farmland at cost. [2]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Irrigation-only and tied to agricultural land use in the Santa Clara River valley; drought and Piru Creek / United Water Conservation District supply conditions are direct risks. [1] No drinking-water record (no PWSID) and thin public governance detail. [2]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.absence: No composite is composed for this system. 1 of 3 components could be computed (Drought regime), which is not enough to compose a read over. The components that could not be computed are listed with the reason each one failed; a single reading presented as a composite would claim a completeness this system does not have.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 3 documented, 3 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Verified, so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 27 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The eAR documents that the system charges for water and reports a rate structure, so charges are tied to service. The detailed basis (metered tiers versus shares or parcels) is only partially documented for a system this small, so the proportionality evidence is incomplete.
principles.finding: The system charges customers for water and reports a rate structure to the State, but the detailed basis is only partially documented.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer-charges block.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The mutual-company form documents that customers are shareholders who elect the directors, so a collective-choice mechanism exists on paper. No record of the specific board, elections, or member votes was found, so the evidence is partial. The specific board is now on the record: the Statement of Information filed 7/2/2026 names 1 director and 3 officers, transcribed as filed. That closes one of the gaps named above. It does NOT close the others: a filed roster shows who governs, not how members choose them, and carries no election, turnout or member vote. The evidence status therefore stays PARTIAL, because what this principle asks about is member participation and that remains undocumented.
principles.finding: As a mutual it is owned by its customer-shareholders who elect the board, but specific board membership and votes are not documented.
principles.signal: Mutual (501(c)(12)) ownership structure; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0494202, first registered 07/19/1965, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 7/2/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.
principles.signal: SDWIS Primary Water Source Type: groundwater (shared basin).

member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water.
