governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 5 documented, 1 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 92 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents a collective-choice mechanism: customers are shareholders who elect a named board that governs the company. Turnout and specific member votes on major decisions are not documented, but the elected-board structure and its membership are on record.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and run by a named board they elect, documented in its Form 990 governance section.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; named elected board of directors (Form 990).

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0954249, first registered 03/06/1980, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 4/21/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.
principles.signal: SDWIS Primary Water Source Type: groundwater (shared basin).

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 10 of the 12 years, from 1 customer class.
coverage.tail: Separately, 93 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 14 were left blank. 16 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: SANTA YNEZ RIVER VALLEY
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Medium priority, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. 3 agencies are named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Santa Ynez River Valley Basin Central Management Area GSA; Santa Ynez River Valley Basin Eastern Management Area GSA; Santa Ynez River Valley Basin Western Management Area GSA
basins.gw_level_comment:
No documented Groundwater Level Declines

2) This basin is not subject to overdraft (i.e. a progressive long-term drop in water levels) because the average annual flow to the Santa Ynez River (the main recharge source) is greater than the volume of the basin. Water is extracted from this basin for municipal and agricultural uses by many entities both private and public.
Source: 3-015_7a_SLOGP_2012-2014_ASR FINAL.pdf pg. 54 

3) There was no significant change in water level or water quality during the 2009-2011 time period in the Lompoc area. As previously mentioned, water levels are balanced by releases made from Lake Cachuma, thus in essence the basin is managed to maintain water level and water quality thresholds under current operation of the reservoir.
Source: 3-015_7a_SantaBarbaraCoGWReport-2011.pdf  pg. 66
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.
sgma_basin.source: CA DWR Bulletin 118 groundwater basins and SGMA Basin Prioritization, https://gis.water.ca.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Geoscientific/i08_B118_CA_GroundwaterBasins/MapServer/0/query Retrieved 2026-08-18.

tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA4200619. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.

gap_evidence.status_line: 1 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 600001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $248,215 (990 program-service revenue) minus $210,201 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $38,014. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A California mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving about 92 service connections and roughly 304 residents in the Santa Ynez Rancho Estates residential subdivision, Santa Ynez Valley, Santa Barbara County. [C][E][1] It is a residential estates community system, not agricultural. [1]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $546,703 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $213,691 and total expenses of $272,675, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is local groundwater from the Santa Ynez River Valley basin, with at least one 100,000-gallon storage tank; no wholesale supplier was identified. [1][2] SDWIS classifies the primary source as groundwater. [C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Incorporated March 6, 1980 (IRS recognition 1986) to supply water to the Santa Ynez Rancho Estates subdivision as a member-owned mutual. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Governed by a shareholder board (President Hayden Landon and officers in FY2024, all uncompensated). [1] It is a CalWARN mutual-aid member. Published bylaws and minutes were not found online.

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A clearly documented founding (1980) tied to a defined residential subdivision, with its own groundwater and storage. [1] An active named volunteer board and CalWARN mutual-aid membership. [1]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Single-basin groundwater dependence with a flagged nitrate vulnerability from surrounding livestock and septic systems. [2] At about 92 connections fixed costs run high per connection, and no backup or wholesale supply is documented. [1]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 80.4% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
High zone
detail.value: about 80.2% of the service area (427.4 acres), SRA

detail.label: Moderate zone
detail.value: about 19.5% of the service area (104.0 acres), SRA

detail.label: Very High zone
detail.value: about 0.2% of the service area (1.2 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 4.44 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Santa Barbara County was in severe drought or worse 40.9% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Santa Barbara County (FIPS 06083); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2023 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4200619&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 5 documented, 1 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 91 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents a collective-choice mechanism: customers are shareholders who elect a named board that governs the company. Turnout and specific member votes on major decisions are not documented, but the elected-board structure and its membership are on record.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and run by a named board they elect, documented in its Form 990 governance section.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; named elected board of directors (Form 990).

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0147674, first registered 01/06/1932, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 1/22/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.
principles.signal: SDWIS Primary Water Source Type: groundwater (shared basin).

member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending March 31
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends March 31. A fiscal year therefore shares three of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other nine with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 106 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 14 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

violations.violation_name: Consumer Confidence Report Complete Failure to Report
Consumer Confidence Report Complete Failure to Report

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

code_reference.source: US EPA ECHO SDWA bulk data download (https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/SDWA_latest_downloads.zip), member SDWA_REF_CODE_VALUES.csv, retrieved by ranged read (CRC 55b22a40)

tables.says: Returned 5 violation record(s) for PWSID CA4200578, which are the records listed on this page.

Returned 27 link row(s) for PWSID CA4200578, naming 9 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 1100021, 300003, 300009, 400015, 500016, 500017, 600018, 800020, 9700001.

gap_evidence.status_line: 9 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 1100021, 300003, 300009, 400015, 500016, 500017, 600018, 800020, 9700001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.
gap_evidence.source: US EPA Envirofacts SDWIS, https://data.epa.gov/efservice, tables VIOLATION and VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC, queried with the BEGINNING operator on the full PWSID. Retrieved 2026-09-23.

plant_per_acre.logic: Infrastructure built per acre of service area. Gross plant per acre is the primary read because it measures how much plant the system has put in the ground per acre, and unlike net plant it does not fall over time purely because the assets depreciate on the books. Net plant per acre is shown alongside as the depreciated book value per acre.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $35,270 (990 program-service revenue) minus $35,849 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $-579. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A residential mountain-community mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving about 85 to 91 metered single-family connections and roughly 160 residents in Painted Cave, an unincorporated community on San Marcos Pass above Santa Barbara, on steep canyon and mountain terrain zoned very high fire severity. [C][E][2]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $44,152 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $37,270 and total expenses of $32,636, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is entirely groundwater from three active wells, about 8 million gallons a year, with precautionary disinfection only and no treatment plant or purchased water. [2][C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Incorporated January 6, 1932, the oldest of the Santa Barbara batch mutuals, formed to provide domestic water to the Painted Cave mountain community. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Operated by a certified operator (Michael Stephens, Grade 2) under a shareholder board; billing is a flat base charge (about $42) plus a per-unit rate (about $0.75 per HCF). [2] A broader board roster was not found. In a 2026 dispute the company approved a residential water hookup but declined the County Fire Department's request to install a fire hydrant. [2]

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: State drinking-water compliance standing is shown below from the SAFER risk assessment. [S] The community was the origin area of the June 1990 Painted Cave Fire, an arson fire that burned about 5,000 acres and destroyed 427 structures; the record documents the fire geographically, not specific damage to the water system. [3]

compliance.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Not At-Risk. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-08-27.
compliance.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: The oldest mutual in the batch (1932), with its own groundwater and a certified operator on record. [1][2] A defined, tightly bounded mountain-community membership. [2]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Textbook wildland-urban-interface exposure: a canyon community on San Marcos Pass in a very-high fire-severity zone, at the origin of the 1990 Painted Cave Fire, with disinfection-only groundwater and no pressurized fire supply. [2][3] At about 85 connections fixed costs land on a tiny base, and its decision to decline a fire hydrant is a documented risk posture. [2]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 99.5% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 99.5% of the service area (43.1 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 0.93 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-04-01 to 2025-03-31), Santa Barbara County was in severe drought or worse 38.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Santa Barbara County (FIPS 06083); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4200578&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 4 documented, 2 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 23 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The mutual-company form documents that customers are shareholders who elect the directors, so a collective-choice mechanism exists on paper. No record of the specific board, elections, or member votes was found, so the evidence is partial. The specific board was looked for in the state record and is not there. The California Nonprofit Corporation Statement of Information form has no Directors section, so no director roster exists in this filing to report. Structural to the form for this entity type, not a missing extraction. So this gap is not closed, and the evidence status stays PARTIAL for the same reasons as before.
principles.finding: As a mutual it is owned by its customer-shareholders who elect the board, but specific board membership and votes are not documented.
principles.signal: Mutual (501(c)(12)) ownership structure; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 1017677, first registered 02/09/1981, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 5/12/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.
principles.signal: SDWIS Primary Water Source Type: groundwater (shared basin).

residual.period_alignment: Both inputs cover the same period: the eAR Section 8b is the fiscal year ending January 31, 2024 and the Form 990 fiscal year 2024 ends January 31, 2024, so the residual is period-aligned.
residual.represents: What it IS: revenue the system booked as program service on its 990 that is not accounted for by the eAR water-rate line, plausibly member assessments and other service revenue.
residual.does_not_represent: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. The quartiles are never added up, weighted, ranked or turned into a single figure: this is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. A metric this system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place, is named above rather than counted against it.
cohort_position.cohort_note: The cohort is the mutual water companies in this project that file a Form 990 carrying financial data, which is not a sample of California's mutuals. Each metric places only the systems that report it at comparability tier A or B, so the n differs by metric and is stated on every line.

denominators.title: System Size and Water Use
denominators.note: System size and water use per fiscal year (the operating denominators that per-customer and per-acre metrics divide by), each cited to file and field. The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. Point-in-time counts (connections, population) are matched to the closest eAR year and never summed. Every derived figure states its formula and accounting rationale.
denominators.monthly_source: California open-data portal (data.ca.gov): the separate Produced Water (by month and source) and Delivered Water (by month and connection type) resources, which cover every public water system (not only urban suppliers), one resource per reporting year, matched by exact PWSID. This is the aggregate publication of eAR Section 6.

member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending January 31
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends January 31. A fiscal year therefore shares one of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other eleven with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 3 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 97 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 12 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sdwis_compliance.plain_lead: Two federal EPA tables disagree about this system. One lists no violations; the other points to 5 violation records it does not actually contain. Because the sources contradict each other, this system cannot be confirmed clean and cannot be confirmed as having violated. The conflict is preserved below rather than resolved.

tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA4200714. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.
Returned 10 link row(s) for PWSID CA4200714, naming 5 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 200005, 4, 9600001, 9700002, 9800003.

gap_evidence.status_line: 5 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 200005, 4, 9600001, 9700002, 9800003. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $65,176 (990 program-service revenue) minus $20,400 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $44,776. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A small domestic mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving about 23 service connections and roughly 43 residents in the Hollister Ranch and Gaviota coast area of Santa Barbara County, on coastal terrace and rural ranch terrain about 30 miles west of Santa Barbara. [C][E][2] SDWIS spells the system San Augustine; the company we hold is San Augustin, a one-letter variant of the same entity. [C]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $86,048 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $65,175 and total expenses of $70,737, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is local groundwater wells on the Gaviota coast. [2][C] SDWIS classifies the primary source as groundwater; production volume is not reported. [C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: This company files Form 990-EZ, which carries no balance-sheet plant detail, so a net plant age cannot be computed and reads not reported. [990] Physical system detail is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: needs form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross), which Form 990-EZ does not carry
needs form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation), which Form 990-EZ does not carry
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: Form 990 Part X lines 10a and 10b are not both reported for this system, so the ratio is not computable.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (1015.8 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.28 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-02-01 to 2025-01-31), Santa Barbara County was in severe drought or worse 34.9% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Santa Barbara County (FIPS 06083); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2023 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA4200714 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4200714&Year=2023 (3244171 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4200714&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990-EZ Part I line 9 (total revenue)
Form 990-EZ Part I line 17 (total expenses); the excluding variant needs a depreciation line, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Both variants are shown and the displayed variant is labeled (5A).

metrics.name: Days cash on hand
metrics.subtitle: days of operating cost covered by cash and marketable securities
metrics.limitation_note: Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

metrics.reference_source: Rating-agency convention: 200 plus days is strong, under roughly 90 days reads as stress, on unrestricted cash and investments (the State Water Board's SAFER risk indicator uses the same basis: Draft Final White Paper, Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, p. 28). Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.
metrics.formula: (cash, line 1; savings and temporary cash investments, line 2; publicly traded securities, line 11; other securities described as marketable on Schedule D Part VII, line 12) x 365 / (total expenses, line 25, less depreciation, line 22)
source_lines: Form 990-EZ Part II line 22 (cash, savings, and investments); needs a depreciation line, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: This depends on a figure the filing does not give, so we leave it not reported rather than guess.. Lines 1, 2 and 11 are counted as filed; line 12 only where the filer's own Schedule D Part VII description reads as marketable. metrics.subtitle: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: not reported (no comparable years in window)

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: needs Form 990 Part X line 10a in two consecutive years and Part IX line 22, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.
