governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 4 documented, 2 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 19 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The mutual-company form documents that customers are shareholders who elect the directors, so a collective-choice mechanism exists on paper. No record of the specific board, elections, or member votes was found, so the evidence is partial. The specific board is now on the record: the Statement of Information filed 5/12/2026 names 8 directors and 4 officers, transcribed as filed. That closes one of the gaps named above. It does NOT close the others: a filed roster shows who governs, not how members choose them, and carries no election, turnout or member vote. The evidence status therefore stays PARTIAL, because what this principle asks about is member participation and that remains undocumented.
principles.finding: As a mutual it is owned by its customer-shareholders who elect the board, but specific board membership and votes are not documented.
principles.signal: Mutual (501(c)(12)) ownership structure; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0981449, first registered 04/25/1980, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 5/12/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.
principles.signal: SDWIS Primary Water Source Type: groundwater (shared basin).

residual.period_alignment: Both inputs cover the same period: the eAR Section 8b is the fiscal year ending January 31, 2024 and the Form 990 fiscal year 2024 ends January 31, 2024, so the residual is period-aligned.
residual.represents: What it IS: revenue the system booked as program service on its 990 that is not accounted for by the eAR water-rate line, plausibly member assessments and other service revenue.
residual.does_not_represent: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

logic.formula_share: residual $32,705 / 990 program-service revenue $89,148 = 36.69%

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending January 31
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends January 31. A fiscal year therefore shares one of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other eleven with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 97 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 14 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $89,148 (990 program-service revenue) minus $56,443 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $32,705. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A small domestic mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving about 19 service connections and roughly 38 residents in the Hollister Ranch and Gaviota coast area of Santa Barbara County, on coastal terrace and rural ranch terrain. [C][E][2] It is the Gaviota Santa Anita, distinct from the Santa Anita in Los Angeles County. [2]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $81,469 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $89,148 and total expenses of $93,362, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is local groundwater wells on the Gaviota coast. [2][C] SDWIS classifies the primary source as groundwater; production volume is not reported. [C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: This company files Form 990-EZ, which carries no balance-sheet plant detail, so a net plant age cannot be computed and reads not reported. [990] Physical system detail is not reported in a public source.

net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (1239.5 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 6.24 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-02-01 to 2025-01-31), Santa Barbara County was in severe drought or worse 34.9% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Santa Barbara County (FIPS 06083); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds 1 surface water right of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds 1 licensed surface water right of its own
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2023 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA4200678 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4200678&Year=2023 (3414597 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4200678&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

plant_per_acre.logic: Infrastructure built per acre of service area. how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A small private mutual water company (501(c)(12)) serving Montecito shareholders from Hot Springs Canyon, Santa Barbara County, on canyon and foothill terrain at the front of the Santa Ynez Mountains. [1][2] It is distinct from the Montecito Water District and is not a State-regulated public drinking-water system (no PWSID, not in SDWIS). [C][2]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $56,238 in FY2025, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Supply is surface water diverted from Hot Spring Creek in Hot Springs Canyon, under riparian rights held by the company; no wholesale supplier. [2] It is not in the SDWIS drinking-water registry, so a treated public-supply record is not reported. [C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: This company files Form 990-EZ, which carries no balance-sheet plant detail, so a net plant age cannot be computed and reads not reported. [990] Physical system detail is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: needs form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross), which Form 990-EZ does not carry
needs form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation), which Form 990-EZ does not carry
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: Form 990 Part X lines 10a and 10b are not both reported for this system, so the ratio is not computable.

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: One of the oldest water entities in the county, incorporated March 20, 1893 (IRS recognition 1948) as a member mutual supplying Montecito properties from Hot Spring Creek. A detailed founding narrative is not documented. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: Governed by a shareholder board and officers (President Ronald D. Fendon and directors per corporate records). [1] Published bylaws and minutes were not found online.

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: This company has no PWSID and is not in the State Water Board SAFER risk assessment, so a State drinking-water compliance standing is not reported. [C] In a 2019 settlement with Santa Barbara County it paid about $25,000 and agreed to a streambed alteration agreement after diverting Hot Spring Creek water without a Fish and Wildlife permit, with investigators finding broken pipes in the creek. [2] Hot Springs Canyon was among the drainages in the January 2018 Montecito debris flow, though no source documents specific damage to the system. [2]

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: One of the oldest mutuals in California (1893) with a long-held riparian surface-water right on Hot Spring Creek. [1] A small, member-owned system serving Montecito shareholders at cost. [1]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: A very small canyon system exposed to wildfire and post-fire debris flow (the 2018 Montecito event hit its drainage), running a deficit in its latest year. [2][D] A 2019 permit-violation settlement shows regulatory and streambed-management risk on its creek diversion. [2] No drinking-water oversight record (no PWSID) and thin public governance detail. [C]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.absence: No composite is composed for this system. 1 of 3 components could be computed (Drought regime), which is not enough to compose a read over. The components that could not be computed are listed with the reason each one failed; a single reading presented as a composite would claim a completeness this system does not have.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.plain_lead: No service-area boundary is on file for this system, so there is no shape to lay over the fire hazard map. That is a missing outline, not a finding that the system faces no fire risk.
components.reason: No PWSID is recorded for this system, so there is no SABL service-area polygon to intersect with the hazard zone layer. The join is areal and there is no geometry to join with; this is a missing key, not a finding that the system faces no fire hazard.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.value: not reported

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Santa Barbara County was in severe drought or worse 40.9% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Santa Barbara County (FIPS 06083); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 5 documented, 1 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 4,493 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (not verified (sabl)); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set, whether a filed metered rate schedule or a share-and-acreage allocation, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is only partially visible at this scale, but a real cost-to-service rule is on record.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to service under a documented rate or share-based allocation rule reported to the State or set in the company's structure.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; documented rate or share-allocation rule.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents a collective-choice mechanism: customers are shareholders who elect a named board that governs the company. Turnout and specific member votes on major decisions are not documented, but the elected-board structure and its membership are on record.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and run by a named board they elect, documented in its Form 990 governance section.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; named elected board of directors (Form 990).

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the State rates the system Not Failing on its drinking-water risk assessment and the system files an annual eAR. No independent audited financial statement is published, so financial monitoring is weaker, but the operational record is present.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: the State SAFER risk assessment shows it Not Failing, and it files an annual eAR.
principles.signal: SAFER Not Failing; annual eAR reporting; metered connections.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was found for a system this small. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was found. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented: the company is an incorporated mutual recognized by the IRS as a tax-exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a regulated water system. This records the right to organize as a member entity, not a documented instance of exercising it. The California Secretary of State holds the company as a registered corporation, entity number 0025301, first registered 03/26/1896, status as filed "Active", with a governing body named in the Statement of Information filed 2/25/2026. That is a direct state record of the right to organize being recognized, so the evidence behind this status is now a filed corporate record rather than an inference from the company's tax form. The status was already DOCUMENTED and does not move.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS (501(c)(12)) and by the State Water Board as a public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS public water system.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: The system relies on a shared groundwater basin, so it is physically nested in a larger hydrologic system. Its participation in a groundwater sustainability agency or basin governance is not documented, so the nesting evidence is partial.
principles.finding: The system draws on a shared local groundwater basin, embedding it in a larger physical water system, though its role in basin governance is not documented.
principles.signal: SDWIS Primary Water Source Type: groundwater (shared basin).

logic.what_it_is: A DERIVED residual (medium confidence): the part of the Form 990 program-service revenue that is not matched by the eAR water-rate revenue for the same period. Computed by us, not a filed line.

residual.period_alignment: Both inputs cover the same period: the eAR Section 8b is the calendar year 2023 and the Form 990 fiscal year 2023 ends December 31, 2023, so the residual is period-aligned.
residual.represents: What it IS: revenue the system booked as program service on its 990 that is not accounted for by the eAR water-rate line, plausibly member assessments and other service revenue.
residual.does_not_represent: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. The quartiles are never added up, weighted, ranked or turned into a single figure: this is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. A metric this system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place, is named above rather than counted against it.
cohort_position.cohort_note: The cohort is the mutual water companies in this project that file a Form 990 carrying financial data, which is not a sample of California's mutuals. Each metric places only the systems that report it at comparability tier A or B, so the n differs by metric and is stated on every line.

The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 30 survey years, 1994 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 23 of the 30 years, across 3 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 20 of the 27 years, across 5 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 84 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 70 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1994 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: RAYMOND
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Annual Water Master report hydrographs are stable.
Source: http://sgma.water.ca.gov/adjudbasins/report/preview/41  2014-15 RBMB AR.pdf  Pg. 22-23
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A private not-for-profit mutual water company serving about 4,490 service connections and roughly 16,000 residents in western and northwest Altadena, Los Angeles County, in the San Gabriel Mountain foothills and canyons. [C][E][1] Customers are co-owner shareholders and the company operates at cost. [1]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of about $6,225,040 in FY2024, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D] The State Water Board eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reported total revenue of $6,191,765 and total expenses of $6,122,008, on the filer's own self-reported basis. [E] A detailed rate history beyond the filed schedule is not reported.

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Three supplies: local groundwater from the Monk-Hill sub-area of the Raymond Basin (treated for perchlorate and VOCs since 1992), local canyon surface water treated at the South Coulter plant (built 1997), and imported water delivered through Foothill Municipal Water District (a Metropolitan Water District blend of Colorado River and State Water Project supply). [1][2] SDWIS classifies the primary source as surface water. [C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] Detailed infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Roots trace to five Altadena families who formed the Millard Canyon Water Company as citrus groves drove water demand; Lincoln Avenue Water Company acquired the Millard system on March 2, 1896, then added the Pasadena Improvement Company and El Prieto Canyon water rights, drilling its first well in 1913 and building out five wells and eleven reservoirs by the 1970s. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual governed by bylaws and a shareholder board, operating at cost; it publishes Consumer Confidence Reports and detailed post-fire shareholder briefings on its website. [1] Current board and general-manager names were not captured in this pass. [1]

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: State drinking-water compliance standing is shown below from the SAFER risk assessment. [S] The January 2025 Eaton Fire devastated Altadena: roughly 2,600 of the company's ~4,500 connections were damaged or destroyed and about 58 percent of its customer base and revenue was lost; a benzene Do-Not-Drink order was issued in February 2025 after fire-driven pressure loss, bills rose about $15 a month, and the company is exploring a merger with Las Flores Water Company. [3] Earlier, JPL-area contamination discovered in 1984 led to activated-carbon (1992) and perchlorate ion-exchange treatment. [1]

compliance.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as At-Risk, and records the designation as automatic for BOTTLED OR HAULED WATER rather than as a result of its category scores. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-08-27.
compliance.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: By far the largest system in the batch, with three independent supplies (groundwater, local surface, and imported) that reduce single-source risk. [1][2] A deep, well-documented 130-year history and an active, transparent governance record including public post-fire briefings. [1] A demonstrated treatment record on perchlorate and VOCs. [1]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: The 2025 Eaton Fire is a severe, current shock: a majority of connections damaged and roughly 58 percent of revenue lost, a benzene contamination event, a rate increase, and a possible merger, all signs of acute financial and operational stress on a fire-exposed foothill system. [3] Rebuilding demand and revenue while maintaining three supplies and water quality is the central near-term risk. [3]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 48.7% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 48.7% of the service area (823.2 acres), LRA, SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.63 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 44.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells for 77% of its supply, takes 12% from its own surface source and buys 11% from other agencies; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from this system's own 2023 Consumer Confidence Report, which states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: These two records disagree and both are kept as filed. The State Water Board inventory publishes this system's primary source as Surface Water. Its own 2023 Consumer Confidence Report states a mix in which pumps 77% from its own wells, which is the majority of its supply. The band above is built from the report, because the report states figures and the inventory states one code; the code is not corrected, overwritten or removed, and a reader can see both.
components.cross_source_heading: The two records disagree, and both are kept as filed
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910063&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 4 documented, 2 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary here is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried, which is stronger than most of this cohort.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: about 3,128 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 1,337.2 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set: the filer reports metered service, monthly billing, a variable base residential rate structure and a filed rate schedule, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is not visible in the filing and is not claimed here.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to metered use under a filed rate schedule: a variable base residential structure billed monthly and priced per hundred cubic feet.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; metered service; variable base residential rate structure priced per hundred cubic feet.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: customers are shareholders and the company states a five member board governs it. Three gaps keep this at PARTIAL rather than met, and the corporate registration that would close the first is NOT YET CHECKED for this company: the specific board membership, the election procedure, and any record of member votes. A stated board size is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and states that a five member Board of Directors governs it, but the specific board, the election procedure and member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; a five member Board of Directors stated by the company; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing: the system reports metered service and files an annual eAR, its own Consumer Confidence Report states what it pumped, treated and imported for the year, and it holds a dated emergency response plan. The federal SDWIS violation check returned no violation records.
principles.finding: The system is metered and monitored: it files an annual eAR, publishes an annual Consumer Confidence Report that states its supply volumes, and holds a dated emergency response plan.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; metered connections; 2024 Consumer Confidence Report with stated volumes; emergency response plan dated 10/24/2023.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. Unlike the 22 mutuals covered by the 2026-08-21 Secretary of State pull, this status does NOT yet rest on a filed corporate record, because that check has not been run; the tier stands on the tax and drinking-water records alone.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: Physical nesting is documented twice over: the company holds a purchased connection to a regional wholesaler through Foothill MWD and pumps groundwater from a basin it shares with neighbors, and it holds three approved emergency interties with other systems. What is not documented is any governance role in the wholesaler or in a groundwater sustainability agency, so the tier is PARTIAL rather than met.
principles.finding: The system buys imported water through Foothill Municipal Water District, a member agency of the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, and pumps from a shared local groundwater basin, so it sits inside two larger systems; its role in governing either is not documented.
principles.signal: eAR one approved purchased surface water source and three approved emergency interties; Consumer Confidence Report naming Foothill MWD and MWD of Southern California; own groundwater wells.

logic.formula_share: water rate revenue $3,945,052 / total annual revenue (eAR Section 8b B1.8) $3,994,188 = 98.77%
logic.period_treatment: Numerator (eAR Section 8b, the calendar year 2023) and denominator (eAR Section 4 connections reported in the same eAR filing) are both the eAR reporting year 2023, so the two sides are bound to the same reporting year.
logic.rationale: Dividing water-rate revenue by the number of metered service connections gives the average revenue per customer; dividing by total annual revenue shows how much of the system's income comes from water rates.

rate_structure.illustration_note: This block is a rate-schedule illustration at defined usage levels. It is NOT billed revenue and not a claim about any real customer's usage. The revenue side of unit economics is the separate Unit Economics block.

structure.display: Tiered increasing-block with a fixed base, billed monthly, priced per HCF

usage_levels.sentence: Defined single-family usage levels, identical for every company so the bill is comparable: Low = 5 HCF/month (~125 gallons/day); Median = 10 HCF/month (~249 gallons/day); High = 25 HCF/month (~623 gallons/day). 1 HCF = 748 gallons, and 1 thousand gallons = 1,000 gallons. components.name: Equity as a share of assets

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. The quartiles are never added up, weighted, ranked or turned into a single figure: this is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. A metric this system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place, is named above rather than counted against it.
cohort_position.cohort_note: The cohort is the mutual water companies in this project that file a Form 990 carrying financial data, which is not a sample of California's mutuals. Each metric places only the systems that report it at comparability tier A or B, so the n differs by metric and is stated on every line.

denominators.title: System Size and Water Use
denominators.note: System size and water use per fiscal year (the operating denominators that per-customer and per-acre metrics divide by), each cited to file and field. The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

pwss_volume.title: Water volume history (DWR PWSS survey)

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period
calendar_basis.label: Same reporting period. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 1994-2005 form (no untreated-water column in this era)
DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 29 survey years, 1994 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 20 of the 29 years, across 5 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 21 of the 29 years, across 5 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 63 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 61 were left blank. 5 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1994 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
pwss_volume.source: DWR Public Water System Statistics survey, received by email from DWR 2026-08-03; see data/pwss_historical/MANIFEST.md for provenance and data/staging/PWSS__cawc_0027.jsonl for the staged evidence.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: RAYMOND
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Annual Water Master report hydrographs are stable.
Source: http://sgma.water.ca.gov/adjudbasins/report/preview/41  2014-15 RBMB AR.pdf  Pg. 22-23
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

safer_standing.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad
safer_standing.note: Failing, At-Risk, Potentially At-Risk, Not At-Risk and Not Assessed are the State Water Board's own categories and its own determination about this system. They are carried here in the state's words and are not this project's assessment of the company. An automatic designation is made regardless of the category scores beneath it, so a system can be listed At-Risk while scoring NONE or LOW on most categories.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $93,067 (990 program-service revenue) minus $3,945,052 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $-3,851,985. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)

entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A private not-for-profit mutual water company serving the central and eastern portions of Altadena, an unincorporated town in Los Angeles County north of Pasadena. [1] Customers are co-owner shareholders. [1] Three sources count its connections and they do not agree, so all three are carried as filed: SDWIS publishes 3,128 service connections [C], the State Water Board eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 3,136 active and 3,158 total potable connections [E], and the company's own site says more than 3,140 [1]. Population served is reported as 9,600 by both SDWIS and the eAR. [C][E] The State Water Board's field-verified service-area boundary measures about 1,337.2 acres. [G]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $4,989,018 in FY2024 against expenses of $3,333,755, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reports total revenue of $3,994,188 and total expenses of $4,302,719 on the filer's own self-reported basis, while the Form 990 for the same calendar year reports $2,746,190 and $1,933,240. [E][D] Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. The filer left Section 8b blank in reporting year 2024, so there is no eAR revenue figure for that year. [E] Charges are metered and billed monthly on a variable base residential structure priced per hundred cubic feet, and the filer reports the rate increased during reporting year 2024. [E]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: Three channels: groundwater from the company's own wells, local canyon surface water treated at the company's own conventional treatment plant, and imported water bought from Foothill Municipal Water District, a member agency of the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California. [CCR] The eAR reports two approved groundwater sources, three approved surface water sources and one approved purchased surface water source, plus three approved emergency interties. [E] The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report states the year's volumes: 1,696 acre-feet pumped, 194 acre-feet of surface water treated, and no water imported at all that year, which is a filed zero and not a missing figure. [CCR] The same report describes importing as the company's normal practice between November and April; both statements are carried as filed. [CCR] SDWIS classifies the primary source as Surface Water. [C]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] The company states it is continuing to upgrade its infrastructure. [1] A dated infrastructure history is not reported in a public source.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: The company was incorporated in 1886 and has served Altadena since. [1] Earlier history is not reported in a source this project holds.

blocks.body: A member-owned mutual that provides water to its shareholders throughout the service area, governed by a five member Board of Directors. [1] The eAR records the ownership type as a privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 16 Central, with an emergency response plan on file dated 10/24/2023. The corporate registration and board roster are not yet checked. [SOS] Its service area sits in a fire hazard severity zone: the highest class touching it is Very High, with about 19.8 percent of the area in High or Very High. [FH]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 19.8% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 19.8% of the service area (264.7 acres), LRA, SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.35 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 44.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from this system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report, which states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: These two records disagree and both are kept as filed. The State Water Board inventory publishes this system's primary source as Surface Water. Its own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report states a mix in which pumps 89.7% from its own wells, which is the majority of its supply. The band above is built from the report, because the report states figures and the inventory states one code; the code is not corrected, overwritten or removed, and a reader can see both.
components.cross_source_heading: The two records disagree, and both are kept as filed
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910140&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.
