governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 4 documented, 2 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon, so who is inside and outside the system is documented, and SDWIS and the eAR agree on the count exactly. The boundary is Not Verified (SABL), so its outer edge rests on that State layer rather than on a field check.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 1,479 service connections over a State-published service-area boundary of roughly 491.9 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Not Verified (SABL)); connections defined and agreed by two sources.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set: a filed rate schedule with a Uniform Usage residential structure priced per hundred cubic feet, so cost tracks use. The filer did not answer the metering question for reporting year 2024, so whether every connection is metered is not confirmed from that year's filing and is not claimed.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to use under a filed rate schedule: a Uniform Usage residential structure priced per hundred cubic feet, unchanged in the reporting year.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; Uniform Usage residential rate structure priced per hundred cubic feet.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the State records the company as a privately owned mutual, so customers are shareholders. Three gaps keep this at PARTIAL: the specific board membership, the election procedure, and any record of member votes. The corporate registration that would close the first is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, and no company website was found that would document the rest.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and files a Form 990 governance section, but the specific board, the election procedure and member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership (eAR ownership type); Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented: the system files an annual eAR, published a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 that was located and downloaded, and holds a dated emergency response plan. That the report carries no text layer is a limit on what this project can read out of it, not evidence that the monitoring is absent.
principles.finding: The system files an annual eAR, publishes an annual Consumer Confidence Report, and holds a dated emergency response plan.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting including a complete Section 8b for reporting year 2023; 2024 Consumer Confidence Report located; emergency response plan dated 6/15/2022.

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a graduated shut-off or penalty policy was located, and no company website was found that might publish one. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced sanctions policy.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a member dispute or conflict-resolution procedure was located, and no company website was found that might publish one. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. Unlike the 22 mutuals covered by the 2026-08-21 Secretary of State pull, this status does NOT yet rest on a filed corporate record, because that check has not been run.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: Physical nesting is documented as clearly as anywhere in this cohort: the company reports no source of its own and one purchased connection, so the larger system is not merely one of its supplies, it is its supply. What is not documented is any governance role in the wholesaler, so the tier is PARTIAL rather than met.
principles.finding: The system buys effectively all of its water through Foothill Municipal Water District, which makes it deeply nested in a larger supply system; its role in governing that system is not documented.
principles.signal: eAR zero approved groundwater and zero approved surface water sources of its own, one approved purchased surface water source (Foothill MWD treated connection), one approved emergency intertie; SDWIS primary source Surface Water Purchased.

anomalies.title: FY2024 net assets do not sum to the lines we extract
anomalies.flag_reason: Flagged because the lines we extracted do not sum to the total reported on the filing: the ending net assets on the form do not equal the beginning net assets plus the year's surplus or deficit plus the other changes we read. This may indicate a line on the form that we did not map, rather than an error by the company. The figure is shown exactly as filed, and the difference is noted, not corrected.

what.text: FY2024 net assets are carried exactly as filed at $2,772,106. The lines we extracted do not sum to that total: the ending net assets it reports (Form 990 Part XI line 10) should equal the beginning net assets (line 4) plus revenue less expenses (line 3) plus other changes (lines 5-9), which computes to $2,428,313 (a difference of $343,793 against the $2,772,106 on the form). This may mean a line on the form that we do not yet read, rather than an error by the company. The filed figure is kept and the difference is flagged, not reconciled.
source_lines: Net assets, end of year (as filed): $2,772,106 (Form 990 Part XI line 10 / Part X line 32 (net assets, end of year))
Net assets, end of year (recomputed from the lines we extract): $2,428,313
Difference (as filed less our computed sum): $343,793
what.confidence_reason: The net-assets figure is a direct filed line item, carried exactly as filed; confidence is held to medium (not high) because the lines we extract do not sum to the total on the form, so the figure is flagged rather than presented as clean. That can mean a line we do not read as easily as an inconsistency in the filing, and this project has found the former three times. Nothing is reconciled.

why.text: The filing does not state a reason.
why.guess: Possible explanation, not stated in filing: an ending net-worth figure that does not equal the beginning balance plus the year's surplus or deficit usually reflects a prior-year adjustment, a reclassification between balance-sheet lines, or a rounding or transcription difference on the filed form. This is an educated guess, not something the filing actually says.

rate_structure.title: Rate structure and representative bill
rate_structure.illustration_note: This block is a rate-schedule illustration at defined usage levels. It is NOT billed revenue and not a claim about any real customer's usage. The revenue side of unit economics is the separate Unit Economics block.

structure.display: Uniform: fixed base plus a single volumetric rate, billed monthly, priced per HCF

usage_levels.sentence: Defined single-family usage levels, identical for every company so the bill is comparable: Low = 5 HCF/month (~125 gallons/day); Median = 10 HCF/month (~249 gallons/day); High = 25 HCF/month (~623 gallons/day). 1 HCF = 748 gallons, and 1 thousand gallons = 1,000 gallons. The usage is converted into the company's own filed unit before the filed tiers are applied, and the bill is stated as a monthly equivalent: a bimonthly structure is computed at twice the monthly usage and divided by two, and any other billing period the same way with its factor stated. These are an illustration, not a measured usage for any real customer.

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

pwss_volume.title: Water volume history (DWR PWSS survey)

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period
calendar_basis.label: Same reporting period. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 11 of the 12 years, from 1 customer class.
coverage.tail: Separately, 94 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 14 were left blank. 8 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
pwss_volume.source: DWR Public Water System Statistics survey, received by email from DWR 2026-08-03; see data/pwss_historical/MANIFEST.md for provenance and data/staging/PWSS__cawc_0028.jsonl for the staged evidence.

water_rights.reason: Searched the state water rights list by owner name on 2026-08-27 and found no record. This is the expected result for a system supplied by groundwater or purchased water, and it is a finished state: the source was read and it holds nothing for this company, which is not the same as not having looked.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: RAYMOND
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2023, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

entries.found: A period-aligned residual cannot be computed for this filer, so the metric is rendered IMPOSSIBLE rather than guessed.
entries.note: Not derivable. The eAR Section 8b is the calendar year 2023 while the Form 990 fiscal year ends December 31, 2023; the two period ends are not aligned, so a period-aligned residual cannot be computed.

State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)

Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A private not-for-profit mutual water company serving Altadena, an unincorporated town in Los Angeles County. [C][E] SDWIS and the State Water Board eAR agree on its size: 1,479 active service connections and a population of 4,847. [C][E] The eAR breaks those connections down as 1,469 single family, 6 multi family, 2 commercial or institutional and 2 landscape irrigation, so it is an almost entirely residential system. [E] Its State-published service-area boundary measures about 491.9 acres, the smallest area of the three Altadena mutuals; the Water Board has NOT field-verified that polygon. [G] The company's principal address is on the same Altadena street as Rubio Canon's. [E] Customers are co-owner shareholders; the eAR records the ownership type as a privately owned mutual water company or association. [E]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $1,804,118 in FY2024 against expenses of $2,629,920. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2023 reports total revenue of $1,734,238 and total expenses of $1,006,100 on the filer's own self-reported basis, while the Form 990 for the same calendar year reports $686,016 and $647,062. [E][D] Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. The filer left Section 8b blank in reporting year 2024, so there is no eAR revenue figure for that year, and it did not report a metering or billing frequency answer for that year either. [E] The filed residential rate structure is Uniform Usage priced per hundred cubic feet, and the filer reports the rate did not change during reporting year 2024. [E] THE FY2024 FORM 990 CARRIES AN AS-FILED ANOMALY: the Part XI reconciliation does not foot, by $343,793. It is carried exactly as filed, flagged, and not adjusted; the FY2024 figures are held at medium confidence for that reason. [990]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: This system buys essentially all of its water rather than producing it. The eAR reports ZERO approved groundwater sources and ZERO approved surface water sources of its own, against one approved purchased surface water source and one approved emergency intertie; the named purchased connection is a treated supply from Foothill Municipal Water District. [E] SDWIS classifies the primary source as Surface Water Purchased, which agrees. [C] A 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and downloaded from the State Water Board viewer, but it is published as page images with no text layer; this project does not run optical character recognition, so no supply figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. [CCR] The system holds no surface water right of its own in the State Water Board eWRIMS record, which is the expected state for a system that buys its water.

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age (accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant) is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] A dated infrastructure history is not reported in a public source this project holds.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

No company website was found for this system and no dated founding or incorporation record is held: the California Secretary of State registration, which would carry the initial filing date, is NOT YET CHECKED because that source is reachable only through a browser session with an operator present. [SOS] The IRS holds the company as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer, but a tax recognition date is not a founding date and the two are not collapsed here. [990]

blocks.body: A member-owned mutual; the eAR records the ownership type as a privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 16 Central, with an emergency response plan on file dated 6/15/2022. [E] Officer and director information filed on the Form 990 governance section is captured in the filings, but the California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company, so no board roster is shown rather than one being assembled from elsewhere. blocks.body: State drinking-water compliance standing is shown below from the SAFER risk assessment. [S] The US EPA SDWIS check returned TWO violation records for this system, both non health based and both flagged major, with compliance periods beginning 2010-07-01 and 2014-07-10 and no recorded end date; no enforcement action is linked to either. [C] The records are shown as EPA holds them and nothing is inferred about their current status. blocks.body: An almost entirely residential customer base of 1,469 single family connections out of 1,479, so demand is not concentrated in a few large accounts. [E] SDWIS and the eAR agree exactly on both connection count and population, which is not true of every system in this cohort. blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: The FY2024 Form 990 does not foot on Part XI, by $343,793, and is carried at medium confidence for that reason. [990] The eAR Section 8b figures for reporting year 2023 and the Form 990 for the same calendar year differ substantially in both revenue and expenses, and Section 8b is blank for reporting year 2024. [E][D] The system reports no approved groundwater or surface water source of its own and one purchased connection, so its supply rests on a single external channel with one emergency intertie behind it. [E] Its Consumer Confidence Report is published as page images, so its supply mix cannot be read without optical character recognition. [CCR] Its service-area boundary is carried by the Water Board but NOT field-verified, so every areal figure computed over it is held at low join confidence. [G] The corporate registration and board roster are not yet checked. [SOS] The highest fire hazard class touching its service area is Very High, with about 19.0 percent of the area in High or Very High. [FH]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 19.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 19.0% of the service area (93.4 acres), LRA, SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.98 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 44.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Buys treated water from other agencies; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.value: Surface Water Purchased (purchased treated surface water)
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1910061 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910061&Year=2024 (1329742 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910061&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 2 documented, 2 partial, 4 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending June 30
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends June 30. A fiscal year therefore shares six of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other six with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 4 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 83 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 12 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA1910199. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.
Returned 1 link row(s) for PWSID CA1910199, naming 1 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 9399991.

gap_evidence.status_line: 1 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 9399991. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A private not-for-profit mutual water company incorporated in 1902, which sells water only to its shareholders at or near cost. [1] It describes itself as functioning largely as a WHOLESALE water provider, with three majority wholesale shareholders (Suburban Water Systems, the City of La Habra and the City of Brea) and roughly 160 residential retail properties remaining as shareholders. [1] Its system begins in Los Angeles County and ends in north Orange County, crossing El Monte, Industry, Whittier, La Habra, La Habra Heights and Brea. [1] The State's own count is a different kind of number and the two are carried side by side rather than reconciled: SDWIS publishes 21 service connections against a served population of 290,814, and the eAR Section 4 open data for reporting year 2022 independently reports the same 21 active potable connections. [C][E] A connection count of that size against a population of that size is an as-filed extreme, flagged and not explained away.

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $15,414,997 in FY2024 against expenses of $15,937,555, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR carries no Section 8b revenue figure for this company, so there is no second filed revenue basis to compare against. [E]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: The company reports securing regional water in the Main San Gabriel Basin, with supply originating from local groundwater wells rather than imported sources. [1] SDWIS classifies the primary source as Groundwater. [C] It reports annual production of 20,000 to 25,000 acre-feet. [1] The DWR Public Water System Statistics survey carries 12 years of filed volume history for this system. [P]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: The company records County franchises dating to 1912 and describes acquiring land, wells, equipment, flumes, ditches and rights-of-way from its predecessor. [1] A dated capital-improvement schedule is not reported in a source this project holds.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Water service in the area began in 1889 when Simon J. Murphy founded the East Whittier Land and Water Company. California Domestic was incorporated in 1902 when George Chaffey purchased water rights from that company; Chaffey managed it and later joined the Board of Directors. The offices moved from Los Angeles to Whittier in 1907. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds. [990] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company. [SOS]

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Not Assessed. [S] The US EPA SDWIS check could not be trusted for this system: the federal VIOLATION table returned no rows while VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC referenced violation ids for the same system, so EPA's own tables disagree and this system cannot be reported as clean. The disagreement is recorded and not reconciled. [C] A Consumer Confidence Report for 2022 was located at the State Water Board's CCR portal; no supply-mix figure has been transcribed from it, which is a hand-transcription step and not an automated one. [CCR] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company: that source is reachable only through a browser session with an operator present and it now answers a persistent CAPTCHA, so nothing is recorded rather than guessed. [SOS]

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: It sits on the Main San Gabriel Basin and reports supply from its own wells rather than purchased imports, so its principal channel is one it owns. [1] It is the largest company in this batch by total assets and carries the deepest filed revenue base. [D] Its service connections are independently counted the same by two State publications, SDWIS and the eAR Section 4 open data, which is a corroboration most of this cohort does not have. [C][E]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Two things a reader should not skip. First, the State publishes no SAFER risk determination for this system at all: it reads Not Assessed, which is neither a clean bill nor a finding. [S] Second, no State Water Board SABL service-area polygon was matched, so there is no boundary to lay over the fire hazard map and no acreage, and the fire hazard check is therefore not_matched rather than a finding of no risk. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Drought regime, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Fire hazard, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.plain_lead: No service-area boundary is on file for this system, so there is no shape to lay over the fire hazard map. That is a missing outline, not a finding that the system faces no fire risk.
components.reason: SABL holds no service-area polygon for PWSID CA1910199, so there is no geometry to intersect with the hazard zone layer.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.value: not reported

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-07-01 to 2024-06-30), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 55.3% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and its groundwater basin placement is not on record.

detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.value: No groundwater basin placement is recorded
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2022 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1910199 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910199&Year=2022 (1448187 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910199&Year=2022
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 3 documented, 3 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: Membership is documented as a fixed set of service connections, so the social boundary is clear. The physical boundary is published but carries the State's Not Verified flag, so it is drawn dashed and every figure derived from its acreage is held at lower confidence.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system with 11,448 service connections and a State-published service area of roughly 19,161.9 acres, but the State Water Board has NOT verified that boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Not Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set: the filer reports metered service, a billing frequency, a residential rate structure and a filed rate schedule, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is not visible in the filing and is not claimed here.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to metered use under a filed rate schedule: a variable base residential structure billed m and priced per hundred cubic feet.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; metered service; Variable Base residential rate structure.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its shareholders and publishes the time and place of its regular monthly board meeting.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; published monthly board meeting; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and it reports metered service, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State's own CCR portal, and it holds an emergency response plan dated 7/1/2024.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; metered connections; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced graduated sanctions record.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: Physical nesting is documented. What is not documented is any governance role in a wholesaler or in a groundwater sustainability agency, so the tier is PARTIAL rather than met.
principles.finding: The system sits inside larger water systems: it pumps from 1 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors. Its role in governing any of them is not documented.
principles.signal: it pumps from 1 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors

residual.period_alignment: Both inputs cover the same period: the eAR Section 8b is the calendar year 2024 and the Form 990 fiscal year 2024 ends December 31, 2024, so the residual is period-aligned.

member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 31 survey years, 1994 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 23 of the 31 years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 23 of the 31 years, across 7 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 78 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 73 were left blank. 6 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1994 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

sdwis_compliance.title: Drinking-water compliance (US EPA SDWIS)
sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

Returned 14 link row(s) for PWSID CA1510029, naming 5 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 812005, 9212001, 9312002, 9312003, 9312004.

gap_evidence.status_line: 5 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 812005, 9212001, 9312002, 9312003, 9312004. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.
gap_evidence.source: US EPA Envirofacts SDWIS, https://data.epa.gov/efservice, tables VIOLATION and VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC, queried with the BEGINNING operator on the full PWSID. Retrieved 2026-09-23.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2024, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $11,206,435 (990 program-service revenue) minus $10,997,261 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $209,174. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)

Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company serving the Rosedale area of northwest Bakersfield since 1928. [1] Three counts of its size are on the record and they do not agree, so all three are carried: the company states it grew from 3 connections in 1928 to over 9,300 in 2010 and elsewhere reports 11,361 [1], SDWIS publishes 11,448 service connections and a population of 37,075 [C], and the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 11,448 active service connections. [E]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $12,086,327 in FY2024 against expenses of $11,046,499, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $11,028,563 and total expenses of $13,091,174. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D] Charges are metered and billed m on a variable base residential structure priced per hundred cubic feet. [E]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: The company states that all of its supply comes from groundwater and usually requires some form of treatment, operating twelve wells of which nine carry specialised treatment systems. [1] SDWIS records the primary source as Groundwater. [C] The eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 13 approved groundwater sources, 0 approved surface water sources and 0 approved purchased surface water sources. [E] The DWR survey carries 31 years of filed volume history, the deepest run in this batch. [P]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] The company describes nine of its twelve wells as carrying treatment systems, which is a statement about equipment rather than a dated schedule. [1] No dated capital plan is reported in a source this project holds.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

The company is owned by its shareholders and publishes the time and place of its regular monthly board meeting. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Kern County was in severe drought or worse 44.4% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Kern County (FIPS 06029); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and the ground beneath it is in critical overdraft, which is the state's finding that the basin is pumped faster than it refills.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by SAN JOAQUIN VALLEY - KERN COUNTY (5-022.14) in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

detail.label: Basin placement confidence
detail.value: The basin placement is an areal join and is carried at low; it is never better than the service-area boundary it rests on.
detail.source: BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1510029 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1510029&Year=2024 (599325 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1510029&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)
Form 990 Part IX line 25 (total functional expenses)
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation), subtracted for the excluding variant

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 3 documented, 2 partial, 3 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 3,957 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 1,188.2 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: This company files no eAR, so the filing that would document metering and rate structure does not exist for it. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No filed rate schedule or metering statement was located for this company.
principles.signal: No eAR Section 8a rate record held.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State's own CCR portal, and it holds an emergency response plan dated 8/18/2022.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced graduated sanctions record.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: Physical nesting is documented. What is not documented is any governance role in a wholesaler or in a groundwater sustainability agency, so the tier is PARTIAL rather than met.
principles.finding: The system sits inside larger water systems: it pumps from 1 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors, and it holds 9 approved emergency intertie(s) with other systems. Its role in governing any of them is not documented.
principles.signal: it pumps from 1 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors; it holds 9 approved emergency intertie(s) with other systems

The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending June 30
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends June 30. A fiscal year therefore shares six of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other six with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 1994-2005 form (no untreated-water column in this era)
DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 31 survey years, 1994 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 21 of the 31 years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 12 of the 21 years, across 7 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 61 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 76 were left blank. 1 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1994 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
