basins.name: COASTAL PLAIN OF LOS ANGELES - CENTRAL
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment:

Source: 4-011.04_7a_Hydrographs_CoastalPlainCentral.pdf 
Examples:
02S12W24M008S (45+ ft of decline)
02S12W10Q008S (60+ ft of decline)
03S11W17F002S (40+ ft of decline)
03S12W09J002S (30+ ft of decline)

2) CBMWD is moving forward with a groundwater storage plan because there are threats to the integrity of the Central Groundwater Basin. Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2024, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $6,786,362 (990 program-service revenue) minus $6,662,418 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $123,944. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company serving Montebello, operating since 1900 and describing itself as Montebello Land and Water Mutual Water Company. [1] SDWIS publishes 3,957 service connections and a population of 26,554; the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 3,956 active service connections. [C][E] The State publishes the name as MONTEBELLO LAND & WATER CO. while the Form 990 filer block reads MONTEBELLO LAND AND WATER COMPANY; the filed name is canonical here and the State string is preserved. [C][990]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $10,411,332 in FY2024 against expenses of $4,760,974, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $6,715,191 and total expenses of $6,140,569. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: SDWIS records the primary source as Groundwater. [C] The eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 7 approved groundwater sources, 0 approved surface water sources and 0 approved purchased surface water sources. [E] The DWR survey carries 31 years of filed volume history. [P]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] A dated infrastructure history is not reported in a public source this project holds.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Montebello began in May 1899 from the Newmark and Cohn shares of a 1,200 acre purchase. The area was named Montebello at the suggestion of William Mulholland, who developed the water system and had it incorporated as the Montebello Land and Water Company in 1900. [2] The company's own site carries the date 1900. [1]

blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds. [990] The eAR records the ownership type as privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 16 - Central, with an emergency response plan on file dated 8/18/2022. [E] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company. [SOS]

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: The State Water Board has FIELD-VERIFIED its service-area boundary, which most of this cohort's mutuals do not have. [G][FH] Its filed revenue more than doubled between FY2021 and FY2024 while expenses stayed close to flat, so its filed margin is the widest in this batch. [D] It sits in a single adjudicated groundwater basin rather than straddling several. [SG]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Its Part XI reconciliation does not foot in any of the four years held, by amounts between about 25 thousand and about 180 thousand dollars, in both directions. [990] Every year is carried exactly as filed and every year is stamped medium confidence for that reason; nothing is adjusted toward anything. FY2020 is absent because the IRS efile index carries no return for tax period 202006, so this company holds four years and not five. [990]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-07-01 to 2024-06-30), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 55.3% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1910091 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910091&Year=2024 (481729 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910091&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation

metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: cumulative over 5 comparable years (FY2021-25)

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment at cost), year over year
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation)
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

A fiscal year therefore shares six of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other six with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The count is from eAR reporting year 2024, 181 days before the fiscal year end.

reference.label: revenue per connection lagging expense growth is the pattern cost-of-service rate-setting aims to prevent

metrics.reference_source: Interpretive context only. Rate discipline is a trend display, not a threshold metric; no pass/fail grade and no graded external benchmark.
metrics.logic: Whether rates are keeping pace with cost over time: the multi-year trajectory of revenue per connection set beside the growth in operating expense per connection.
metrics.formula: revenue per connection and operating expense per connection, each year divided by that year's own paired count; both series indexed to 100 at the window start on total revenue and total expense, so the count does not enter the index
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue) and Part IX line 25 (total expenses)

connection denominator: State Water Board eAR Section 4 active service connections (CurTotalConnections), each fiscal year paired with the reporting year closest to its fiscal year end within 366 days
metrics.confidence_reason: The revenue and expense inputs are filed line items and every per-connection figure names the count it divides by, with that count's source, reporting year and any gap from the fiscal year end (high confidence count). The trend is shown with no overall grade.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 3 documented, 2 partial, 3 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 6,996 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 2,376.7 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: This company files no eAR, so the filing that would document metering and rate structure does not exist for it. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No filed rate schedule or metering statement was located for this company.
principles.signal: No eAR Section 8a rate record held.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its stockholders, and its shares are attached to the land at one share per acre rather than being owned separately, a rule it traces to its 1911 founding.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; shares attached to land at one share per acre; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State's own CCR portal, and it holds an emergency response plan dated 3/1/2022.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced graduated sanctions record.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: Physical nesting is documented. What is not documented is any governance role in a wholesaler or in a groundwater sustainability agency, so the tier is PARTIAL rather than met.
principles.finding: The system sits inside larger water systems: it holds 1 approved purchased surface water connection(s) to a wholesaler, and it pumps from 1 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors. Its role in governing any of them is not documented.
principles.signal: it holds 1 approved purchased surface water connection(s) to a wholesaler; it pumps from 1 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors

unit_economics.title: Unit economics
unit_economics.basis_note: Every metric here is PER CUSTOMER (a metered service connection). It is not a per-member figure; the member (shareholder) count is a different denominator, shown in the denominator block. The visible cell shows the value and its classification; the numerator, denominator, formula, and rationale are in each metric's LOGIC popup.

unit_economics.primary_source: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue by rate/fee), reporting year 2024

logic.what_it_is: Revenue customers paid for water service, read straight off the filed eAR Section 8b water-rate line. A DIRECT filed figure, not computed by us.

logic.formula_per_customer: water rate revenue $9,640,849 / 6,996 connections = $1,378.05 per connection
logic.formula_share: water rate revenue $9,640,849 / total annual revenue (eAR Section 8b B1.8) $11,097,935 = 86.87%
logic.period_treatment: Numerator (eAR Section 8b, the fiscal year ending June 30, 2025) and denominator (eAR Section 4 connections reported in the same eAR filing) are both the eAR reporting year 2024, so the two sides are bound to the same reporting year.
logic.rationale: Dividing water-rate revenue by the number of metered service connections gives the average revenue per customer; dividing by total annual revenue shows how much of the system's income comes from water rates.

metrics.name: Assessment revenue (990 program-service revenue not matched to eAR water-rate revenue)

logic.what_it_is: A DERIVED residual (medium confidence): the part of the Form 990 program-service revenue that is not matched by the eAR water-rate revenue for the same period. Computed by us, not a filed line.

input_a.name: Form 990 program-service revenue
input_a.source: Form 990 Part VIII line 2 (total program-service revenue), fiscal year 2025 ending June 30, 2025

input_b.name: eAR water-rate revenue
input_b.source: State Water Board eAR Section 8b, question B1.1 + B1.2 (revenue from water rates), reporting year 2024

residual.period_alignment: Both inputs cover the same period: the eAR Section 8b is the fiscal year ending June 30, 2025 and the Form 990 fiscal year 2025 ends June 30, 2025, so the residual is period-aligned.
residual.represents: What it IS: revenue the system booked as program service on its 990 that is not accounted for by the eAR water-rate line, plausibly member assessments and other service revenue.
residual.does_not_represent: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

logic.formula_per_customer: residual $1,485,029 / 6,996 connections = $212.27 per connection
logic.formula_share: residual $1,485,029 / 990 program-service revenue $11,125,878 = 13.35%

rate_structure.title: Rate structure and representative bill
rate_structure.illustration_note: This block is a rate-schedule illustration at defined usage levels. It is NOT billed revenue and not a claim about any real customer's usage. The revenue side of unit economics is the separate Unit Economics block.

structure.display: Tiered increasing-block with a fixed base, billed bimonthly, priced per HCF

usage_levels.sentence: Defined single-family usage levels, identical for every company so the bill is comparable: Low = 5 HCF/month (~125 gallons/day); Median = 10 HCF/month (~249 gallons/day); High = 25 HCF/month (~623 gallons/day). 1 HCF = 748 gallons, and 1 thousand gallons = 1,000 gallons. The usage is converted into the company's own filed unit before the filed tiers are applied, and the bill is stated as a monthly equivalent: a bimonthly structure is computed at twice the monthly usage and divided by two, and any other billing period the same way with its factor stated. These are an illustration, not a measured usage for any real customer.

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending June 30
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends June 30. A fiscal year therefore shares six of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other six with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 1994-2005 form (no untreated-water column in this era)
DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 31 survey years, 1994 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 23 of the 31 years, across 5 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 15 of the 24 years, across 9 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 54 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 94 were left blank. 1 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1994 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
pwss_volume.source: DWR Public Water System Statistics survey, received by email from DWR 2026-08-03; see data/pwss_historical/MANIFEST.md for provenance and data/staging/PWSS__cawc_0032.jsonl for the staged evidence.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: COASTAL PLAIN OF LOS ANGELES - CENTRAL
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) CASGEM/WDL/GWIDS: Long term hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 4-011.04_7a_Hydrographs_CoastalPlainCentral.pdf 
Examples:
02S12W24M008S (45+ ft of decline)
02S12W10Q008S (60+ ft of decline)
03S11W17F002S (40+ ft of decline)
03S12W09J002S (30+ ft of decline)

2) CBMWD is moving forward with a groundwater storage plan because there are threats to the integrity of the Central Groundwater Basin. Namely, the Water Replenishment District (WRD) the agency with the singular responsibility of replenishing the groundwater basin has failed to do its job, allowing the groundwater table to decline, and allowing portions of the basin to fall to very low levels. 
Source: 4-011.04_7a_CentralBasinGWStoragePlanFAQ.pdf
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: not recorded. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.
sgma_basin.source: CA DWR Bulletin 118 groundwater basins and SGMA Basin Prioritization, https://gis.water.ca.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Geoscientific/i08_B118_CA_GroundwaterBasins/MapServer/0/query Retrieved 2026-08-27.

violations.violation_name: Follow-up Or Routine LCR Tap M/R

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

safer_standing.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Potentially At-Risk. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-08-27.

comparable.state_basis: State Water Board definition: unrestricted cash and investments divided by per-day operating expenses excluding depreciation (Draft Final White Paper, July 16, 2020, p. 28). The Hydronomics headline uses the same basis as far as Form 990 allows. The state publishes a risk level and a threshold result, not a figure, and the file does not state which assessment year it reflects.
comparable.state_definition_source: State Water Resources Control Board, Draft Final White Paper Discussion On: Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, pp. 27 and 28
comparable.ours_basis: Computed by this project from the filed financial statements, on the basis set out in the anchor-metrics framework.
comparable.comparison_note: Two readings of the same indicator from two different bases. They are shown side by side and are deliberately NOT combined: the state's is a threshold test whose definition this project does not hold, and this project's is a computed figure. Neither is used to check or correct the other.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2024, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $11,125,878 (990 program-service revenue) minus $9,640,849 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $1,485,029. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company formed from two 1911 predecessors and owned by its stockholders, whose shares are attached to the land at one share per acre rather than held separately. [1] SDWIS publishes 6,996 service connections and a population of 46,300; the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 6,996 active service connections. [C][E] The State publishes the name as BELLFLOWER - SOMERSET MWC while the Form 990 filer block reads BELLFLOWER SOMERSET MUTUAL WATER COMPANY. [C][990]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $11,030,604 in FY2024 against expenses of $7,826,601, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $11,097,935 and total expenses of $11,791,476. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: SDWIS records the primary source as Surface Water Purchased, so this system buys treated surface water rather than pumping its principal supply. [C] The eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 5 approved groundwater sources, 0 approved surface water sources and 1 approved purchased surface water sources. [E] The DWR survey carries 31 years of filed volume history. [P]

net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Two mutual water companies were formed in 1911: Somerset Mutual Water Company in July and Bellflower Mutual Water Company in December. Emil Firth, one of the founders of Bellflower, proposed a mutual owned by the property owners themselves and donated wells and facilities to establish Somerset, on the condition that shares could not be owned separately but would attach to the land at one share per acre; F. E. Woodruff followed with Bellflower Mutual. [1] The two later combined into the present company. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company is owned by its stockholders, and its shares are attached to the land at one share per acre rather than being owned separately, a rule it traces to its 1911 founding. [990] The eAR records the ownership type as privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 07 - Hollywood, with an emergency response plan on file dated 3/1/2022. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2019-07-01 to 2025-06-30), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 44.7% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Buys treated water from other agencies; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.value: Surface Water Purchased (purchased treated surface water)
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1910013 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910013&Year=2024 (641534 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910013&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 3 documented, 2 partial, 3 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 6,326 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 1,853.5 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: This company files no eAR, so the filing that would document metering and rate structure does not exist for it. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No filed rate schedule or metering statement was located for this company.
principles.signal: No eAR Section 8a rate record held.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2022 was located at the State's own CCR portal.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.

components.name: Equity as a share of assets

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. The quartiles are never added up, weighted, ranked or turned into a single figure: this is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. A metric this system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place, is named above rather than counted against it.
cohort_position.cohort_note: The cohort is the mutual water companies in this project that file a Form 990 carrying financial data, which is not a sample of California's mutuals. Each metric places only the systems that report it at comparability tier A or B, so the n differs by metric and is stated on every line.

denominators.title: System Size and Water Use
denominators.note: System size and water use per fiscal year (the operating denominators that per-customer and per-acre metrics divide by), each cited to file and field. The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. Point-in-time counts (connections, population) are matched to the closest eAR year and never summed. Every derived figure states its formula and accounting rationale.
denominators.monthly_source: California open-data portal (data.ca.gov): the separate Produced Water (by month and source) and Delivered Water (by month and connection type) resources, which cover every public water system (not only urban suppliers), one resource per reporting year, matched by exact PWSID. member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period

The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. eras.label: DWR PWSS, 1994-2005 form (no untreated-water column in this era)
DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 28 survey years, 1994 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 21 of the 28 years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 17 of the 21 years, across 6 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 137 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 37 were left blank. 2 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1994 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
pwss_volume.source: DWR Public Water System Statistics survey, received by email from DWR 2026-08-03; see data/pwss_historical/MANIFEST.md for provenance and data/staging/PWSS__cawc_0033.jsonl for the staged evidence.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

plant_per_acre.title: Plant assets per acre
plant_per_acre.acres_source: Geodesic area (WGS84 spherical excess) of the SABL service-area polygon.
plant_per_acre.logic: Infrastructure built per acre of service area. Gross plant per acre is the primary read because it measures how much plant the system has put in the ground per acre, and unlike net plant it does not fall over time purely because the assets depreciate on the books. Net plant per acre is shown alongside as the depreciated book value per acre.
plant_per_acre.formula: gross plant per acre = Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment, gross) / SABL service-area acres; net plant per acre uses Part X line 10c (net)
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (gross) and line 10c (net)
Geodesic area (WGS84 spherical excess) of the SABL service-area polygon.
plant_per_acre.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Filed gross/net plant over the measured SABL service-area acreage.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year None, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

entries.found: A period-aligned residual cannot be computed for this filer, so the metric is rendered IMPOSSIBLE rather than guessed.

State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)

Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A private mutual water company incorporated in 1895 in an unincorporated area of Los Angeles County in the eastern portion of Pasadena, supplying water at cost to its stockholders. [1][2] SDWIS publishes 6,326 service connections and a population of 25,252; the eAR Section 4 open data for reporting year 2022 reports 6,337 active potable connections. [C][E]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $7,117,630 in FY2024 against expenses of $5,197,001, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR carries no Section 8b revenue figure for this company, so there is no second filed revenue basis to compare against. [E]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: The company states it relies on 100 percent groundwater, pumped from the Raymond Basin and the Main San Gabriel Basin. [1] SDWIS records the primary source as Groundwater. [C] Sitting across two basins is visible in the State record too: the SGMA check matches this system to 2 groundwater basins. [SG] The DWR survey carries 28 years of filed volume history. [P]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] The company has publicly described deploying advanced nitrate removal treatment. [2] No dated capital schedule is reported in a source this project holds.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: Leonard J. Rose named his ranch Sunny Slope Farm, irrigated from artesian wells; by 1895 there were twenty-two wells producing roughly 2,200 acre-feet a year, and in that year the Sunny Slope Water Company was organized to take over the system and serve water to other ranchers. [2] A 1934 California Supreme Court opinion records the company as engaged since 1895 in owning, developing and acquiring water, water rights and waterworks and distributing water at cost to its stockholders across some 2,282 acres. [2]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds. [990] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company. [SOS]

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Not At-Risk. [S] The US EPA SDWIS violation and enforcement check returned no violation records for this system. [C] A Consumer Confidence Report for 2022 was located at the State Water Board's CCR portal; no supply-mix figure has been transcribed from it, which is a hand-transcription step and not an automated one. [CCR] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company: that source is reachable only through a browser session with an operator present and it now answers a persistent CAPTCHA, so nothing is recorded rather than guessed. [SOS]

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: It draws on two separate groundwater basins rather than one, which the State's own basin match confirms. [SG] The State Water Board has FIELD-VERIFIED its service-area boundary. [G][FH] The federal SDWIS violation and enforcement check returned no violation records for this system. [C] Its service area carries no elevated fire hazard on the CAL FIRE layer. [FH]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: Its Part XI reconciliation does not foot in any of the five years held, by amounts from about 167 thousand to about 1.8 million dollars, in both directions. [990] Every year is carried exactly as filed and stamped medium confidence for that reason. Separately, the bulk eAR section files carry no rows for this PWSID in reporting years 2023 or 2024 while the data.ca.gov Section 4 open-data resource does list the system, so two State publications of the same filing disagree; both are recorded. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 44.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 2 designated basins, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2022 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1910157 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910157&Year=2022 (523166 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910157&Year=2022
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.

metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: cumulative over 4 comparable years (FY2021-24), excludes 1 not-reported year

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 4 documented, 2 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 1,681 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 1,788.6 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set: the filer reports metered service, a billing frequency, a residential rate structure and a filed rate schedule, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is not visible in the filing and is not claimed here.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to metered use under a filed rate schedule: a variable base residential structure billed m and priced per hundred cubic feet.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; metered service; Variable Base residential rate structure.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and states that a seven member Board of Directors governs it, and that every property owner in the service area is a stockholder including the directors, a requirement it says is written into its By-laws.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; seven member Board of Directors stated by the company; By-laws requirement that directors be shareholders; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and it reports metered service, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2023 was located at the State's own CCR portal, and it holds an emergency response plan dated 12/27/2023.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; metered connections; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced graduated sanctions record.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

principles.name: Nested enterprises

logic.formula_per_customer: water rate revenue $3,244,113 / 1,682 connections = $1,928.72 per connection
logic.formula_share: water rate revenue $3,244,113 / total annual revenue (eAR Section 8b B1.8) $4,513,945 = 71.87%

residual.represents: What it IS: revenue the system booked as program service on its 990 that is not accounted for by the eAR water-rate line, plausibly member assessments and other service revenue.
residual.does_not_represent: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.
