cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. The quartiles are never added up, weighted, ranked or turned into a single figure: this is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. A metric this system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place, is named above rather than counted against it.
cohort_position.cohort_note: The cohort is the mutual water companies in this project that file a Form 990 carrying financial data, which is not a sample of California's mutuals. member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending October 31
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends October 31. A fiscal year therefore shares ten of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other two with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2024, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $3,576,987 (990 program-service revenue) minus $3,244,113 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $332,874. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company formed in November 1912 as a not-for-profit California corporation, originally to irrigate citrus groves and supply domestic water to large estates. [1] It serves portions of the City of Covina, the City of West Covina and unincorporated Los Angeles County. [1] Members receiving water are also stockholders. [1] SDWIS publishes 1,681 service connections and a population of 7,775; the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 1,682 active service connections and 1,684 total potable connections against a served population of 7,775. [C][E]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $4,262,194 in FY2024 against expenses of $3,776,504, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $4,513,945 and total expenses of $4,604,225. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D] Charges are metered and billed m on a variable base residential structure priced per hundred cubic feet. [E]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: SDWIS records the primary source as Surface Water Purchased. [C] The eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 3 approved groundwater sources, 0 approved surface water sources and 2 approved purchased surface water sources, the purchased connections being a Metropolitan Water District middle feeder treated connection and a treated CIC connection. [E] The DWR survey carries 12 years of filed volume history. [P]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] The eAR names three approved groundwater wells, one of them recorded as standby. [E] No dated capital schedule is reported in a source this project holds.

Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: The company was formed in November 1912 in Los Angeles as a not-for-profit California corporation, its original purpose being irrigation of citrus groves and domestic supply to large estates. [1] It continues from the same headquarters address recorded in its eAR filing. [1][E]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company is owned by its customer-shareholders and states that a seven member Board of Directors governs it, and that every property owner in the service area is a stockholder including the directors, a requirement it says is written into its By-laws. [990] The eAR records the ownership type as privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 16 - Central, with an emergency response plan on file dated 12/27/2023. [E] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company. [SOS]

The disagreement is recorded and not reconciled. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.32 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.

components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 4 documented, 2 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 3,063 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 2,747.8 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set: the filer reports metered service, a billing frequency, a residential rate structure and a filed rate schedule, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is not visible in the filing and is not claimed here.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to metered use under a filed rate schedule: a variable base residential structure billed m and priced per hundred cubic feet.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; metered service; Variable Base residential rate structure.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.

metrics.name: Member Income Ratio
metrics.logic: The share of the mutual's income that comes from its own members. The tax rules for this kind of member-owned nonprofit (a 501(c)(12) mutual) expect at least 85 percent to come from members; slipping below can signal that member charges are not covering costs, and can even put the tax status at risk.
metrics.formula: member gross income / total gross income (members + other sources)
source_lines: Form 990 Part V line 11a (gross income from members)
Form 990 Part V line 11b (gross income from other sources)
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.
metrics.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

unit_economics.title: Unit economics
unit_economics.basis_note: Every metric here is PER CUSTOMER (a metered service connection). It is not a per-member figure; the member (shareholder) count is a different denominator, shown in the denominator block. The visible cell shows the value and its classification; the numerator, denominator, formula, and rationale are in each metric's LOGIC popup.

denominator.source: State Water Board eAR Section 4 (CurTotalConnections), reporting year 2024
denominator.note: The per-customer denominator is the eAR Section 4 total service-connection count for the SAME eAR reporting year (2024) that supplies the Section 8b revenue, so numerator and denominator are bound to the same reporting year.

total_revenue.source: State Water Board eAR Section 8b, question B1.8 (total annual revenue), reporting year 2024

unit_economics.primary_source: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue by rate/fee), reporting year 2024

logic.what_it_is: Revenue customers paid for water service, read straight off the filed eAR Section 8b water-rate line. A DIRECT filed figure, not computed by us.

numerator.name: Water rate revenue
numerator.as_filed: eAR Section 8b field B1.1 (residential water rates) + B1.2 (non-residential water rates)
numerator.source: State Water Board eAR Section 8b, question B1.1 + B1.2 (revenue from water rates), reporting year 2024

denominator.name: Total service connections
denominator.as_filed: eAR Section 4 CurTotalConnections, reporting year 2024
denominator.source: State Water Board eAR Section 4 (CurTotalConnections), reporting year 2024

logic.formula_per_customer: water rate revenue $2,749,185 / 3,063 connections = $897.55 per connection
logic.formula_share: water rate revenue $2,749,185 / total annual revenue (eAR Section 8b B1.8) $2,841,058 = 96.77%
logic.period_treatment: Numerator (eAR Section 8b, the calendar year 2024) and denominator (eAR Section 4 connections reported in the same eAR filing) are both the eAR reporting year 2024, so the two sides are bound to the same reporting year.
logic.rationale: Dividing water-rate revenue by the number of metered service connections gives the average revenue per customer; dividing by total annual revenue shows how much of the system's income comes from water rates.

metrics.name: Assessment revenue (990 program-service revenue not matched to eAR water-rate revenue)

logic.what_it_is: A DERIVED residual (medium confidence): the part of the Form 990 program-service revenue that is not matched by the eAR water-rate revenue for the same period. Computed by us, not a filed line.

input_a.name: Form 990 program-service revenue
input_a.source: Form 990 Part VIII line 2 (total program-service revenue), fiscal year 2024 ending December 31, 2024

input_b.name: eAR water-rate revenue
input_b.source: State Water Board eAR Section 8b, question B1.1 + B1.2 (revenue from water rates), reporting year 2024

residual.period_alignment: Both inputs cover the same period: the eAR Section 8b is the calendar year 2024 and the Form 990 fiscal year 2024 ends December 31, 2024, so the residual is period-aligned.
residual.represents: What it IS: revenue the system booked as program service on its 990 that is not accounted for by the eAR water-rate line, plausibly member assessments and other service revenue.
residual.does_not_represent: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

logic.formula_per_customer: residual $2,461,091 / 3,063 connections = $803.49 per connection
logic.formula_share: residual $2,461,091 / 990 program-service revenue $5,210,276 = 47.24%

structure.display: Tiered increasing-block with a fixed base, billed monthly, priced per HCF

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. The quartiles are never added up, weighted, ranked or turned into a single figure: this is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. A metric this system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place, is named above rather than counted against it.
cohort_position.cohort_note: The cohort is the mutual water companies in this project that file a Form 990 carrying financial data, which is not a sample of California's mutuals. Each metric places only the systems that report it at comparability tier A or B, so the n differs by metric and is stated on every line.

denominators.title: System Size and Water Use
denominators.note: System size and water use per fiscal year (the operating denominators that per-customer and per-acre metrics divide by), each cited to file and field. The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period

The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 6 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 67 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 4 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

violations.violation_name: Follow-up Or Routine LCR Tap M/R

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

gap_evidence.status_line: 6 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 1020004, 1020006, 1020007, 920002, 920003, 94V0001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2024, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $5,210,276 (990 program-service revenue) minus $2,749,185 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $2,461,091. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company serving parts of Calimesa and Yucaipa since 1912, with a service area that straddles the San Bernardino and Riverside county line. [1] SDWIS publishes 3,063 service connections and a population of 10,108; the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 3,063 active service connections. [C][E]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $5,271,327 in FY2024 against expenses of $3,613,581, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $2,841,058 and total expenses of $2,761,616. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D] Charges are metered and billed m on a variable base residential structure priced per hundred cubic feet. [E]

blocks.body: SDWIS records the primary source as Groundwater. [C] The eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 8 approved groundwater sources, 0 approved surface water sources and 0 approved purchased surface water sources. [E] The SGMA check matches this system to 2 groundwater basins. [SG] The DWR survey carries 12 years of filed volume history. [P]

net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: The company was established on 6 November 1912 as Yucaipa Water Company Number 3, part of the original Redlands and Yucaipa Water Company, and changed its name to South Mesa Water Company in 1913. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds. [990] The eAR records the ownership type as privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 20 - Riverside, with an emergency response plan on file dated 2/7/2024. [E] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company. [SOS]

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as Not At-Risk. [S] The US EPA SDWIS check returned 1 violation record(s) and 0 enforcement action(s) for this system. [C] A Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State Water Board's CCR portal; no supply-mix figure has been transcribed from it, which is a hand-transcription step and not an automated one. [CCR] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company: that source is reachable only through a browser session with an operator present and it now answers a persistent CAPTCHA, so nothing is recorded rather than guessed. [SOS]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 12.1% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 12.1% of the service area (333.7 acres), LRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.12 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Riverside County was in severe drought or worse 51.0% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Riverside County (FIPS 06065); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds 7 surface water rights of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds 7 licensed surface water rights of its own
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 2 designated basins, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA3310017 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3310017&Year=2024 (48684 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3310017&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)
Form 990 Part IX line 25 (total functional expenses)
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation), subtracted for the excluding variant
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Both variants are shown and the displayed variant is labeled (5A).

metrics.name: Days cash on hand
metrics.subtitle: days of operating cost covered by cash and marketable securities
metrics.limitation_note: Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

metrics.reference_source: Rating-agency convention: 200 plus days is strong, under roughly 90 days reads as stress, on unrestricted cash and investments (the State Water Board's SAFER risk indicator uses the same basis: Draft Final White Paper, Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, p. 28). Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.
metrics.formula: (cash, line 1; savings and temporary cash investments, line 2; publicly traded securities, line 11; other securities described as marketable on Schedule D Part VII, line 12) x 365 / (total expenses, line 25, less depreciation, line 22)
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 1 (cash, non-interest-bearing)
Form 990 Part X line 2 (savings and temporary cash investments)
Form 990 Part X line 11 (investments, publicly traded securities)

Form 990 Part IX line 25 less line 22 (operating expense excluding depreciation)

metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: cumulative over 4 comparable years (FY2021-24), excludes 1 not-reported year

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment at cost), year over year
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation)
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 3 documented, 2 partial, 3 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 2,574 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 1,649.8 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: This company files no eAR, so the filing that would document metering and rate structure does not exist for it. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No filed rate schedule or metering statement was located for this company.
principles.signal: No eAR Section 8a rate record held.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State's own CCR portal, and it holds an emergency response plan dated 3/25/2022.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.signal: No sourced graduated sanctions record.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize

This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.

principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. pwss_volume.title: Water volume history (DWR PWSS survey)

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending June 30
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends June 30. A fiscal year therefore shares six of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other six with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 1994-2005 form (no untreated-water column in this era)
DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 30 survey years, 1994 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 22 of the 30 years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 22 of the 30 years, across 5 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 66 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 74 were left blank. 8 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1994 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
pwss_volume.source: DWR Public Water System Statistics survey, received by email from DWR 2026-08-03; see data/pwss_historical/MANIFEST.md for provenance and data/staging/PWSS__cawc_0036.jsonl for the staged evidence.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: COACHELLA VALLEY - INDIO
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Medium priority, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. 6 agencies are named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Coachella Valley Water District GSA - Indio; Coachella Water Authority GSA; Desert Water Agency GSA - Non-Statutory Area - Indio; Desert Water Agency GSA - Statutory Area - Indio; Indio Water Authority GSA - Indio; Mission Springs Water District GSA - Indio
basins.gw_level_comment: No documented Groundwater Level Declines
basins.subsidence_comment:
1) It may be noted that preliminary results from a high-precision GPS survey in Sept/Oct 2015 indicate that much of the basin stopped subsiding since Sept 2010. The preliminary results also indicate that some areas near Palm Desert, Indian Wells, and La Quinta subsided since 2010, albeit at reduced rates compared to subsidence rates before 2010.
Source: USGS:
7-021.01_7b_LandSubsidenceGroundwaterLevelsandGeologyintheCoachellaValleyCA1993to2010SIR2014-5075USGS.pdf

2) "USGS has commenced their  next round of subsidence monitoring in the Coachella Valley. This report will be available in 2018. Since 1990, CVWD has invested over $1 million to monitor land subsidence in the region." 
Source: CVWD SGMA Alternative GSP (2016) 
7-021.01_7b_SGMA_AlternativeGSPBridgeDocumentIndio_Final.pdf

3)Text from the GSP Alternative Plan Bridge Document stated that …"decreased rates of subsidence, or uplift, were observed in the La Quinta area in 2010."  Figure 2 in the comment document for Basin Prioritization showed that 3 of 7 survey locations showed subsidence between 2010 and 2015.  In other words, 43% of survey locations showed active subsidence between 2010 and 2015.
Source: 7-021.01_7b_SGMA_AlternativeGSPBridgeDocumentIndio_Final.pdf
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: not recorded. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.
sgma_basin.source: CA DWR Bulletin 118 groundwater basins and SGMA Basin Prioritization, https://gis.water.ca.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Geoscientific/i08_B118_CA_GroundwaterBasins/MapServer/0/query Retrieved 2026-08-27.

sdwis_compliance.plain_lead: Two federal EPA tables disagree about this system. One lists no violations; the other points to 1 violation record it does not actually contain. Because the sources contradict each other, this system cannot be confirmed clean and cannot be confirmed as having violated. The conflict is preserved below rather than resolved.
sdwis_compliance.reason: Checked on 2026-08-31: the federal VIOLATION table returned no rows for PWSID CA3310051, but VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC references 1 violation id(s) for the same system. EPA's own tables disagree, so this system cannot be reported as clean. The disagreement is recorded and not reconciled; no violation record was invented for the referenced ids, because none was returned.
sdwis_compliance.title: Drinking-water compliance (US EPA SDWIS)

tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA3310051. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.
Returned 1 link row(s) for PWSID CA3310051, naming 1 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 94V0001.

gap_evidence.status_line: 1 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 94V0001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.
gap_evidence.source: US EPA Envirofacts SDWIS, https://data.epa.gov/efservice, tables VIOLATION and VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC, queried with the BEGINNING operator on the full PWSID. Retrieved 2026-09-23.

comparable.state_basis: State Water Board definition: unrestricted cash and investments divided by per-day operating expenses excluding depreciation (Draft Final White Paper, July 16, 2020, p. 28). The Hydronomics headline uses the same basis as far as Form 990 allows. The state publishes a risk level and a threshold result, not a figure, and the file does not state which assessment year it reflects.
comparable.state_definition_source: State Water Resources Control Board, Draft Final White Paper Discussion On: Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, pp. 27 and 28
comparable.ours_basis: Computed by this project from the filed financial statements, on the basis set out in the anchor-metrics framework.
comparable.comparison_note: Two readings of the same indicator from two different bases. blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A small mutual water company that has served Bermuda Dunes, an unincorporated part of Riverside County formerly called Myoma Dunes, since 1953, and a portion of the La Quinta area since 2005. [1] SDWIS publishes 2,574 service connections and a population of 9,445; the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 2,574 active service connections. [C][E]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $3,628,881 in FY2024 against expenses of $3,297,728, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $3,868,922 and total expenses of $3,978,690. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: The community is served from five company-owned wells drawing on the Lower Whitewater River sub-basin of the Coachella Valley aquifer. [1] SDWIS records the primary source as Groundwater. [C] The eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 5 approved groundwater sources, 0 approved surface water sources and 0 approved purchased surface water sources. [E] The DWR survey carries 30 years of filed volume history. [P]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] The company reports five owned wells located in the same area. [1] No dated capital schedule is reported in a source this project holds.

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: The company was established in the mid twentieth century by local residents and has supplied Bermuda Dunes since 1953. Ernie Dunlevie, a developer of the Bermuda Dunes Country Club, airport and racquet club, acquired the company to meet the expanding water needs of the community. [1] Service extended into part of La Quinta in 2005. [1]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds. [990] The eAR records the ownership type as privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 20 - Riverside, with an emergency response plan on file dated 3/25/2022. [E] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company. [SOS]

blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as At-Risk. [S] The US EPA SDWIS check could not be trusted for this system: the federal VIOLATION table returned no rows while VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC referenced violation ids for the same system, so EPA's own tables disagree and this system cannot be reported as clean. The disagreement is recorded and not reconciled. [C] A Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State Water Board's CCR portal; no supply-mix figure has been transcribed from it, which is a hand-transcription step and not an automated one. [CCR] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company: that source is reachable only through a browser session with an operator present and it now answers a persistent CAPTCHA, so nothing is recorded rather than guessed. [SOS]

blocks.body: The State Water Board has FIELD-VERIFIED its service-area boundary. [G][FH] Its service area carries no elevated fire hazard on the CAL FIRE layer. [FH] The federal SDWIS violation check returned no violation records. [C] Its filed revenue rose in every year held. [D]

blocks.body: The State Water Board records this system as At-Risk in its SAFER assessment. [S] That determination is carried in the State's own words and is not softened here, and it sits alongside a clean federal violation record, which is a disagreement between two regulators' views of the same system rather than a contradiction this project resolves. All five wells draw on one sub-basin, so the supply has a single physical source. [1]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2019-07-01 to 2024-06-30), Riverside County was in severe drought or worse 46.0% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Riverside County (FIPS 06065); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA3310051 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3310051&Year=2024 (1184137 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3310051&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 3 documented, 2 partial, 3 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 1,265 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 1,526.5 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: This company files no eAR, so the filing that would document metering and rate structure does not exist for it. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No filed rate schedule or metering statement was located for this company.
principles.signal: No eAR Section 8a rate record held.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State's own CCR portal, and it holds an emergency response plan dated 7/5/2022.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced graduated sanctions record.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned, non-PUC-regulated (Community Water System)'.

cohort_position.what_this_is: Where this system sits among this project's own filers on each anchor metric, as a quartile of the whole mutual cohort. Each metric is placed on its own. member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period
calendar_basis.label: Same reporting period. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $1,963,409 (990 program-service revenue) minus $1,811,319 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $152,090. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

blocks.body: A mutual water company founded on 9 August 1977, providing water and sewer service to the members of the community known as The Farm, in Wildomar. [1][2] It is the youngest company in this batch by more than three decades. SDWIS publishes 1,265 service connections and a population of 4,026; the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 1,265 active service connections. [C][E] The State publishes the name as FARM MUTUAL W.C. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $1,939,378 and total expenses of $1,276,082. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 98.8% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 98.8% of the service area (1508.5 acres), LRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.47 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Riverside County was in severe drought or worse 51.0% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Riverside County (FIPS 06065); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.
