governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 4 documented, 2 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: SDWIS defines the membership as a fixed set of service connections and the State Water Board publishes a SABL service-area polygon for it, so who is inside and outside the system is documented. The boundary is FIELD-VERIFIED by the Water Board rather than merely carried.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system: 6,217 service connections over a State-published and field-verified service-area boundary of roughly 5,418.6 acres.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set: the filer reports metered service, a billing frequency, a residential rate structure and a filed rate schedule, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is not visible in the filing and is not claimed here.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to metered use under a filed rate schedule: a variable usage residential structure billed bm and priced per hundred cubic feet.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; metered service; Variable Usage residential rate structure.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and it reports metered service, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State's own CCR portal.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; metered connections; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.

principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

metrics.name: Member Income Ratio
metrics.logic: The share of the mutual's income that comes from its own members. metrics.formula: member gross income / total gross income (members + other sources)
source_lines: Form 990 Part V line 11a (gross income from members)
Form 990 Part V line 11b (gross income from other sources)
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.

denominators.title: System Size and Water Use
denominators.note: System size and water use per fiscal year (the operating denominators that per-customer and per-acre metrics divide by), each cited to file and field. The eAR is reported on the calendar year; the 990 fiscal year differs by company. A calendar-year filer's volume is the eAR annual total (fiscal year = calendar year); an offset filer's is recast by a true monthly sum of the covered calendar months, or read not reported naming the missing months. Point-in-time counts (connections, population) are matched to the closest eAR year and never summed. Every derived figure states its formula and accounting rationale.
denominators.monthly_source: California open-data portal (data.ca.gov): the separate Produced Water (by month and source) and Delivered Water (by month and connection type) resources, which cover every public water system (not only urban suppliers), one resource per reporting year, matched by exact PWSID. This is the aggregate publication of eAR Section 6.

member_vs_customer.difference_note: One of the two counts is not published, so the difference is not stated.
member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period
calendar_basis.label: Same reporting period. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 1994-2005 form (no untreated-water column in this era)
DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 28 survey years, 1994 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 19 of the 28 years, across 3 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 21 of the 28 years, across 10 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 40 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 75 were left blank. 5 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1994 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
pwss_volume.source: DWR Public Water System Statistics survey, received by email from DWR 2026-08-03; see data/pwss_historical/MANIFEST.md for provenance and data/staging/PWSS__cawc_0038.jsonl for the staged evidence.

violations.violation_name: Follow-up Or Routine LCR Tap M/R

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

tables.says: Returned 1 violation record(s) for PWSID CA3610057, which are the records listed on this page.
Returned 3 link row(s) for PWSID CA3610057, naming 1 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 9813001.

gap_evidence.status_line: 1 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 9813001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

plant_per_acre.title: Plant assets per acre
plant_per_acre.acres_source: Geodesic area (WGS84 spherical excess) of the SABL service-area polygon.
plant_per_acre.logic: Infrastructure built per acre of service area. Gross plant per acre is the primary read because it measures how much plant the system has put in the ground per acre, and unlike net plant it does not fall over time purely because the assets depreciate on the books. Net plant per acre is shown alongside as the depreciated book value per acre.
plant_per_acre.formula: gross plant per acre = Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment, gross) / SABL service-area acres; net plant per acre uses Part X line 10c (net)
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (gross) and line 10c (net)
Geodesic area (WGS84 spherical excess) of the SABL service-area polygon.
plant_per_acre.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Filed gross/net plant over the measured SABL service-area acreage.
plant_per_acre.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

water_operations.note: Water production and demand profile. Sourced field by field from the system Consumer Confidence Report and SDWIS Drinking Water Watch (State Water Board), the ACFR statistical section where a filer reports it, and the eAR; each field carries its source, year, and confidence. how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2024, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: A period-aligned residual cannot be computed for this filer, so the metric is rendered IMPOSSIBLE rather than guessed.
entries.note: Not derivable. The eAR Section 8b is the calendar year 2024 while the Form 990 fiscal year ends None; the two period ends are not aligned, so a period-aligned residual cannot be computed.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company incorporated on 21 February 1898, successor to the Vivienda company that began moving water from artesian wells along the Lytle Creek wash in 1871. [1] It was one of three companies supplying water for citrus on the Riverside Mesa south of the Santa Ana River, serving the highest elevations, an area now known as Grand Terrace. [1] SDWIS publishes 6,217 service connections and a population of 67,304; the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 6,217 active service connections. [C][E]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $5,953,474 in FY2023 against expenses of $5,535,377, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $5,302,355 and total expenses of $5,695,919. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D] Charges are metered and billed bm on a variable usage residential structure priced per hundred cubic feet. [E]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: SDWIS records the primary source as Groundwater. [C] The eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 3 approved groundwater sources, 0 approved surface water sources and 0 approved purchased surface water sources. [E] The SGMA check matches this system to 2 groundwater basins. [SG] The DWR survey carries 28 years of filed volume history. [P]

blocks.body: This company holds THREE years of filed financials, not five. Neither the IRS efile index nor ProPublica carries a return for tax period 202112 or 202412, so FY2021 and FY2024 are absent and its latest available year is FY2023. [990] Nothing was lost in acquisition; the returns are not published. Its Part XI reconciliation does not foot in any of the three years held, and its FY2020 filing also reported 3,925 dollars of royalties on Part VIII line 5, a line this project did not capture until the defect this batch exposed was fixed. Roughly 49.8 percent of its service area falls in a CAL FIRE High or Very High fire hazard severity zone. [FH]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 49.8% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 49.8% of the service area (2699.3 acres), LRA, SRA

detail.label: Moderate zone
detail.value: about 0.0% of the service area (0.4 acres), LRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 10.15 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2023-12-31), San Bernardino County was in severe drought or worse 65.4% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, San Bernardino County (FIPS 06071); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds 14 surface water rights of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.value: Underlain by 2 designated basins, none in critical overdraft

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA3610057 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3610057&Year=2024 (1374981 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3610057&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 3 documented, 3 partial, 2 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: Membership is documented as a fixed set of service connections, so the social boundary is clear. The physical boundary is published but carries the State's Not Verified flag, so it is drawn dashed and every figure derived from its acreage is held at lower confidence.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system with 1,219 service connections and a State-published service area of roughly 1,101.3 acres, but the State Water Board has NOT verified that boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Not Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: The record documents how charges are set: the filer reports metered service, a billing frequency, a residential rate structure and a filed rate schedule, so cost tracks service. Whether every tier scales precisely with use is not visible in the filing and is not claimed here.
principles.finding: Charges are tied to metered use under a filed rate schedule: a variable base residential structure billed bm and priced per hundred cubic feet.
principles.signal: eAR Section 8a customer charges; metered service; Variable Base residential rate structure.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company distributes water to shareholders in proportion to the stock they hold, and its shareholders include two cities and a water district; the City of Upland alone holds a 68 percent interest.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; distribution in proportion to stock held; institutional shareholders including a 68 percent city interest; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and it reports metered service, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State's own CCR portal, and it holds an emergency response plan dated 1/1/2022.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; metered connections; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced graduated sanctions record.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: Physical nesting is documented. What is not documented is any governance role in a wholesaler or in a groundwater sustainability agency, so the tier is PARTIAL rather than met.
principles.finding: The system sits inside larger water systems: it pumps from 3 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors, and it holds 2 approved emergency intertie(s) with other systems, and it holds 22 State-recorded surface water right(s) on a shared river system. Its role in governing any of them is not documented.
principles.signal: it pumps from 3 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors; it holds 2 approved emergency intertie(s) with other systems; it holds 22 State-recorded surface water right(s) on a shared river system

logic.logic: At 10 HCF/month, a single-family customer's monthly bill is $34.32: a fixed base charge of $27.52 plus $6.80 of metered (volumetric) charges. The effective price is $3.43 per HCF at this usage.
source_lines: eAR Section 8a single-family charges grid (base + tiers), reporting year 2024

kv.v: Bimonthly biller: the bill is computed on 20 HCF per bimonthly bill (2 times the monthly usage) against the filed per-bill tiers, then divided by 2 to state it per month.

Defined single-family usage levels, identical for every company so the bill is comparable: Low = 5 HCF/month (~125 gallons/day); Median = 10 HCF/month (~249 gallons/day); High = 25 HCF/month (~623 gallons/day). 1 HCF = 748 gallons, and 1 thousand gallons = 1,000 gallons. The usage is converted into the company's own filed unit before the filed tiers are applied, and the bill is stated as a monthly equivalent: a bimonthly structure is computed at twice the monthly usage and divided by two, and any other billing period the same way with its factor stated. These are an illustration, not a measured usage for any real customer.

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period
calendar_basis.label: Same reporting period. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 4 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 11 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 67 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 22 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. sdwis_compliance.title: Drinking-water compliance (US EPA SDWIS)
sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2024, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $5,180,653 (990 program-service revenue) minus $4,945,555 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $235,098. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company incorporated on 25 October 1882 to bring water down from the mountains north of its land, distributing water to shareholders in proportion to the stock they hold. [1] Its shareholders are largely institutional rather than households: most residents of unincorporated San Antonio Heights, the cities of Upland and Ontario, Monte Vista Water District, a local golf course, rock product companies and a few remaining grove irrigators; the City of Upland alone holds a 68 percent shareholder interest. [1][2] SDWIS publishes 1,219 service connections against a served population of 79,217. [C] A connection count of that size against a population of that size is an as-filed extreme, flagged and not explained away.

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $5,418,549 in FY2024 against expenses of $5,336,688, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $5,418,550 and total expenses of $5,177,629. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D] Charges are metered and billed bm on a variable base residential structure priced per hundred cubic feet. [E]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: SDWIS records the primary source as Groundwater. [C] The eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 10 approved groundwater sources, 0 approved surface water sources and 0 approved purchased surface water sources. [E] The SGMA check matches this system to 3 groundwater basins, the widest basin footprint in this batch. [SG] The DWR survey carries 12 years of filed volume history. [P]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] No dated capital schedule is reported in a source this project holds.

Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: The company was incorporated on 25 October 1882 and formed to bring mountain water down to its members' land. [1] Additional production from the Chino Basin followed a lowered water table in the Cucamonga Basin, and the company filed a complaint in the Superior Court to determine the water rights of all Cucamonga Basin users. [2] A chronological company history from 1882 to 1947 is held in the Upland Public Library local history collection. [2]

blocks.title: Who runs it and how
blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company distributes water to shareholders in proportion to the stock they hold, and its shareholders include two cities and a water district; the City of Upland alone holds a 68 percent interest. [990] The eAR records the ownership type as privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 27 - Mojave, with an emergency response plan on file dated 1/1/2022. [E] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company. [SOS]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 43.1% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 43.1% of the service area (474.8 acres), LRA, SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 3.23 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), San Bernardino County was in severe drought or worse 58.6% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 2 documented, 3 partial, 3 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: Membership is documented as a fixed set of service connections, so the social boundary is clear. The physical boundary is published but carries the State's Not Verified flag, so it is drawn dashed and every figure derived from its acreage is held at lower confidence.

member_vs_customer.explainer: In a mutual water company a MEMBER is a shareholder who owns part of the system; a CUSTOMER is a metered service connection that receives water. The two diverge because one owner can hold several connections, a connection can serve people who are not owners, and some mutuals attach shares to land by acreage rather than counting heads. Per-customer metrics divide by service connections; per-member metrics divide by shareholders; the two counts are never used interchangeably.

calendar_basis.short: Same reporting period
calendar_basis.label: Same reporting period. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31, and this system also files on the calendar year (fiscal year ends December 31), so the two series cover the same twelve months. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 5 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 82 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 7 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
pwss_volume.source: DWR Public Water System Statistics survey, received by email from DWR 2026-08-03; see data/pwss_historical/MANIFEST.md for provenance and data/staging/PWSS__cawc_0040.jsonl for the staged evidence.

tables.says: Returned no rows for PWSID CA3610053. On this table alone the system has no violation on record.
Returned 2 link row(s) for PWSID CA3610053, naming 1 violation id(s) in the same id space that the VIOLATION table did not return: 613001.

gap_evidence.status_line: 1 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 613001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

The state publishes a risk level and a threshold result, not a figure, and the file does not state which assessment year it reflects.

comparable.state_basis: State Water Board definition: operating revenue divided by operating expenses including depreciation (Draft Final White Paper, July 16, 2020, p. 27). safer_standing.note: Failing, At-Risk, Potentially At-Risk, Not At-Risk and Not Assessed are the State Water Board's own categories and its own determination about this system. They are carried here in the state's words and are not this project's assessment of the company. An automatic designation is made regardless of the category scores beneath it, so a system can be listed At-Risk while scoring NONE or LOW on most categories.

how_built.title: How this was built
how_built.intro: A plain account of the forensic lineage behind the hard-to-source metrics: what sources were checked, what was found, what was derived, and what could not be built and why. Every figure marked DERIVED or IMPOSSIBLE above is traceable to a line here.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
State Water Board eAR Section 4 (connection count, same reporting year)
audited financial statement (secondary cross-check, where published)
entries.found: The eAR Section 8b reports water-rate revenue for reporting year 2024, so this is a DIRECT filed figure; per customer it is divided by the eAR Section 4 connection count for the same reporting year, so numerator and denominator share the year.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8b (water-rate revenue B1.1/B1.2)
entries.found: No source separately reports a member assessment, so it is DERIVED as a residual: $4,391,157 (990 program-service revenue) minus $2,869,831 (eAR water-rate revenue) = $1,521,326. Period-aligned; medium confidence.
entries.note: This residual is a difference between two sources for the same period; it is not a separately filed assessment line and may include other unmatched revenue.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports a base/meter rate PRICE, but the filing carries no meter revenue line and no tier volume, and the base charge is already inside the water-sales revenue (eAR Section 8b water rates). Building a separate meter figure would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

sources_checked: State Water Board eAR Section 8a (rate prices)
State Water Board eAR Section 8b (revenue lines)
entries.found: The rate price exists in Section 8a but no revenue or tier volume is reported, and the base charge is already inside water sales.
entries.note: The eAR Section 8a reports tiered/overage rate PRICES, but the filing carries no overage revenue and no tier consumption volume, and any overage billed is already inside the water-sales revenue. Building it would double-count. Not backed into from a total.

entries.found: The reporting basis (fiscal vs calendar year) is read from the filer's own B0.1/B0.2 answer and staged verbatim, never hardcoded, so the 990 comparison and the residual are period-aligned.
No filing states a member/shareholder count, so the per-member unit economics read not reported rather than borrowing the connection count.
Volume delivered in acre-feet is not in the Form 990 and the CCR states only a source mix, so the per-acre-foot metrics read not reported; the eAR Section 6 is named as the source still needed.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: An incorporated mutual water company founded in 1910, owned and supported by its shareholders, serving portions of Yucaipa and part of Redlands across roughly four square miles. [1] SDWIS publishes 2,307 service connections and a population of 7,521; the eAR for reporting year 2024 reports 2,307 active service connections. [C][E]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $4,585,880 in FY2024 against expenses of $3,291,645, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR Section 8b for reporting year 2024 reports total revenue of $3,257,610 and total expenses of $2,893,934. Those are two filings on two bases and the gap is surfaced rather than reconciled; neither figure is adjusted toward the other. [E][D]

The company is owned by its shareholders and states that a five member Board of Directors governs it, with directors required to be shareholders. [990] The eAR records the ownership type as privately owned mutual water company or association, regulated by State Water Board District 27 - Mojave, with an emergency response plan on file dated 1/19/2021. blocks.title: On the record
blocks.body: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as At-Risk, an automatic designation. [S] The US EPA SDWIS check could not be trusted for this system: the federal VIOLATION table returned no rows while VIOLATION_ENF_ASSOC referenced violation ids for the same system, so EPA's own tables disagree and this system cannot be reported as clean. The disagreement is recorded and not reconciled. [C] A Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State Water Board's CCR portal; no supply-mix figure has been transcribed from it, which is a hand-transcription step and not an automated one. [CCR] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company: that source is reachable only through a browser session with an operator present and it now answers a persistent CAPTCHA, so nothing is recorded rather than guessed. blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: A five member Board of Directors governs the company and directors are required to be shareholders, which is a documented collective-choice rule rather than an inferred one. [1] It draws on more than one groundwater basin. [SG] The federal SDWIS violation check returned no violation records. [C]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: TWO RECORDS OF THIS SYSTEM DISAGREE AND BOTH ARE CARRIED. The State Water Board records it as At-Risk in its SAFER assessment, and the determination is an AUTOMATIC one on the stated basis of bottled or hauled water. [S] The company's own site describes five groundwater recharge wells and three reservoirs totalling 4.5 million gallons. [1] Those two statements are not reconciled here; the State's determination is printed in the State's own words and the company's description is printed in its own, and closing the gap needs a source neither of them is. Separately, the State Water Board has NOT verified its service-area boundary [G][FH], and roughly 45.9 percent of its service area falls in a CAL FIRE High or Very High fire hazard severity zone. [FH]

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 45.9% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 45.9% of the service area (1345.4 acres), LRA, SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.61 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), San Bernardino County was in severe drought or worse 58.6% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, San Bernardino County (FIPS 06071); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Buys treated water from other agencies; it holds 8 surface water rights of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.value: Surface Water Purchased (purchased treated surface water)
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds 8 licensed surface water rights of its own
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 2 designated basins, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA3610053 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3610053&Year=2024 (289236 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3610053&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

blocks.title: Who they are
blocks.body: A mutual water company incorporated on 15 June 1903 by Redlands and Highland area citrus growers, owned and supported by its shareholders. [1] IT IS NOT A PUBLIC DRINKING WATER SYSTEM. The company states that its water is NON-POTABLE and available only for irrigation, and that most of its stockholders use it to irrigate citrus and avocado groves and some landscaping, with a narrow exception where potable water is delivered under City of Redlands agreements for specific partner companies. [1] At its first annual meeting on 18 November 1903, 70,559 shares had been subscribed by users of the Bear Valley System. [1] This company therefore has NO PWSID: the statewide SDWIS inventory was searched by name, by city Redlands and by county San Bernardino and matched nothing, which is consistent with a system that does not sell treated drinking water to the public. [C]

blocks.title: How the money works
blocks.body: Revenue of $1,818,801 in FY2024 against expenses of $1,703,071, from water charges and assessments to member-shareholders. [D][990] The eAR carries no Section 8b revenue figure for this company, so there is no second filed revenue basis to compare against. [E]

blocks.title: Where the water comes from
blocks.body: The company reports drawing on the Santa Ana River as its primary supply, together with Big Bear Lake, Mill Creek, wells, the State Water Project and seasonal precipitation. [1] It supplies water from the lake to North Fork Water Company and to Redlands through Bear Creek, a tributary running from the lake to the Santa Ana River. [2] The State Water Board water rights check matched 6 surface water rights to this company, and those rights ARE its supply record: with no PWSID there is no SDWIS source classification, no eAR filing, no Consumer Confidence Report and no DWR volume survey for it. [WR][C][E]

blocks.title: Infrastructure and its age
blocks.body: Plant is read from the Form 990 balance sheet; the computed net plant age is shown with its multi-year trend. [990][D] The company maintains dams and distribution works and operates seasonally. [1] In 1884 Bear Valley was dammed with a single arch granite structure impounding some 25,000 acre-feet for irrigation in the Redlands area, and in 1912 a 72 foot multiple arch dam designed by John S. Eastwood was built about 300 feet downstream, raising capacity to 73,000 acre-feet. [2]

source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment; gross)
Form 990 Part X line 10b (accumulated depreciation)
net_plant_age.logic: Accumulated depreciation as a share of gross plant (Form 990 Part X line 10b over line 10a): the portion of the system's plant already depreciated, a proxy for average plant age. A falling trend means reinvestment is renewing the plant faster than it wears down. This shares its inputs with the Asset Consumption Ratio on the tearsheet.
net_plant_age.confidence_reason: A ratio derived from two filed Part X figures; medium per the BLUEPRINT confidence tiers (a derivation, not a direct line item).
net_plant_age.what_would_change: nothing; the value is comparable as filed

blocks.title: How they got here
blocks.body: In the summer of 1883 Frank Brown began taking prospective investors up and down the mountains to sell the idea of an arch dam in Bear Valley, and the valley was dammed in 1884. [2] The Certificate of Incorporation for Bear Valley Mutual Water Company was issued by the California Secretary of State on 15 June 1903, with the first meeting eleven days later. [1] It was formed by Redlands and Highland area citrus growers. [1]

blocks.body: A member-owned mutual water company that provides water to its shareholders. The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds. [990] The California Secretary of State corporate registration and filed officer roster are NOT YET CHECKED for this company. [SOS]

blocks.title: Strengths
blocks.body: Its supply rests on senior surface water rights on the Santa Ana River system together with storage at Big Bear Lake, which is a materially different position from a groundwater pumper's. [1][WR] It carries the longest documented physical infrastructure history of any company in this batch, with two dated dams. [2] Its filed revenue exceeded expenses in every year held. [D]

blocks.title: Weak points and watch items
blocks.body: This company is the least externally corroborated in the batch and that is stated rather than implied. ProPublica publishes no parsed extract for any year in the FY2020 to FY2024 window, carrying only filing PDFs for FY2021 and FY2024, and the company is absent from the committed CA 501(c)(12) IRS Business Master File extract entirely, so NONE of its five years has a second publisher of its revenue figure. [PP][BMF] Its figures come from its own IRS efile XML and pass every internal identity, and all five years are staged at high confidence, but the absent corroboration is a fact about the sources and is recorded here. Because it holds no PWSID, the two PWSID-scoped standard recipe steps are a structural not-applicable, no SABL polygon exists to lay over the fire hazard map, and the State publishes no SAFER determination for it. [C][FH][S] None of those absences is a finding that the system is sound.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.absence: No composite is composed for this system. 1 of 3 components could be computed (Drought regime), which is not enough to compose a read over. The components that could not be computed are listed with the reason each one failed; a single reading presented as a composite would claim a completeness this system does not have.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.plain_lead: No service-area boundary is on file for this system, so there is no shape to lay over the fire hazard map. That is a missing outline, not a finding that the system faces no fire risk.
components.reason: No PWSID is recorded for this system, so there is no SABL service-area polygon to intersect with the hazard zone layer. The join is areal and there is no geometry to join with; this is a missing key, not a finding that the system faces no fire hazard.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.value: not reported

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2019-11-01 to 2024-10-31), San Bernardino County was in severe drought or worse 56.7% of the time.

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, San Bernardino County (FIPS 06071); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.

metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

governance.title: Institutional design: Ostrom's eight principles (evidence status)

overall.summary: 2 documented, 3 partial, 3 not documented of eight principles.
overall.reason: A count of how many of Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles have a supporting record on file, not a grade. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

governance.not_documented_distinction: NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
governance.note: Each mutual is read against Elinor Ostrom's eight design principles for institutions that govern a shared resource durably. Per principle: a one-line finding, the observable signal, a citation, and an evidence status stating whether the supporting record exists: DOCUMENTED (a cited record supports alignment), PARTIAL (some evidence exists but it is incomplete), or NOT DOCUMENTED (no supporting record was found). This is an evidence-status read, not a grade: the principles are never ranked, weighted, or given a letter, consistent with reporting as filed and not grading companies. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.

principles.name: Clearly defined boundaries
principles.evidence_reason: Membership is documented as a fixed set of service connections, so the social boundary is clear. The physical boundary is published but carries the State's Not Verified flag, so it is drawn dashed and every figure derived from its acreage is held at lower confidence.
principles.finding: The system is a defined public water system with 387 service connections and a State-published service area of roughly 650.0 acres, but the State Water Board has NOT verified that boundary.
principles.signal: SDWIS Community water system; SABL service-area boundary (Not Verified); connections defined.

principles.name: Rules fit local conditions
principles.evidence_reason: This company files no eAR, so the filing that would document metering and rate structure does not exist for it. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No filed rate schedule or metering statement was located for this company.
principles.signal: No eAR Section 8a rate record held.

principles.name: Collective-choice arrangements
principles.evidence_reason: A collective-choice mechanism is documented in outline: the customers are the shareholders. It stays PARTIAL rather than met because the filed corporate record that would carry the director roster and the election procedure is NOT YET CHECKED for this company, the California Secretary of State being reachable only through a browser session that now answers a CAPTCHA. A stated board is not a filed roster.
principles.finding: The company is owned by its customer-shareholders, but the specific board, the election procedure and any record of member votes are not in a source this project holds.
principles.signal: Mutual ownership; Form 990 governance section.

principles.name: Monitoring
principles.evidence_reason: Operational monitoring is documented from more than one filing. What the federal violation check found is reported separately in the On the record block and is not folded into this tier.
principles.finding: The system is monitored and reports on itself: it files an annual eAR, and a Consumer Confidence Report for 2024 was located at the State's own CCR portal, and it holds an emergency response plan dated 3/14/2025.
principles.signal: Annual eAR reporting; located Consumer Confidence Report

principles.name: Graduated sanctions
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published shut-off, penalty, or delinquency policy was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced graduated sanctions record.

principles.name: Conflict-resolution mechanisms
principles.evidence_reason: No public record of a bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was located. NOT DOCUMENTED means the supporting record was not found, not that the company governs badly. It marks a gap in the documentary record, an evidence gap to close, never a governance failing.
principles.finding: No published bylaws, dispute procedure, or grievance mechanism was found for this system.
principles.signal: No sourced conflict-resolution mechanisms record.

principles.name: Recognized right to organize
principles.evidence_reason: Baseline legal standing is documented by two independent regulators: the IRS accepts it as a tax-exempt 501(c)(12) filer and the State Water Board holds it as a Community public water system with a mutual ownership type. This status does NOT rest on a filed corporate record, because the Secretary of State check has not been run for this company.
principles.finding: An incorporated California mutual water company recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(12) exempt filer and by the State Water Board as a Community public water system.
principles.signal: IRS 501(c)(12) exempt filer (Form 990); SDWIS Community public water system; eAR ownership type 'Privately owned Mutual Water Company or Association'.

principles.name: Nested enterprises
principles.evidence_reason: Physical nesting is documented. What is not documented is any governance role in a wholesaler or in a groundwater sustainability agency, so the tier is PARTIAL rather than met.
principles.finding: The system sits inside larger water systems: it pumps from 1 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors, and it holds 2 approved emergency intertie(s) with other systems. Its role in governing any of them is not documented.
principles.signal: it pumps from 1 groundwater basin(s) shared with neighbors; it holds 2 approved emergency intertie(s) with other systems
