metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.

metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.

metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Riverside County was in severe drought or worse 56.9% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Riverside County (FIPS 06065); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Buys treated water from other agencies for 100% of its supply; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.source: https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3310033&Year=2023 (as filed: "All SARWC water was purchased from JCSD 870 Zone.")

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from this system's own 2023 Consumer Confidence Report, which states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: These two records disagree and both are kept as filed. The State Water Board inventory publishes this system's primary source as Groundwater. Its own 2023 Consumer Confidence Report states a mix in which buys 100% from other agencies, which is the majority of its supply. The band above is built from the report, because the report states figures and the inventory states one code; the code is not corrected, overwritten or removed, and a reader can see both.
components.cross_source_heading: The two records disagree, and both are kept as filed
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3310033&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.

Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.

metrics.name: Reinvestment ratio
metrics.subtitle: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: cumulative over 4 comparable years (FY2022-25), excludes 1 not-reported year

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 27 survey years, 1997 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 20 of the 27 years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 22 of the 27 years, across 5 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 72 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 63 were left blank. 7 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 1997 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (1008.6 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 3.63 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-07-01 to 2025-06-30), Lake County was in severe drought or worse 53.8% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Lake County (FIPS 06033); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Takes surface water from its own source; it holds no surface water right of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The State Water Board report viewer was asked for PWSID CA1710014 for every year in the declared window 2021 to 2024 on 2026-09-23 and returned no readable document (2024: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2023: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2022: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2021: HTTP 404 Not Found). The report was searched for and could not be located; nothing is concluded here about this system's supply. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

The state publishes a risk level and a threshold result, not a figure, and the file does not state which assessment year it reflects.
comparable.state_definition_source: State Water Resources Control Board, Draft Final White Paper Discussion On: Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, pp. 27 and 28
comparable.direction: revenue over expenses; 1.0x or above means revenue covers expenses
comparable.ours_basis: Computed by this project from the filed financial statements, on the basis set out in the anchor-metrics framework.
comparable.comparison_note: Two readings of the same indicator from two different bases. They are shown side by side and are deliberately NOT combined: the state's is a threshold test whose definition this project does not hold, and this project's is a computed figure. Neither is used to check or correct the other.

safer_standing.no_year_note: The state's published file carries no assessment year: its own date field is identical on every row and is the date the extract was produced. The date shown here is when this project retrieved the determination.
safer_standing.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad
safer_standing.note: Failing, At-Risk, Potentially At-Risk, Not At-Risk and Not Assessed are the State Water Board's own categories and its own determination about this system. They are carried here in the state's words and are not this project's assessment of the company. An automatic designation is made regardless of the category scores beneath it, so a system can be listed At-Risk while scoring NONE or LOW on most categories.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (27.4 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 0.6 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2019-07-01 to 2025-06-30), Alpine County was in severe drought or worse 34.8% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Alpine County (FIPS 06003); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Takes surface water from its own source; it holds no surface water right of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA0202504&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)

A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 22 survey years, 2003 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 22 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 20 of those years, across 3 customer classes.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2019-11-01 to 2024-10-31), Madera County was in severe drought or worse 43.3% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Madera County (FIPS 06039); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and the ground beneath it is in critical overdraft, which is the state's finding that the basin is pumped faster than it refills.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by SAN JOAQUIN VALLEY - MADERA (5-022.06) in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

detail.label: Basin placement confidence
detail.value: The basin placement is an areal join and is carried at low; it is never better than the service-area boundary it rests on.
detail.source: BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA2010010&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 51.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Buys treated water from other agencies; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.value: Surface Water Purchased (purchased treated surface water)
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910086&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: SAN JACINTO
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. One agency is named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: West San Jacinto GSA
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 8-005_7a_Hydrographs_SanJacinto.pdf

2) The Hemet/San Jacinto Grounjdwater Management Area monitors around 200 wells twice a year, but report has no hydrographs and does not summarize long-term history. There is a Basin Storage graph that shows delining storage.
Source: 8-005_7a_HemetSanJacintoGWMA2015AnnualReport.pdf  pg 225

3) Historically, extraction in excess of recharge has resulted in lowered groundwater levels and altered directions of groundwater flow. 
Source: 8-005_7a_HSJ_WMP_final.pdf  pg 55
basins.subsidence_comment:
1) Subsidence related to tectonic deformation and aquifer compaction; reported subsidence of 2.3 feet between 1939 and 1959

Lofgren (1976) measured compaction of aquifer materials with a 377-m deep extensometer from 1970 to 1974 and concluded that inelastic compaction of aquifer materials in the depth range of the extensometer amounted to about 1 cm /yr (0.04 ft/yr) and that tectonic subsidence amounted to 0.3-0.6 cm/yr (0.1-0. 2 in/yr). That is, most permanent subsidence (70-80 percent) resulted from groundwater withdrawal, with the remainder from tectonic downwarping of the valley.
Source: USGS Journal of Research: 
8-005_7b_JournalofResearchoftheUSGeologicalSurveyJantoFeb1976Vol4Number1USDeptInterior.pdf

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 33.4% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 31.6% of the service area (1018.4 acres), LRA, SRA

detail.label: High zone
detail.value: about 1.8% of the service area (58.9 acres), SRA

detail.label: Moderate zone
detail.value: about 1.2% of the service area (39.1 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 10.04 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Riverside County was in severe drought or worse 56.9% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Riverside County (FIPS 06065); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Buys treated water from other agencies; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.value: Surface Water Purchased (purchased treated surface water)
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2023 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA3310026 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3310026&Year=2023 (5873961 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3310026&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 44.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910169&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 18 survey years, 2007 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 18 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 16 of the 18 years, across 4 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 87 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 32 were left blank. 3 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2007 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 99.4% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 99.4% of the service area (1337.8 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 5.03 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2025-12-31), Calaveras County was in severe drought or worse 32.6% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Calaveras County (FIPS 06009); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Buys treated water from other agencies; it holds no surface water right of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.value: Surface Water Purchased (purchased treated surface water)
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA0510009 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA0510009&Year=2024 (2226790 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA0510009&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: UPPER MOJAVE RIVER VALLEY
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) CASGEM/WDL/GWIDS: Some Long term hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 6-042_7a_Hydrographs_UpperMojave.pdf

2) USGS hydrographs show majority of hydrographs are stable with two hydrographs showing long-term decline (correlating the DWR Upper Mojave River Valley with the USGS Mojave River Basin, Alto Subbasin).
Source:  Various_7a_Mojave&MorongoGroundwaterBasinHydrographs_USGS.pdf
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: not recorded. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

basins.name: EL MIRAGE VALLEY
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) CASGEM/WDL/GWIDS: Long term hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 6-043_7a_Hydrographs_ElMirageValley.pdf

2) Research shows that water levels have declined about 15 meters within the last 80 years. 
Source: 6-043_7a_HiQualityGWinElMirageValley.pdf  pg 1
basins.subsidence_comment:
1) Because surface water is scarce, groundwater has been the source of water for agricultural, industrial, and municipal uses throughout the Mojave Desert since the early 1900s (Sneed et al., 2003). Unplanned and unmonitored development of groundwater has produced unanticipated land subsidence when aquifer systems transitioned from elastic compression to inelastic compaction. The results included an increase in the extent of inland flooding, damaged engineered infrastructure, and the sudden appearance and erosional enlargement of destructive earth fissures, which have become permanent features of the landscape.
Source: USGS Various_7b_1992-2009LandSubsidenceinSWMojaveDesrtCaUSGSINSARFactsheet2017-3053.pdf

2) Land surface subsided a total of about 35 millimeters (mm), or 1.38 inches (in.), from May 2005 to May 2009 near the southeastern tip of El Mirage Lake (dry) at a fairly steady rate of about 9 millimeters per year (mm/yr.), or 0.35 inches per year (in./yr.)
Source: Various_7b_USGS_2004-2009MojaveRegionLand-SubsidenceStudyWebsite

Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

gap_evidence.status_line: 1 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 95V0001. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 29.2% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Moderate zone
detail.value: about 69.4% of the service area (4864.2 acres), SRA

detail.label: High zone
detail.value: about 15.3% of the service area (1070.2 acres), SRA

detail.label: Very High zone
detail.value: about 13.9% of the service area (975.2 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 17.82 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), San Bernardino County was in severe drought or worse 58.6% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, San Bernardino County (FIPS 06071); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds 1 surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds 1 licensed surface water right of its own
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 3 designated basins, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3610109&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.
