weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (324.9 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 2.23 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2019-07-01 to 2025-06-30), San Bernardino County was in severe drought or worse 60.7% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, San Bernardino County (FIPS 06071); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Buys treated water from other agencies; it holds 14 surface water rights of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.value: Surface Water Purchased (purchased treated surface water)
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds 14 licensed surface water rights of its own
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3610002&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

metrics.window_average_basis: cumulative over 5 comparable years (FY2021-25)
metrics.rank_exclusion_reason: C1: a depreciation denominator flag (stale depreciation or an implied depreciation rate outside 1 to 6 percent) on an included year

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment at cost), year over year
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation)
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

unit_economics.title: Unit economics
unit_economics.basis_note: Every metric here is PER CUSTOMER (a metered service connection). It is not a per-member figure; the member (shareholder) count is a different denominator, shown in the denominator block. The visible cell shows the value and its classification; the numerator, denominator, formula, and rationale are in each metric's LOGIC popup.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

From 1990 to 2000, nearly 0.4 feet of subsidence (Sneed and Galloway, 2000).  Fissures range from one inch to over one foot wide and can be as long as 700 feet.
Source: 
6-044_7b_ComplaintforDeclaratoryandConjunctiveReliefSeekingAdjudicationofWaterRightsWillisLosAngelesSuperiorCourt.pdf

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending April 30
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends April 30. A fiscal year therefore shares four of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other eight with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 5 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 95 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 6 were left blank.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

sdwis_compliance.title: Drinking-water compliance (US EPA SDWIS)
sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-05-01 to 2025-04-30), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 50.6% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds 2 surface water rights of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds 2 licensed surface water rights of its own
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910165&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends November 30. A fiscal year therefore shares eleven of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other one with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in only 2 of the 10 years, across 2 customer classes.

A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2019-12-01 to 2025-11-30), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 51.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2023 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1910012 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910012&Year=2023 (2971690 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910012&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

Groundwater-level declines of more than 270 feet in some parts of the groundwater basin have resulted in an increase in pumping lifts, reduced well efficiency, and land subsidence of more than 6 feet in some areas."
Source: 6-044_7b_USGSGroundwaterFLowandLandSubsidenceModelofAntelopeValleyCAsir2014-5166.pdf

2) Estimates of pumping in 2005 are in the 110-120K AF. 2012 was 90K AF. From 1990 to 2000, nearly 0.4 feet of subsidence (Sneed and Galloway, 2000).  Fissures range from one inch to over one foot wide and can be as long as 700 feet.

sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 3 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Drought regime, Supply sensitivity).

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Drought regime
components.value: Across the years this company filed (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31), Los Angeles County was in severe drought or worse 44.1% of the time.

detail.label: Filing window read over
Weeks in severe drought or worse
Average share of the county in severe drought or worse
County

components.confidence_reason: The weekly series is published by the US Drought Monitor and is high confidence; the share is arithmetic over it across this company's own filed periods, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.source: US Drought Monitor, Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/DmData/DataDownload/WebServiceInfo.aspx
components.logic: Every week of this company's own filing years is checked against the US Drought Monitor record for its county, and the share of those weeks spent at D2 (severe) or worse is counted. It ties the water conditions to the years the financial statements were actually lived through, rather than to a fixed recent period.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and no basin beneath it is in critical overdraft.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: This system's own 2024 Consumer Confidence Report was located and read, and it describes its sources without stating a share or a volume for any of them, so there is no mix to read from it. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type. Ranking a supply out of the report's wording would be reading a category out of prose, which this component refuses to do.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report states no mix, and that was checked
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910246&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (84.2 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 1.1 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.value: Takes surface water from its own source; it holds no surface water right of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA4300517 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4300517&Year=2024 (51589 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4300517&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)
Form 990 Part IX line 25 (total functional expenses)
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation), subtracted for the excluding variant
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Both variants are shown and the displayed variant is labeled (5A).

metrics.name: Days cash on hand
metrics.subtitle: days of operating cost covered by cash and marketable securities
metrics.limitation_note: Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

metrics.reference_source: Rating-agency convention: 200 plus days is strong, under roughly 90 days reads as stress, on unrestricted cash and investments (the State Water Board's SAFER risk indicator uses the same basis: Draft Final White Paper, Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, p. 28). Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.
metrics.formula: (cash, line 1; savings and temporary cash investments, line 2; publicly traded securities, line 11; other securities described as marketable on Schedule D Part VII, line 12) x 365 / (total expenses, line 25, less depreciation, line 22)
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 1 (cash, non-interest-bearing)
Form 990 Part X line 2 (savings and temporary cash investments)
Form 990 Part X line 11 (investments, publicly traded securities)
Form 990 Part X line 12 (investments, other securities), counted only where Schedule D Part VII describes the holding as marketable
Form 990 Part IX line 25 less line 22 (operating expense excluding depreciation)

calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends February 28. A fiscal year therefore shares two of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other ten with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.value: Takes surface water from its own source; it holds no surface water right of its own, and the ground beneath it is in critical overdraft, which is the state's finding that the basin is pumped faster than it refills.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2023 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA3910022 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3910022&Year=2023 (242777 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3910022&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

sdwis_compliance.title: Drinking-water compliance (US EPA SDWIS)
sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (89.2 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 1.55 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1500475 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1500475&Year=2024 (1123154 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1500475&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.

calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends October 31. A fiscal year therefore shares ten of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other two with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 18 survey years, 2007 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 17 of the 18 years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 14 of the 18 years, across 5 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 83 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 30 were left blank. 27 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2007 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

gap_evidence.status_line: 3 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 9600006, 9600007, 9600008. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 2.12 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.

components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4100503&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1000054 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1000054&Year=2024 (47945 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1000054&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (655.2 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 3.6 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA3700905 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3700905&Year=2024 (232926 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3700905&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.

metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

basins.name: LOS OSOS VALLEY - LOS OSOS AREA
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has designated it in critical overdraft: the state has found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. That is a supply-risk signal about the basin itself, not a finding about this system. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) The primary constraint on water availability in the Los Osos Valley Groundwater Basin is deteriorating water quality due to sea water intrusion and nitrate contamination.   
Source: 3-008_01_7a_L_Appendix_SLOGWBasins.pdf   pg L-15
