basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: not recorded. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: The service area touches mapped fire hazard zones, but none of them is in the High or Very High classes; the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 0.0% of the service area (0.0 acres), SRA

detail.label: Moderate zone
detail.value: about 0.0% of the service area (0.0 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 1.32 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and the ground beneath it is in critical overdraft, which is the state's finding that the basin is pumped faster than it refills.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by LOS OSOS VALLEY - LOS OSOS AREA (3-008.01) in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

detail.label: Basin placement confidence
detail.value: The basin placement is an areal join and is carried at low; it is never better than the service-area boundary it rests on.
detail.source: BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2022 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA4000523 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4000523&Year=2022 (1308639 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4000523&Year=2022
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: SANTA CLARA RIVER VALLEY - OXNARD
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has designated it in critical overdraft: the state has found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. That is a supply-risk signal about the basin itself, not a finding about this system. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. 3 agencies are named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Camrosa Water District GSA - Oxnard; County of Ventura GSA - Oxnard Basin Outlying Areas; Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency GSA - Oxnard
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 4-004.02_7a_Hydrographs_Oxnard.pdf

2) There is evidence for the occurrence of long-term overdraft in at least two of the groundwater basins of the District. Groundwater levels have generally been declining for periods of several decades in the Oxnard Plain and Pleasant Valley basins. While the factors causing declining groundwater trends may have varied among these two basins, long-term replenishment rates have not kept up with long-term withdrawal rates in either of them. Thus, these basins are considered by the District to be in a condition of long-term overdraft.
Source: 4-004.02_7a_2016GWConditionsReportFINAL.pdf  pg. 12
basins.subsidence_comment:
1)  Water-level declines in the basin have induced land subsidence that was first measured in 1939 and have resulted in as much as 2.7 feet land subsidence in the southern part of the Oxnard Plain. The model simulated a total of 3 feet of land subsidence in the southern part of the Oxnard Plain and as much as 5 feet in the Las Posas Valley subbasins. Model simulations indicate that most of the land subsidence occurred after the drought of the late 1920s and during the agricultural expansion of the 1950s and 1960s. The results also indicate that subsidence occurred primarily in the upper-aquifer system prior to 1959, but in the lower-aquifer system between 1959-93 owing to an increase in pumpage from the lower-aquifer system. 

"groundwater and oil and gas production are probably major causes in the Oxnard Plain subbasin, and tectonic activity is probably a minor cause (Hanson et al., 2003)" Subsidence has been documented in the Oxnard Plain:                                                     Source: 4-004.02_7b_SimulationofgroundwaterSurfaceWaterFlowinSantaClara-CalleguarsBasinVenturaCountyWIR02-4136CaPDF
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: not recorded. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA5610068 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5610068&Year=2024 (262348 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5610068&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 2.54 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA4000834 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4000834&Year=2024 (200259 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4000834&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1500409 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1500409&Year=2024 (42670 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1500409&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends January 31. A fiscal year therefore shares one of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other eleven with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 97.9% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
High zone
detail.value: about 97.9% of the service area (194.5 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 2.32 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 11 survey years, 2014 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 11 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 8 of the 11 years, across 2 customer classes.

Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

Share in High or Very High
High zone
detail.value: about 60.4% of the service area (79.6 acres), SRA

detail.label: Very High zone

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 1.65 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA5400754 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5400754&Year=2024 (141288 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5400754&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 13 survey years, 2003 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 12 of the 13 years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 9 of the 12 years, from 1 customer class.
coverage.tail: Separately, 103 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 15 were left blank. 7 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2003 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (91.8 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 0.99 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2023 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA3100041 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3100041&Year=2023 (324781 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA3100041&Year=2023
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends March 31. A fiscal year therefore shares three of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other nine with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

safer_standing.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad
safer_standing.note: Failing, At-Risk, Potentially At-Risk, Not At-Risk and Not Assessed are the State Water Board's own categories and its own determination about this system. They are carried here in the state's words and are not this project's assessment of the company. An automatic designation is made regardless of the category scores beneath it, so a system can be listed At-Risk while scoring NONE or LOW on most categories.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (189.7 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 2.71 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA4900570 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4900570&Year=2024 (341119 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4900570&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.value: About 55.1% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is High.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 1.07 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1900100 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1900100&Year=2024 (46943 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1900100&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.tail: Separately, 83 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 13 were left blank. 15 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: CORRALITOS - PAJARO VALLEY
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has designated it in critical overdraft: the state has found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. That is a supply-risk signal about the basin itself, not a finding about this system. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. One agency is named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Pajaro Valley Water Management Agency GSA
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) CRITICAL OVERDRAFT 2016
Source: DWR

"Most recently, groundwater levels collected from PVWMA’s network of monitoring wells throughout the 2013 water year were used to map the water table elevation in the basin. It is evident that a significant trough below sea level still exists throughout the valley floor, centered around the Pajaro River channel."  And  "If drought conditions were to occur again with the basin in its current state, overdraft conditions would worsen and seawater intrusion rates would accelerate beyond what has been measured in the past."
Source: 3-002.01_7a_BMPUpdateFinalFebruary 2014.pdf
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: not recorded. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.
sgma_basin.source: CA DWR Bulletin 118 groundwater basins and SGMA Basin Prioritization, https://gis.water.ca.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Geoscientific/i08_B118_CA_GroundwaterBasins/MapServer/0/query Retrieved 2026-09-20.

safer_standing.plain_sentence: The State Water Board's SAFER assessment lists this system as At-Risk. Retrieved from the state's published file on 2026-09-20.

comparable.state_basis: State Water Board definition: unrestricted cash and investments divided by per-day operating expenses excluding depreciation (Draft Final White Paper, July 16, 2020, p. 28). The Hydronomics headline uses the same basis as far as Form 990 allows. The state publishes a risk level and a threshold result, not a figure, and the file does not state which assessment year it reflects.
comparable.state_definition_source: State Water Resources Control Board, Draft Final White Paper Discussion On: Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, pp. 27 and 28
comparable.ours_basis: Computed by this project from the filed financial statements, on the basis set out in the anchor-metrics framework.
comparable.comparison_note: Two readings of the same indicator from two different bases. They are shown side by side and are deliberately NOT combined: the state's is a threshold test whose definition this project does not hold, and this project's is a computed figure. Neither is used to check or correct the other.

comparable.state_basis: State Water Board definition: operating revenue divided by operating expenses including depreciation (Draft Final White Paper, July 16, 2020, p. 27). Same direction as the Hydronomics figure, revenue over expenses, so no conversion is made. The state publishes a risk level and a threshold result, not a figure, and the file does not state which assessment year it reflects.
comparable.state_definition_source: State Water Resources Control Board, Draft Final White Paper Discussion On: Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, pp. 27 and 28

safer_standing.no_year_note: The state's published file carries no assessment year: its own date field is identical on every row and is the date the extract was produced. The date shown here is when this project retrieved the determination.
safer_standing.source: California State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water: SAFER Drinking Water Risk Assessment Public Flat File, data.ca.gov resource 255887bb-5451-4c19-8e35-27899ae8c3ad
safer_standing.note: Failing, At-Risk, Potentially At-Risk, Not At-Risk and Not Assessed are the State Water Board's own categories and its own determination about this system. They are carried here in the state's words and are not this project's assessment of the company. An automatic designation is made regardless of the category scores beneath it, so a system can be listed At-Risk while scoring NONE or LOW on most categories.

The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

plant_per_acre.title: Plant assets per acre
plant_per_acre.acres_source: Geodesic area (WGS84 spherical excess) of the SABL service-area polygon.
plant_per_acre.logic: Infrastructure built per acre of service area. Gross plant per acre is the primary read because it measures how much plant the system has put in the ground per acre, and unlike net plant it does not fall over time purely because the assets depreciate on the books. Net plant per acre is shown alongside as the depreciated book value per acre.
plant_per_acre.formula: gross plant per acre = Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment, gross) / SABL service-area acres; net plant per acre uses Part X line 10c (net)
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (gross) and line 10c (net)

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and the ground beneath it is in critical overdraft, which is the state's finding that the basin is pumped faster than it refills.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory

detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.label: Groundwater basin condition
detail.value: Underlain by CORRALITOS - PAJARO VALLEY (3-002.01) in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

detail.label: Basin placement confidence
detail.value: The basin placement is an areal join and is carried at low; it is never better than the service-area boundary it rests on.
detail.source: BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA4400558 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4400558&Year=2024 (159425 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4400558&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)

No change is measured across a change of filing form.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2011 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. gap_evidence.status_line: 5 violation id(s) are REFERENCED BUT NOT RETURNED: 1100006, 1100007, 500001, 600002, 600003. No violation record was retrieved for them, none was invented, and nothing is stated here about what they were for. They are unresolved.
gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

An automatic designation is made regardless of the category scores beneath it, so a system can be listed At-Risk while scoring NONE or LOW on most categories.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

detail.value: Underlain by 1 designated basin, none in critical overdraft
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The State Water Board report viewer was asked for PWSID CA3400172 for every year in the declared window 2021 to 2024 on 2026-09-23 and returned no readable document (2024: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2023: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2022: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2021: HTTP 404 Not Found). The report was searched for and could not be located; nothing is concluded here about this system's supply. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990-EZ Part I line 9 (total revenue)
Form 990-EZ Part I line 17 (total expenses); the excluding variant needs a depreciation line, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Both variants are shown and the displayed variant is labeled (5A).
