explainer.reason: Form 990-EZ has no depreciation line, so operating expenses less depreciation cannot be formed; its line 22 already combines cash, savings and investments, so a cash-and-investments numerator exists but has no denominator on the same basis as every other company.

metrics.name: Reinvestment ratio
metrics.subtitle: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: not reported (no comparable years in window)

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: needs Form 990 Part X line 10a in two consecutive years and Part IX line 22, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 11 survey years, 2014 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 11 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in only 1 of the 9 years, from 1 customer class.
coverage.tail: Separately, 66 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 2 were left blank.
coverage.assurance: This data was pulled and verified in full. The thinness above is what Kyburz Mutual Water Company filed with the survey, not a gap in what we retrieved. Its production filing is complete over the same period, which is the clearest evidence that the pull worked.
coverage.unit_note: 37 of its 69 delivery figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain. Those figures are shown as filed in the table and were not converted to acre-feet, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume. That is why the delivery table shows figures the delivery chart cannot draw.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2014 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

ca_sos.plain_lead: This check has not been run for this system yet. Nothing below is a finding about the system; it records that the work is outstanding.
ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 85.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 85.0% of the service area (79.1 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 0.93 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA0900300 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA0900300&Year=2024 (540371 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA0900300&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

sdwis_compliance.note: Violations and enforcement as recorded by the US EPA Envirofacts federal SDWIS mirror, carried exactly as published (high confidence). Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA4900608 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4900608&Year=2024 (120139 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA4900608&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.

components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1900794 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1900794&Year=2024 (45451 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1900794&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending June 30
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends June 30. A fiscal year therefore shares six of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other six with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in only 2 of the 12 years, from 1 customer class.

ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.

components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). The quartiles are never added up, weighted, ranked or turned into a single figure: this is a position, not a grade, not a rating, and not a ranking of companies. A metric this system does not report, or that is not comparable enough to place, is named above rather than counted against it.
cohort_position.cohort_note: The cohort is the mutual water companies in this project that file a Form 990 carrying financial data, which is not a sample of California's mutuals. calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending May 31
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends May 31. A fiscal year therefore shares five of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other seven with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 11 of the 12 years, across 3 customer classes.
coverage.tail: Separately, 86 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 14 were left blank. 8 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.
pwss_volume.source: DWR Public Water System Statistics survey, received by email from DWR 2026-08-03; see data/pwss_historical/MANIFEST.md for provenance and data/staging/PWSS__cawc_0102.jsonl for the staged evidence.

water_rights.note: Water rights as filed with the State Water Resources Control Board. The right type, status, face value and point of diversion are carried exactly as the state publishes them (high confidence). Annual diverted volumes are DERIVED by summing the filed monthly figures for that right, year and diversion type (medium confidence); the monthly figures are the source of truth. Direct diversion, storage and use are different quantities and are never added together. A Statement of Diversion and Use records claimed use and carries no face value, which the state files as zero.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. ca_sos.plain_lead: This check has not been run for this system yet. Nothing below is a finding about the system; it records that the work is outstanding.
ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 10.3% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 10.3% of the service area (13.4 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 3.51 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA5601122 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5601122&Year=2024 (283114 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA5601122&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990 Part VIII line 12 (total revenue)

metrics.name: Days cash on hand
metrics.subtitle: days of operating cost covered by cash and marketable securities
metrics.limitation_note: Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

metrics.reference_source: Rating-agency convention: 200 plus days is strong, under roughly 90 days reads as stress, on unrestricted cash and investments (the State Water Board's SAFER risk indicator uses the same basis: Draft Final White Paper, Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, p. 28). Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.
metrics.formula: (cash, line 1; savings and temporary cash investments, line 2; publicly traded securities, line 11; other securities described as marketable on Schedule D Part VII, line 12) x 365 / (total expenses, line 25, less depreciation, line 22)
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 1 (cash, non-interest-bearing)
Form 990 Part X line 2 (savings and temporary cash investments)
Form 990 Part X line 11 (investments, publicly traded securities)
Form 990 Part X line 12 (investments, other securities), counted only where Schedule D Part VII describes the holding as marketable
Form 990 Part IX line 25 less line 22 (operating expense excluding depreciation)

metrics.window_average_basis: cumulative over 5 comparable years (FY2021-25)

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: Form 990 Part X line 10a (land, buildings, and equipment at cost), year over year
Form 990 Part IX line 22 (depreciation)
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.
metrics.comparability_basis: B1: one flag that does not touch the denominator (a reversal, unchanged gross plant, or a form change inside the window)

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. Where a service area spans more than one basin every basin is listed and none is ranked, because the source does not say how much of the area lies in each. The groundwater-level line is DWR's own written finding for the basin, quoted rather than scored; no well record is read.

ca_sos.plain_lead: This check has not been run for this system yet. Nothing below is a finding about the system; it records that the work is outstanding.
ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 1.87 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.

High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

metrics.window_average_basis: not reported (no comparable years in window)

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.

metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

basins.name: SANTA CLARA RIVER VALLEY - OXNARD
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin High priority, its top tier, and has designated it in critical overdraft: the state has found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. That is a supply-risk signal about the basin itself, not a finding about this system. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. 3 agencies are named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: Camrosa Water District GSA - Oxnard; County of Ventura GSA - Oxnard Basin Outlying Areas; Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency GSA - Oxnard
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Hydrographs show groundwater level decline.
Source: 4-004.02_7a_Hydrographs_Oxnard.pdf

2) There is evidence for the occurrence of long-term overdraft in at least two of the groundwater basins of the District. Groundwater levels have generally been declining for periods of several decades in the Oxnard Plain and Pleasant Valley basins. While the factors causing declining groundwater trends may have varied among these two basins, long-term replenishment rates have not kept up with long-term withdrawal rates in either of them. Thus, these basins are considered by the District to be in a condition of long-term overdraft.
Source: 4-004.02_7a_2016GWConditionsReportFINAL.pdf  pg. 12
basins.subsidence_comment:
1)  Water-level declines in the basin have induced land subsidence that was first measured in 1939 and have resulted in as much as 2.7 feet land subsidence in the southern part of the Oxnard Plain. The model simulated a total of 3 feet of land subsidence in the southern part of the Oxnard Plain and as much as 5 feet in the Las Posas Valley subbasins. Model simulations indicate that most of the land subsidence occurred after the drought of the late 1920s and during the agricultural expansion of the 1950s and 1960s. The results also indicate that subsidence occurred primarily in the upper-aquifer system prior to 1959, but in the lower-aquifer system between 1959-93 owing to an increase in pumpage from the lower-aquifer system. 

"groundwater and oil and gas production are probably major causes in the Oxnard Plain subbasin, and tectonic activity is probably a minor cause (Hanson et al., 2003)" Subsidence has been documented in the Oxnard Plain:                                                     Source: 4-004.02_7b_SimulationofgroundwaterSurfaceWaterFlowinSantaClara-CalleguarsBasinVenturaCountyWIR02-4136CaPDF
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: not recorded. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.plain_overdraft: What critical overdraft means: it is a designation the Department of Water Resources publishes for a basin it has found is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. It describes the basin, not any one system drawing from it, and it is carried here exactly as the state publishes it.
sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990-EZ Part I line 9 (total revenue)

metrics.name: Days cash on hand
metrics.subtitle: days of operating cost covered by cash and marketable securities
metrics.limitation_note: Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

metrics.reference_source: Rating-agency convention: 200 plus days is strong, under roughly 90 days reads as stress, on unrestricted cash and investments (the State Water Board's SAFER risk indicator uses the same basis: Draft Final White Paper, Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, p. 28). Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.

metrics.confidence_reason: This depends on a figure the filing does not give, so we leave it not reported rather than guess.. metrics.name: Reinvestment ratio
metrics.subtitle: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: not reported (no comparable years in window)

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: needs Form 990 Part X line 10a in two consecutive years and Part IX line 22, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

ca_sos.plain_lead: This check has not been run for this system yet. Nothing below is a finding about the system; it records that the work is outstanding.
ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: No mapped fire hazard zone touches this service area.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1910158 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910158&Year=2024 (34761 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1910158&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends August 31. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.value: About 82.6% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

Share in High or Very High
Very High zone

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 1.75 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.

components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.

components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.
metrics.logic: Whether operating revenue covers operating cost. Revenue over expenses, so higher is better and sustained sub-1.0 signals a structural deficit. This is the reciprocal of the IOU dashboard's regulatory expenses-over-revenue figure; the two are not the same measure and must not be compared directly.
metrics.formula: total revenue / total expenses (including depreciation, shown); the excluding variant divides by total expenses less depreciation
source_lines: Form 990-EZ Part I line 9 (total revenue)
Form 990-EZ Part I line 17 (total expenses); the excluding variant needs a depreciation line, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: This is worked out from filed figures (a ratio, or a year-to-year change), so it is one step removed from the raw numbers.. Both variants are shown and the displayed variant is labeled (5A).

metrics.name: Days cash on hand
metrics.subtitle: days of operating cost covered by cash and marketable securities
metrics.limitation_note: Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

reference.label: 200+ days strong; under about 90 days signals stress, on a rating-agency definition that includes unrestricted investments

metrics.reference_source: Rating-agency convention: 200 plus days is strong, under roughly 90 days reads as stress, on unrestricted cash and investments (the State Water Board's SAFER risk indicator uses the same basis: Draft Final White Paper, Identification of Risk Assessment 2.0 Indicators for Public Water Systems, July 16, 2020, p. 28). Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.
metrics.formula: (cash, line 1; savings and temporary cash investments, line 2; publicly traded securities, line 11; other securities described as marketable on Schedule D Part VII, line 12) x 365 / (total expenses, line 25, less depreciation, line 22)
source_lines: Form 990-EZ Part II line 22 (cash, savings, and investments); needs a depreciation line, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: This depends on a figure the filing does not give, so we leave it not reported rather than guess.. Lines 1, 2 and 11 are counted as filed; line 12 only where the filer's own Schedule D Part VII description reads as marketable. Form 990 does not show restrictions on cash, so restricted reserves held as cash cannot be excluded.

metrics.name: Reinvestment ratio

metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: not reported (no comparable years in window)

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: needs Form 990 Part X line 10a in two consecutive years and Part IX line 22, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.
