pwss_volume.title: Water volume history (DWR PWSS survey)

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending May 31
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends May 31. A fiscal year therefore shares five of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other seven with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

eras.label: DWR PWSS, 2006-2022 form (adds untreated water from 2007)
State Water Board SAFER, 2023-2024 form (splits self-produced from obtained, and potable from non-potable)

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in all 12 of those years, from 1 source. Deliveries carry a positive figure in only 1 of the 11 years, from 1 customer class.
coverage.tail: Separately, 55 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 7 were left blank.
coverage.assurance: This data was pulled and verified in full. The thinness above is what Sky Acres Mutual Water Inc filed with the survey, not a gap in what we retrieved. Its production filing is complete over the same period, which is the clearest evidence that the pull worked.
coverage.unit_note: 62 of its 85 delivery figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain. Those figures are shown as filed in the table and were not converted to acre-feet, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume. That is why the delivery table shows figures the delivery chart cannot draw.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 100.0% of the service area (70.7 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 0.94 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA2000524 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA2000524&Year=2024 (501139 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA2000524&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends September 30. A fiscal year therefore shares nine of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other three with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

basins.name: ANTELOPE VALLEY
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance. 2 agencies are named for this basin, listed below.
basins.gsa_text: East Acton GSA; Leona Valley GSA
basins.gw_level_comment:
1) Overdraft and Subsidence, see lawsuit Pg 4 #10: In recent years, however, population growth and agricultural demands have led to increased pumping and declining groundwater levels...
Source: 6-044_7a_WillisLawsuit-overdraft.pdf
basins.subsidence_comment:
1) "Most groundwater pumping in the valley occurs in the Antelope Valley groundwater basin, which includes the rapidly growing cities of Lancaster and Palmdale. Groundwater-level declines of more than 270 feet in some parts of the groundwater basin have resulted in an increase in pumping lifts, reduced well efficiency, and land subsidence of more than 6 feet in some areas."
Source: 6-044_7b_USGSGroundwaterFLowandLandSubsidenceModelofAntelopeValleyCAsir2014-5166.pdf

2) Estimates of pumping in 2005 are in the 110-120K AF. 2012 was 90K AF. Court Adjudicated;  Prior to 1972, groundwater provided more than 90 percent of the total water supply in the valley; since 1972, it has provided between 50 and 90 percent;  Nearly four feet of land subsidence at Edwards Air Force Based between 1926 and 1992.  From 1990 to 2000, nearly 0.4 feet of subsidence (Sneed and Galloway, 2000).  Fissures range from one inch to over one foot wide and can be as long as 700 feet.
Source: 
6-044_7b_ComplaintforDeclaratoryandConjunctiveReliefSeekingAdjudicationofWaterRightsWillisLosAngelesSuperiorCourt.pdf

Ground deformation has affected the use of the lakebed as a runway for aircraft and space shuttles (Phillips, et al., 2003).
Source: Aquifer-System Compaction and Land Subsidence: Measurements, Analyses, and Simulations of the Holly Site, Edwards Air Force Base, Antelope Valley, California

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over None scan rows of about None m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.

components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1900804 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1900804&Year=2024 (178196 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1900804&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

anchor_framework.title: Anchor metrics
anchor_framework.note: The five canonical financial-health metrics (BLUEPRINT §5A), each a multi-year trend with its external reference band shown as published context, not a grade. Confidence tier and per-line citation are in the logic panel.

metrics.name: Operating ratio
metrics.subtitle: revenue / expenses (at or above 1.0 is a surplus)

reference.label: 1.0 = revenue equals expenses; sustained sub-1.0 signals structural deficit

metrics.reference_source: UNC Environmental Finance Center and CA State Water Board Needs Assessment treat a sustained sub-1.0 operating ratio as a structural-deficit signal. A published reference point, not a Hydronomics grade.

rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

ca_sos.plain_lead: This check has not been run for this system yet. Nothing below is a finding about the system; it records that the work is outstanding.
ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 35.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 35.0% of the service area (54.8 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Verified. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 2.91 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The State Water Board report viewer was asked for PWSID CA4500014 for every year in the declared window 2021 to 2024 on 2026-09-23 and returned no readable document (2024: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2023: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2022: HTTP 404 Not Found, 2021: HTTP 404 Not Found). The report was searched for and could not be located; nothing is concluded here about this system's supply. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

calendar_basis.short: Calendar year, not the fiscal year ending April 30
calendar_basis.label: Different reporting periods. The DWR PWSS survey year is a calendar year ending December 31; this system's fiscal year ends April 30. A fiscal year therefore shares four of its twelve months with the calendar year it is named for and the other eight with the calendar year before it. Read the two side by side with that in mind. Neither series is recast: both are reported as filed. The survey year runs January to December, with the filed annual total reported as filed and never computed from the twelve months.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

coverage.filed: 12 survey years, 2013 to 2024. Production carries a positive figure in 10 of the 12 years, across 2 sources. Deliveries carry a positive figure in 9 of the 12 years, from 1 customer class.
coverage.tail: Separately, 85 cells were filed as zero, which is a figure the system reported and not an absence, and 16 were left blank. 21 figures carry a unit the survey's code list does not contain; those are shown as filed and were not converted, because a guessed unit would be a guessed volume.

pwss_volume.note: Annual water volume as filed with the California Department of Water Resources Public Water System Statistics survey, 2013 to 2024. Each system chooses its own unit of measure and the choice is not stable from year to year, so the acre-feet column is a DERIVED normalization at medium confidence and the filed value and its unit, shown on hover and in the logic panel, are the source of truth at high confidence. Years this system did not file are absent rather than zero. For 2013 and later the State Water Board (eAR and SAFER) is the standard and this DWR series is a backup, except the 2023-2024 SAFER years, which are Water Boards data. Nothing here is reconciled against another source.

sgma_basin.title: Groundwater basin (DWR, SGMA)

basins.name: ACTON VALLEY
basins.plain_lead: The Department of Water Resources ranks this basin Very Low priority, its bottom tier, and has not designated it in critical overdraft, so the state has not found the basin is being pumped faster than it naturally refills. A Groundwater Sustainability Agency is the local body SGMA makes responsible for bringing a basin into balance, and SGMA requires one only for high and medium priority basins, so none is required here.
basins.gsa_text: No GSA required. SGMA requires a Groundwater Sustainability Agency only for high and medium priority basins, and this basin is Very Low priority.
basins.gw_level_comment: No documented Groundwater Level Declines
basins.subsidence_comment: No documented groundwater extraction induced inelastic Subsidence
basins.join_note: SABL boundary verification: not recorded. The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on.

sgma_basin.note: Basin priority, critical overdraft designation and the governing agency are published by the Department of Water Resources and are carried exactly as published (high confidence). Placing this system in a basin is an AREAL join: its service-area boundary is overlapped with the basin boundary, so the placement is derived and is never better than the boundary it rests on. That is why the join confidence reads medium or low and never high. ca_sos.reason: No search has been run for this company. The California Secretary of State is reachable only through a real browser session with the operator present (BLUEPRINT 5P). Both HTTP-client routes were re-probed on 2026-09-23 and both are still refused, and the refusal now takes the shape of a SUCCESS STATUS carrying a challenge body rather than an error status, which is worth stating precisely because a bare 'HTTP 200' reads as though the route worked. GET https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with an _Incapsula_Resource challenge document (1,031 bytes on this probe). POST https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/api/Records/businesssearch, carrying an empty JSON object and therefore asking for nothing, also answered HTTP 200, content-type text/html, with a 212-byte _Incapsula_Resource challenge document rather than any JSON. Neither returned data of any kind. The byte counts are what these two probes returned and are not stable between requests, so they are recorded as observations and not as properties of the endpoint. On 2026-09-20 the same endpoint answered HTTP 429 with errorCode 15, and on 2026-08-31 it answered 403; the refusal keeps changing shape, which is why it is re-observed each time rather than carried over. The browser route has answered a persistent hCaptcha interstitial since 2026-08-26 and this project will not attempt to solve it. This is not_yet_checked and deliberately not not_matched: not-matched means the source was searched and returned nothing that could be confirmed, and nothing was searched here. A California mutual water company is an incorporated entity and must be registered to exist, so an absence here is never a finished answer. The check needs the pending CALICO developer credential, or a browser session on a day the interstitial is not served.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 100.0% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

Share in High or Very High
Very High zone

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 0.67 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.

components.cross_source_note: A Consumer Confidence Report for this system was located but could not be read: The 2024 Consumer Confidence Report for PWSID CA1900903 was located and downloaded from https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1900903&Year=2024 (1559940 bytes), and it carries no text layer: it is published as page images. This project does not run optical character recognition, so no figure is transcribed from it and none is inferred. The document itself is cited and reachable; what is missing is a machine readable rendering of it, and that is recorded rather than worked around. The band above rests on the inventory's single source type alone.
components.cross_source_heading: This system's own report was located and could not be read
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1900903&Year=2024
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.

Wildland-urban-interface systems warrant the high end. Recorded as reference bands only, not a threshold applied to any system.
metrics.logic: How many days the system could cover operating cost from cash and marketable securities if revenue stopped. The cash-only figure beside it is the floor.

metrics.name: Reinvestment ratio

metrics.face_label: Reinvestment ratio: cumulative change in gross plant (Part X line 10a) over cumulative depreciation (Part IX line 22) across the display window
metrics.face_note: Form 990 has no additions line, so this is a floor estimate of additions net of disposals.
metrics.window_average_basis: not reported (no comparable years in window)

reference.label: 1.0 = additions equal depreciation; sustained under 1.0 flags infrastructure consumption

metrics.reference_source: An interpretive reference mark (additions equal to depreciation), not a published external threshold.
metrics.logic: Whether the system reinvests in its plant at least as fast as the plant depreciates, read cumulatively over the display window so one year's timing does not headline. Sustained reinvestment below depreciation flags infrastructure consumption.
metrics.formula: sum of (gross plant this year - gross plant prior filed year) over the comparable years in the display window / sum of depreciation over the same years. A comparable year is a ratio year, a net decrease year (kept with its sign), or a year of no material change (a change smaller than the larger of $1,000 and 0.1 percent of prior gross plant). No change is measured across a change of filing form.
source_lines: needs Form 990 Part X line 10a in two consecutive years and Part IX line 22, which Form 990-EZ does not carry
metrics.confidence_reason: Medium by construction: Form 990 has no additions line, so additions are derived from the change in gross plant, which is net of disposals recorded at cost. The cumulative figure is a floor estimate of additions, not a directly filed additions figure.

rollup.title: Derived comparability view (customer type by water quality)
rollup.note: DERIVED, medium confidence, and shown beside the as-filed classes above, never in place of them. Every figure here is a sum of the filed class figures named on each cell; nothing is estimated and no filed value is altered. Two axes rather than four buckets because the filed classes are not mutually exclusive: the 2023-2024 form files residential non-potable deliveries, which belong to both. Commercial and institutional share one filed column and are not separable from the source, so the bucket keeps both words. The filed urban total is the potable total, so potable buckets reconcile against it and any difference is shown as a residual rather than absorbed; non-potable sits outside it by the survey's own design. A year in which a filed unit could not be recognized is marked incomplete, because the convertible subset is not the system's total. The filed urban total covers URBAN potable deliveries only: agricultural irrigation sits outside it, as does every non-potable class, by the survey's own design and not because anything is missing. Both are reported separately beside it.

A violation is treated as open when the record carries no return-to-compliance date; that date is the evidence, and it remains the only thing the open reading rests on. Codes are shown as filed, with EPA's own name for each beside it; a code EPA's reference does not list is shown as the bare code and marked as unmatched.
sdwis_compliance.code_note: The detail column carries what the record says went wrong, exactly as filed, with EPA's own plain-language name beside each code. The names come from EPA's published SDWA reference code values, retrieved 2026-08-21, matched on the code exactly and never on a near match, so a name is a lookup rather than a reading (high confidence). A code the reference does not list keeps its raw code and is marked not matched; it is never guessed at, because a wrong name is worse than a bare number. Where the record carries a measured result it is shown in the unit it was filed in, beside the state limit it is measured against.

gap_evidence.why_note: Why federal mirror tables commonly disagree: Envirofacts is a mirror of the state's primacy record, and its tables are refreshed on their own schedules, so one table can carry a more recent load than another and the two read differently in between. A violation that was corrected, withdrawn or superseded in the primary table is also not always removed from the cross-reference rows that point at it. Which of those explains this system is not something the source states, so it is not claimed here.

safer_standing.note: Failing, At-Risk, Potentially At-Risk, Not At-Risk and Not Assessed are the State Water Board's own categories and its own determination about this system. They are carried here in the state's words and are not this project's assessment of the company. An automatic designation is made regardless of the category scores beneath it, so a system can be listed At-Risk while scoring NONE or LOW on most categories.

weather_exposure.title: Weather exposure
weather_exposure.lead: A computed read, not a self-report. Three separately sourced components: how much of the service area sits in mapped fire hazard, how much of this company's own filing window its county spent in severe drought, and how exposed its water supply is to a dry year. Each carries its own source and check date, and a component that cannot be computed says so rather than going blank.

composite.basis: Composed from 2 of 3 components (Fire hazard, Supply sensitivity). Not composed from Drought regime, which could not be computed for this system; the composite is held at lower confidence because of it.

components.name: Fire hazard
components.value: About 98.2% of the service area sits in the High or Very High fire hazard zones California maps, and the most severe class mapped there is Very High.

detail.label: Highest class touching the service area
Share in High or Very High
Very High zone
detail.value: about 98.2% of the service area (23.9 acres), SRA

components.confidence_reason: SABL boundary verification: Not Verified (SABL). The areal join is derived and never better than the boundary it rests on, so it is never high. The share is integrated over 600 scan rows of about 1.31 m, so it is approximate to that resolution and is not an exact acreage.
components.source: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones (fhsz24_1), State and Local Responsibility Areas, intersected with the State Water Board SABL service-area boundary
components.logic: The service-area boundary the State Water Board publishes is laid over the fire hazard severity zones CAL FIRE publishes, and the share of the service area inside each class is measured. High and Very High are reported together because those are the classes California attaches building and defensible-space requirements to.

components.name: Supply sensitivity
components.value: Pumps water from its own wells; it holds no surface water right of its own, and it sits over no designated groundwater basin.

detail.label: Source type, State Water Board inventory
detail.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID

detail.label: Own diversion
detail.value: Holds no surface water right of its own, the ordinary result for a groundwater or purchased-water system
detail.source: California surface water rights (eWRIMS), BLUEPRINT 5M check log

detail.value: Sits over no designated groundwater basin
detail.source: DWR SGMA basin prioritization, BLUEPRINT 5N

components.confidence_reason: Each of the facts underneath is a published record carried at high confidence, except a residual share, which is a subtraction and is carried at medium and labelled. Combining them into a sensitivity band is a derivation, which BLUEPRINT 5 puts at medium.
components.band_basis_note: The dependence is taken from the State Water Board inventory's structured source type, which is the default wherever no report states a quantified mix.
components.source: State Water Board public water system inventory (data.ca.gov, Drinking Water Public Water System Information), primary water source type as published, matched by exact PWSID; eWRIMS water rights; DWR SGMA; https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA1700536&Year=2021
components.logic: Three things decide how hard a dry year lands on a system's supply: what it draws on, whether it controls a second source of its own, and whether the ground under it is already being pumped beyond what the state considers sustainable. Buying treated water from a wholesaler is the most exposed position, because the decision to cut back in a dry year is not the system's to make. What a system draws on is read from its own annual report where that report states a mix, and from the State Water Board inventory otherwise.
